## 4eb022dc 2026-07-08 conformance: spec-anchored rule-keyed test system (make check layer 5)

A toolchain-agnostic conformance suite: canonical .xl cases plus a manifest of rule
ids and expected verdicts, driven through a swappable adapter (democ today, the real
then self-hosted compiler later), with a coverage tracker binding cases to the 89 spec
rules. It tests the language (source -> verdict), so it outlives every compiler rewrite;
it is the M3 codegen oracle and the self-hosting bootstrap safety net. The checker and
democ are disposable — this suite is the production artifact of the toolchain.

- runner.py: toolchain adapter + verdict assertion (rejections check the exact rule id,
  DIAG-1) + coverage report of untested rules. case status: runnable | pending | xfail.
- seed corpus (9 cases): 5 PASS, 3 pending/skip, 1 xfail; coverage 15/89 rules.
- wired as make-check layer 5; all five layers green.

Findings the suite already surfaced:
- the xfail case confirms the OWN-1 copy/affine bare-use gap (auto-flags XPASS when fixed).
- democ's parser rejects positional user-calls at parse time without citing GRAM-11 (a
  DIAG-1 gap in the demo parser).

## 68938136 2026-07-08 M-A step 2: democ general struct codegen

Parse `struct TYPEID { field* }` (FORM-3 name check); thread structs through
build_prog so the checker (which already types them) sees them; emit `%T = type
{..}` once per struct; construct = alloca + GEP-store; field read = GEP + typed
load; field set = GEP + store; own structs pass/return by value (alloca-backed,
mem2reg'd by clang -O2). Tokenizer widened for dotted field paths; op-vs-place
discriminator keys on a following `<`.

Adds 6 struct conformance cases (structs had ZERO coverage): construct/read,
field set, nested, mixed-width fields, cross-fn, and a GRAM-8 field-order reject.
PASS 169->175; existing i32/enum .ll byte-identical (91 programs); make check +
make examples green; 0 FAIL/XPASS; coverage 89/89.

## 38f46eac 2026-07-08 research: codegen/perf experiment — xlang vs C/C++/Rust (R0 evidence)

First non-trivial head-to-head. Honest verdict: optimizer-first pays off at the
constitution's claimed level and no more — parity with C/C++/Rust on a real kernel
(splitmix64, byte-identical hot loop), automatic non-defeasible noalias that beats
un-annotated C (O(n)->O(1) affine reduction, ~22x; C needs manual restrict), does
NOT beat Rust (overclaim correctly not observed), no regression anywhere. The big
wall-clock wins (disjoint-buffer vectorization) need arrays/pools not yet built —
projected, not demonstrated.

## 97711899 2026-07-08 M-A step 3: democ general payload-carrying enum codegen

Unify enum lowering to {i32 tag, i<W> payload} (W = widest variant payload):
construct stores tag + zext'd payload; match runs an icmp-eq tag chain and
truncs the payload back to each binder's declared width (bit-preserving round-
trip). Tag-only enums stay bare i32; Bool stays i1. A global variant registry
(prelude + user enums) subsumes the old Ok/Err "pair" hack and True/False into
one enum-value form; Result/Option are enums with one type-erased word payload.

Adds 4 payload-enum conformance cases (give-arith, multi-width dispatch, borrow-
payload, stmt-position). PASS 175->179; scalar/struct/tag-only-enum .ll byte-
identical (only genuine payload/Result enum .ll changed); make check + examples
green; 0 FAIL/XPASS; coverage 89/89.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## ad8dbe02 2026-07-08 research: regions+effects vs safe Rust — adversarial study (make-or-break)

Headline: mostly NO. 4 canonical kernels, safe-Rust adversary (rayon/bumpalo/
iterators/LTO, no unsafe). 3/4 AUTOMATION (safe Rust reaches the xlang ceiling
exactly — twice bit-identical, once 15% faster). 1 STRUCTURAL: disjoint-permutation
parallel scatter, ~1.1-1.5x (regime-dependent), closable with one unsafe store.
The 12,500x/52,000x/3-5x numbers are naive-code footguns safe Rust also fixes,
not ceilings. Raw-perf case for xlang as a general Rust competitor: not supported.
Surviving thread: shift-left/automation for AI codegen, needs the M3 harness to
evaluate. Negative result on the core thesis; the make-or-break gate did its job.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 979e3e2a 2026-07-08 research: auto-parallelism feasibility — NO on strong claim (make-or-break)

Verdict: 'write sequential, get safe automatic parallelism' is the sound-but-
unadopted DPJ dream. Regions+effects prove TASK-level independence but region
granularity is too coarse for data-parallel loops; XL's own scatter win isn't even
provable from effect rows (needs injectivity/index-parameterized regions = DPJ's
fatal annotation machinery). Killed by the granularity/cost-model trap (no type
system solves it; HELIX: real code is genuinely sequential) and the adoption trap
(DPJ = XL's near-twin, sound + deterministic + inference-assisted, ~zero uptake;
rayon ties XL's ceiling with one token). Scoped survivor: safe/deterministic
parallel scatter without unsafe on the injective band (~1.1-1.5x). Cheap 1-2 day
paper falsifier proposed before any build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## f05d6c25 2026-07-24 Add the experiment loop as the trunk workflow

P0 is why the project exists, so work starts from a falsifiable question about
machine code rather than from a specification gap. WORKFLOW.md is rescoped to
hold two loops: the experiment loop as the trunk, and the existing
language-change loop as a branch entered only from the routing stage, when a
measured result names a specification gap as its concrete blocker. That makes
the roadmap reorientation self-enforcing instead of a rule to remember.

The loop is ten stages, each recorded with what it produces and what fails it.
Four carry the discipline the July 8 research notes applied to themselves: the
hypothesis is pre-registered and immutable once the intervention starts;
verification separates correctness, attribution, and magnitude, and no
magnitude may be cited without attribution; the four judgement outcomes are not
interchangeable, and an instrument failure is never filed as parity; and a
parity or negative result is recorded as durably as a win, because an
unrecorded dead channel gets retried weeks later.

Adds an experiment resource contract and a research/experiments/ row to the
parts table. The agent instruction files are rescoped to match and remain
byte-identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 8344c6bd 2026-07-24 Fix unbounded stack growth from in-loop array slot allocas

Dynamic indexing of an array<T,N> SSA value emitted a fresh alloca plus a
whole-array store at the point of use. Inside a loop body that alloca executed
every iteration, so stack use grew without bound and an accepted program died
with SIGSEGV and no DIAG-3 record: fir_filter exited 0 at 5,000 frames and 139
at 10,000, at both optimization levels.

The allocation now hoists to the entry block through a per-function prelude
while the store stays at the use site. One slot per requesting site, with no
reuse across sites. Slot reuse across iterations cannot alias, because a
value-rooted borrow outliving its iteration is already rejected by OWN-11, so
the hoist rests on a language rule rather than on emitter luck. The prelude
anchor cannot produce invalid IR either: an entry block with parameters is
already a BackendFailure::InvalidIr.

Measured against a pristine build of the previous commit: fir_filter runs to
completion at 100,000 frames, non-entry-block allocas drop from present in five
corpus groups to zero everywhere, and sha256_abc loses 18% of its optimized
instruction stream, 1234 to 1012. raw_deflate grows 1.5%.

This is the shallow half of the conservative array lowering repair. The
whole-aggregate copy-modify-reload that owns 472 of the corpus's 1015 signal
remarks remains.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## ba470927 2026-07-24 Compile through one shared host optimization level

The driver shelled to clang with no -O flag, so every executable the compiler
had ever produced was unoptimized. Two test helpers duplicated that invocation,
which meant turning it on in the driver alone would have left every test at -O0
and made the trap-record assertions hold trivially.

The level is now one definition, HOST_OPTIMIZATION_ARGUMENTS, consumed by the
driver and both test helpers. Provisionally -O2. There is deliberately no
writer-facing option: the default shape must be the optimal shape, and where
semantics are identical no writer decision exists, so an unoptimized
alternative would only offer a worse one. whitefootc rejects -O2 as an unknown
option, and its usage line is unchanged.

The 13 existing trapping-program tests all constant-fold at -O2 into the same
write-then-abort shape, so they prove the record plumbing survives optimization
and nothing about check survival. A regression is added that traps out of a
genuinely non-foldable loop, where the backedge, the runtime comparison, and the
trap edge all survive in the optimized assembly.

Also adds a tripwire for a soundness hazard measured but not yet armed:
nounwind willreturn memory(argmem: read) on a function containing a required
trap path causes the trap to be deleted outright, while all six proper subsets
of those attributes abort correctly. EFF-3 already forbids this, since v0
provides no termination checker, so v0.17 never emits willreturn on any row.
The compiler emits no function attributes today, so the test is currently
satisfied by absence; its value is as a guard on the future effect-attribute
channel, and willreturn is the narrowest sufficient token to watch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 7826fc62 2026-07-24 Reorient the roadmap to Phase 10 performance evidence

The constitution makes machine performance the reason the project exists, yet
every recorded fact-channel measurement predated the current compiler, the
driver linked without optimization, and Phase 10 had no starts. Language
amendment now yields to performance evidence: no further specification
amendment starts without naming the measured experiment it unblocks.

Phase 10 opens with a facts-off baseline whose steps are corrected against six
probes and adversarial verification rather than assumption. The array lowering
repair leads, because it owns 472 of 1015 signal remarks and 60% of sha256's
optimized instruction stream and no fact channel touches it. Effect attributes
lose first place: they are consumable in-module, which refuted the
separate-compilation hypothesis, but they are gated on a trap-path memory
modelling decision and have no demonstrated non-degenerate magnitude. Scoped
alias has zero sites in the corpus, since LLVM inlines every internal kernel
into main where buffers already carry noalias. Checked law measures zero and is
dropped.

The grayscale pre-registration is withdrawn: 21 remarks rather than seven,
clearing all 21 leaves the assembly byte-identical, and no debug info means the
remarks are unattributable in principle. Replaced with a bounds-proof
pre-registration measured after the array repair, plus the rule that a
pre-registration taken before a lowering change is void for the compiler that
then exists.

The deepest open question is answered affirmatively. Fold resistance is
achievable by construction, so no language input path and no harness escape is
required: a recurrence with no SCEV closed form, the kernel's result re-entering
its input through a non-convergent mixer, observed through a check trap record.
Verified patterns scale 2.00x for 2x work. Two limits are recorded, and the
presence of the kernel's own call in optimized assembly is documented as an
invalid fold detector, with the counter-example that keeps the call while
deleting the loop around it.

Phase 8 becomes subordinate: freezing behaviour at v0.17 stops its exit
criterion receding, and a remaining gap is worked only when a Phase 10 slice or
a dogfood port names it as the blocker. The parked v0.18 candidate is tracked
here as the non-authoritative design record the roadmap now points at.

## 4ea068ac 2026-08-05 compiler: extend the native grammar path with staged v0.18 tables

Make whitefoot-grammar verify the v0.18 system-interface candidate through
the compiler's own lexer, terminal classifier, and strong-LL(2) parser while
the production compile path keeps exact v0.17 behavior.

Mechanism: staged grammar tables selected by contract identity. A committed
staged table set (src/syntax/grammar/staged.rs) describes the complete
candidate grammar - program_kind? on fn_decl, input_label? on param with the
fixed terminal spelling `as`, and the external/blocks effect categories in
EFF-1's canonical order: 64 productions, 67 fixed terminals, 74 decisions,
1925 SELECT_2 rows, 75 diagnostic predicates. A byte-exact snapshot of the
candidate's frontend-contract sections (staged_frontend.md) pins the contract
those tables describe, and its SHA-256 is the staged selection token. The one
shared engine picks tables by the contract identity the caller names: the
driver always passes the active hash, so active classification, parsing, and
diagnostics are unchanged; finalization fails closed on staged derivations.
The verifier accepts a candidate matching either carried contract, checks the
matching inventory, decision coverage, and cross-arm disjointness, runs real
parser probes including the candidate's canonical command-entry header, and
fails closed on anything else.

The active v0.17 tables are byte-untouched apart from two staged-only
Production enum variants the active tables never reference. The staged data
was generated offline by a one-shot generator validated by reproducing the
committed v0.17 tables exactly (structure byte-identical; all 72 decisions'
1839 SELECT rows and atom metadata set-identical) before emitting v0.18.

Tests: staged parse of the kind-declaring entry, labelled inputs, and
external/blocks rows; staged reservation of as/external/blocks; active-path
spot checks that a program_kind entry and an external row still reject and
that the three spellings remain ordinary identifiers; staged fail-closed
near-miss contracts; finalize fail-closed. make -C compiler check and
make check green.

Task: docs/ongoing/0005-grammar-path-extension.md (plan Work item 1).

## 0b3ecde8 2026-08-06 conformance: extend the harness and land the v0.18 compile-time lane

Schema. A run/trap case may carry an `arrange` describing the invocation it
needs: an argv byte list, a stdin body, file and directory fixtures, and a
redirection map whose sink names make "stdout and stderr to one target"
statable. Byte strings are lowercase hex so a non-UTF-8 argument or path value
is expressible exactly and still diffs readably. Keys are a closed set, and a
case that never executes may not carry an arrangement. Existing manifest
entries remain valid unmodified. Task 0014's runtime lane builds on this.

Verdict. `unsupported` becomes a first-class expectation kind, matched on the
verdict kind rather than the adapter's prose. It is reserved for the stops the
specification itself fixes as non-rejections citing no language rule —
target-qualification failure and pre-entry startup refusal. `expect` remains
the verdict the specification requires; an unimplemented compiler capability
is a `status` fact and never rewrites it.

Pin. The corpus moves to spec/kernel-spec-v0.18.md. Coverage reports 119/119
rules covered (90 by case, 30 by annotation), with 13 new annotations for the
rules that have no compile-time source-to-verdict pair: the runtime lane's
PATH/HOST/SYS-7/SYS-8/EFF-5/TRAP-1 content, the QUAL target-qualification
properties, and GATE-2's separation policy.

Cases. 24 additive compile-time cases from the reviewed v0.18 catalog: the
entry/kind/name-visibility group, reserved and unadmitted program kinds, the
standard-input label near-misses, and the effect-row and release-attribution
group including the EFF-2 canonical `return unit;` pair. No existing case
source, verdict, expectation kind, or status changes.

Every case source was run through whitefootc. The four system-unadmitted cases
produce their exact expected verdict today (accept, accept, OP-1, TYPE-5); the
20 kind-declaring cases pass lexical formation, terminal membership, grammar
derivation, and FORM-2 canonical rendering before stopping at the
system-declaration-domain gate, so they carry `pending` with a reason naming
the gating task.

## aeb6d949 2026-08-06 compiler: admit the FN-7 entry forms and check system call arguments

FN-7. `Checker::check_entry_form` replaces `check_main_header` and implements
the complete v0.18 entry-form judgment over one closed unit. The unlabelled
form keeps its exact admitted set: no program kind, no value parameter, `own
unit`, and one of the same four effect rows. A kind-declaring entry is
admitted through the closed kind table (`command`; `service`, `embedded`, and
every unlisted spelling are the one hard error FN-7 fixes for them), the closed
standard-input table (label prefix equal to the entry's kind IDENT, tail equal
to a row, each row at most once, selected rows in strictly increasing
table-ordinal order, written mode and type equal to the row with the type bound
to the resolved SYS-2 nominal rather than to source bytes), the row's fixed
`own ExitStatus` result, and a written effect row drawn only from that row's
admitted categories. A `command` entry selecting no row is admitted. Whole-unit:
no other declaration may carry a `program_kind`, no `input_label` may sit
outside the entry's own parameters (a `fn_sig` included), and a source `call`
resolving to a kind-declaring entry is rejected -- program start is its only
invocation (PROG-3).

Locations. Every rejection now uses the exact node FN-7 names for it, which
v0.18 fixed and the v0.17-era checker reported at the whole `fn_decl`: the
`program_kind` node, the `input_label` node, the complete `param` node, the
`rtype` node, the `effects` node, the `generics` or `region_params` child, the
`call` node, and the `fn_decl` node only as the stated fallback. Nine new issue
kinds carry the closed table each rejection failed against. No program changes
verdict from this: the accepted set is unchanged.

Ordering. Source-language judgments the checker has implemented now run before
the remaining capability stops. An unsupported capability establishes no source
violation (DIAG-1), and the previous order let an `external` or `blocks` row
mask an FN-7 rejection -- the defect flagged at task 0006's closure. Both
directions are pinned: `fn main() -> own unit external` is an FN-7 rejection,
while the same category on a declaration FN-7 does not govern keeps its
explicit unsupported stop, which is EFF-2's judgment to remove (task 0009).

GRAM-11. A call whose callee resolves to a SYS-2 operation is checked against
that operation's declared parameter names in declared order, with positional
operands inadmissible. This is the argument-spelling half only; region targs,
types, effects, and lowering stay in the system semantic path that still stops
as unsupported. `arg_get` is covered by negative cases alone: SYS-2 names its
second parameter `index`, which FORM-3 excludes from IDENT, so v0.18 admits no
complete legal `arg_get` call (recorded at task 0007 closure; a v0.19 ruling is
requested). Nothing was renamed to work around it.

Boundary. The checker records the admitted entry form, and lowering states that
it implements exactly the unlabelled program start. Every `command` entry names
`ExitStatus`, so it still stops at its first resolved system use: the
unsupported boundary moved from the entry declaration to the system semantic
path, it did not disappear.

Conformance. Nine FN-7 cases flip `pending` -> runnable, each verified to
produce exactly its recorded `expect`, and each additionally pinned in the
compiler's corpus-negative regression. Three entry-form cases stay pending with
their stale reasons refreshed to name the real remaining gate. No `expect`,
`rules`, `doc`, or case source byte changed.

## 61936d6c 2026-08-06 compiler: qualify and emit the argument and path system interface

Implements the QUAL-1 target-qualification table for the macOS/Linux
command targets as fixed Rust data consulted once, before layout and
before any use of an operation is emitted. Each row maps (specification
version, semantic ID, target, program kind) to one approved implementation
version and one private ABI symbol; parallel resource rows fix each opaque
type's target representation and its SYS-5 release code. An absent or
incompatible mapping and an unmet QUAL-2 guarantee are target-qualification
failures citing no language rule; a specified identity this compiler does
not implement stays an explicit unsupported capability.

Approved implementations are alwaysinline private wrappers with one direct
call per use site, which is the QUAL-3 inlining condition. args_count,
arg_get, host_bytes_len, host_copy_bytes, host_utf8_len, host_copy_utf8,
relative_path, and exit_status are implemented over the HOST-3 inline
lease, with a shared complete UTF-8 validator for the text route. The
QUAL-3 command bootstrap establishes the QUAL-2 backing from the native
argument vector, installs the ignored write-to-closed-pipe disposition once
before entry, supplies the declared standard inputs, invokes the entry
once, and maps the returned ExitStatus to the process status exactly.

SYS-8's range validation needs a per-site DIAG-3 record, so the checked
program and typed IR now carry a trap site on a trapping system call.

open_read, read_once, and write_once remain the one unsupported stop.

## 2af4f8bc 2026-08-06 compiler: emit the native I/O system interface

open_read, read_once, and write_once complete the qualified SYS-2
inventory on the macOS and Linux command targets, so an accepted
first-slice program now compiles, links, and runs end to end.

open_read resolves a relative path against the capability's own
descriptor through the target's directory-relative facility, never a
prefix concatenated onto an ambient working directory (PATH-2). Both
transfers validate their range first and trap through the site's own
record before any host action, report a count of zero for an empty
range without issuing a transfer, and return the host's reported
progress without a second attempt (SYS-8): read_once maps the three
ReadOutcome cases with the cursor advancing by exactly the reported
count, and write_once reports the accepted prefix and maps a host
zero-length write to WriteZero rather than Ok(0). One cold shared
mapper turns a native error code into exactly one of SYS-7's thirty
portable classes with the two-field inline detail; each target's table
is the complete closed class set in declared order and an unmapped
native error is Other.

The last UnsupportedSystemInterface stop and its driver arm are
removed with the capability they described.

## 501cf1ef 2026-08-06 programs: the sequential wfgrep command and its correctness oracle

`tests/programs/wfgrep.wf` is the first real Whitefoot command program: a
command entry taking all four standard inputs, a literal byte-pattern
line search over a file list, matched lines to standard output, per-file
diagnostics to standard error, and ExitStatus 0 (match), 1 (no match), or
2 (error). It follows dossier §10.1 exactly — the pattern copied through
`host_copy_bytes` with no Unicode restriction, the path retyped by
`relative_path` and opened under `command.cwd`, one reusable input buffer
whose boundary overlap is carried in ordinary storage, matching over only
the returned prefix, one reusable output batch flushed by `write_once`
through a write-until-accepted loop. Four allocations for the whole
invocation; none per file, line, or match.

`compiler/tests/programs/wfgrep.rs` compares published bytes against a
trusted reference over empty, short, unterminated, exactly-one-buffer,
multichunk, boundary-straddling, non-text, multi-file, and
many-flush inputs, and owns the three cases needing real OS mechanisms:
a destination with no reader (BrokenPipe as a value, never a signal), a
symlink leaving the directory the capability names, and a file whose
content changes between invocations.

## c85a1658 2026-08-06 research: the §9.1 initialization-cost row against an uninitialized control

The one §9.1 row that cannot be a code-shape gate. §9.1 deliberately gives the
two buffer rows different controls: an initialized control answers whether
initialization happens once, which is structural and now gated in
cost_shape.rs; only an uninitialized control can answer whether paying for it
at all is material, because an initialized control carries the same cost on
both sides and cancels it.

Preregistered before any number was observed. Whitefoot's drain over a
language-initialized reused buffer measures at practical parity with the same
drain in C over malloc storage (1.0014 [0.9982, 1.0083]), and the same-source
calloc/malloc ablation is likewise parity (0.9985 [0.9935, 1.0071]).

Those two observables could only ever fail to refute the hypothesis, since a
one-page fill is orders of magnitude below what whole-process timing resolves.
That was stated in the preregistration, which is why a third, decisive
observable measures the cost directly: initializing one 4096-byte page costs
28.76 ns — 10,612x below 1% of the 256 MiB drain, and 612x below 1% of the
program's 1.76 ms empty-input process floor, so no input size makes it
material. Dossier §11's stop condition did not fire.

v0.19 restricts no type under OWN-2, but the checker admitted a non-own mode
only for buffer, slice, struct, box, and system-resource types. Scalars and
enum nominals now take the same path, and with them the deref read, the
write through a uniq holder, the OWN-13 borrowed match, borrow-mode results,
lowering, and the backend.

Two predicates in check/borrows.rs state what is carried and which borrows
address storage; check/types.rs and check/generics.rs consult them for
parameters and results. check_borrow and check_child_reborrow gained the
addressed-storage arm. A reference_value marker on TypedExpression lets
TYPE-7 reject a bare holder, a borrow_expr, and a reference-returning call
where a referent is required, so match scrutinees are judged by one rule.
return now splits FN-1 (result mode) from OWN-4 (region relation).

Representation generalizes the struct-borrow machinery instead of adding a
second one: BorrowStruct/ReborrowStruct become BorrowAddressed/
ReborrowAddressed carrying a type, a new DerefAddressed node keeps reading
through a holder distinct from passing the holder on, and
IrType::NominalAddress(id) becomes IrType::Address(IrAddressed) with
AddressOf/Load/Store over any directly stored referent.

SET-1 hands the shared-borrow referent to OWN-5 in its own text; the set
path cited SET-1 and now cites OWN-5, matching the protected case
x-borrow-write-through-shared-borrow. The lib test asserting the old
citation is updated; the rejection is unchanged.

Five regressions added: the admitted forms with their checked nodes and
binder modes, the still-rejected near misses (OWN-10 escape, OWN-4 return,
TYPE-7 implicit read and three match scrutinee shapes, OWN-5 shared write
and double uniq, OWN-12 aliasing arguments), the EFF-2 row both ways, and
two backend runs proving a callee write through &uniq lands in the caller's
storage.

## b854ec8a 2026-08-06 semantic: one predicate for TYPE-7's implicit read at referent positions

Task 0025 added TYPE-7 exclusivity for a box holder at the match scrutinee
and the indexed-place root; this task added it for a borrow-mode reference
value at the match scrutinee. Both assert the same rule, so they become one
predicate rather than two tests that happen to agree.

reads_implicitly_through_holder takes the two facts the two holder shapes
need, because this compiler represents them differently: a borrow-mode value
already carries its referent's checked type, so only its provenance
distinguishes the holder from the referent, while a box binding carries the
holder's type, so its referent is the question. A RequiredReferent names what
the position wants — Enum for a match scrutinee, IndexableStorage for an
index root — and both clauses are judged against it.

Consequence at the index root: a borrow of something no index could reach
now cites TYPE-5 rather than TYPE-7, matching how the box clause already
behaved and how TYPE-7 words its exclusivity ("where its referent selected
type would be required"). No case moved.

Both regression sets stay green: 0025's box-holder match and index cases and
this task's four borrow-holder scrutinee cases.

## c3e1a0ad 2026-08-06 lowering: emit a check-aware wide probe at recognized byte-walk headers

Recognize, by semantic rule on the checked AST, loops of the byte-walk
form: exit guard on an outside induction/bound pair, one guarded u8 load
at the induction binding, a neutral middle whose observable arms are
dominated by equality tests of the loaded byte, and the single-step
increment. At such a header the single lowering path emits one new IR
operation, buffer.probe.skip: a 16-byte probe whose internal guard
index + 16 <= min(bound, len) proves every skipped iteration is
observationally i := i + 1, so it skips only provably no-op iterations
and never traps or reports. The scalar body, every trap site, and every
DIAG-3 record are untouched; recognition failure is ordinary lowering
with zero change.

Unit tests pin recognition and the decline cases; a new trap-identity
oracle (compiler/tests/programs/wide_scan.rs) runs five probed walks and
asserts exact per-byte results across lane boundaries, exact pre-trap
published effects, and the exact per-site OP-4 record with SIGABRT on
hostile bounds at the first byte and one past the last byte.

Per research/experiments/wide-scan-lowering/PROTOCOL.md (route b); both
gates green.

## c364a9bc 2026-08-06 semantic: admit OWN-14 returned reborrows; recategorize non-argument forms

The written reborrow position becomes an explicit three-way fact
(forbidden, call-argument with OWN-6's result-mode condition, complete
return expression) carried to the one borrow-checking path. The return
position admits a mode-preserving reborrow of a parameter or let-bound
holder: creation keeps the existing OWN-11 loop rule and OWN-10
borrow-rooted region obligation and the OWN-5 loan judgment, and the
created borrow flows into the unchanged OWN-4/FN-1 return judgments, so a
callee-local region still cannot leave through the signature. Every other
non-argument occurrence of a reborrow form, including the deref-free
borrow of a holder binding and a return-position reborrow failing the
admission, is the OWN-14 hard error carrying the rule's restructuring;

## 52d5b0b8 2026-08-06 semantic: OWN-13 arm-scoped child reborrows suspend their uniq root

A borrow-mode payload binder already resolved to the scrutinee root's
place plus its field suffix; what moves is the root's own allowance.
Creating the taken arm's binders from a uniq-mode root marks that root
binding suspended: every read, write, set commit, reborrow creation, or
holder transfer through it is the OWN-5 suspension rejection, asked by
each position after its earlier-defined judgments so same-node citations
keep DIAG-1's first-definition rank. A suspended ancestor's loan no
longer confiscates accesses through its own descendants — the binder's
narrower loan carries the exclusivity — which is exactly the OWN-13/OWN-5
contradiction the v0.20 batch closes. Suspension is a region-scoped claim
like a slice loan: the ownership join takes the union across arms, since
binder borrows live to the end of their derived region's block under
OWN-4's named-region liveness, and there is no arm-end resumption
(deliberately deferred). Shared roots stay plain overlapping shared
borrows, and a shared binder roots the next scrutinee in a chain.
Regressions cover the accepted payload read, shared re-match and chain,
in-arm and post-match suspension (including the mixed-arm join), and
reborrow creation through a suspended holder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## fafd1120 2026-08-06 semantic: DIAG-1 same-node citation rank as a spec-derived order

One offending use establishing several post-resolution rejections cites
the rule defined first in the active specification. The general mechanism
is SemanticRule::definition_rank, the definition order of every citable
rule, machine-checked against the active specification bytes by a test
that re-derives the order from the text; sites with a known simultaneity
ask their judgments in ascending rank and carry a const assertion binding
their code order to the rank. The known instance moves: the return
position asks TYPE-7's implicit read (a live holder returned where the
written rtype requires its referent value, per FN-1's forms-no-candidate
exclusivity) before the operand's OWN-1 spelling judgments, so
'return holder;' on a box holder cites TYPE-7, while returning the holder
where the holder itself is required stays OWN-1. Regressions pin the box
bare and moved forms, the uniq-holder form, and the OWN-1 control.

checks "pbase plus the first N psuffixes" as the base place, with the
wrong-base judgment anchored at the subscript's psuffix node for
subscripts and at the place node for len/slice_of operands.
resolve_struct_path takes the suffix slice to walk and reports a subscript
inside its span as the same CompositeValues unsupported the old
index-based-base produced; the borrow paths keep their v0.21
RegionsAndBorrows class for subscripted borrow places via an explicit
guard. The element type is derived from the base place's indexable type
(the Type child is gone per SWEEP A2); the offset stays own u64 with the
Type5 citation unchanged and its anchor moved to the offset atom node the
rule text names; the OP-4 TrapSite anchors at the psuffix node. FN-8
rejects subscripts by psuffix arm. Every rule citation is otherwise
spelling-transported; lowering consumes the unchanged checked model.

Resolution: the psuffix role classifier adds the projected-field role only
for the field arm; the subscript arm owns bracket punctuation only and its
offset atom classifies through the atom's own productions.

Grammar tables: complete the first generation's SELECT_2 rows with the
84 missing ]-closing follow rows. The subscript's ] occupies exactly the
lookahead contexts the old index call's ) did, so every row carrying the
RightParen predicate gains RightBracket variants (each position
independently, plus both) on the same arm with the same flags, deduped
against existing pairs; without these an inner place before ] fails
closed (table[ordinary] did not parse). Rows 1919 -> 2003; atoms stay
364; cross-arm disjointness and provenance audits stay green.

Identity pins move to the v0.22 candidate
(governance/spec-evolution/kernel-spec-v0.22-candidate.md, SHA-256
b133b793629d28e7ee1b7ad0ae3d49185932b9390f5c25517f0fb0ea2fc8a6e8,
128 rules), matching the 0030 staging pattern: whitefoot-spec compares
those bytes, qualification gates flip to v0.22, and the grammar
expectations pin 65 productions / 75 decisions / 76 terminal predicates.

Catalog: the index_get operation row leaves OPERATION_FAMILIES (84 -> 83),
shrinking the derived reserved sets by its member; the SYS-2 signature
renderer follows the candidate's canonical region-parameter attachment.

This commit is the compiler half of the branch; the corpus and fixture
respell in the following commit turns the full suite green.

## 7f68c71f 2026-08-07 compiler: derive the grammar tables from the specification and gate it

The strong-LL(2) tables are not hand-editable, and every grammar task so
far built a one-shot generator offline and deleted it, so nothing checked
that the committed tables were still the tables the specification implies.
Task 0031 hand-added 84 `]`-closing follow rows; nothing caught it.

Land the generator as `whitefoot-grammar-tables` and wire the invariant to
a test that runs inside `make -C compiler check`, so the committed tables
are now machine-checked against the normative EBNF. `--check` runs the same
comparison from the command line.

Two inputs are historical rather than derived and are carried as explicit
tables with comments saying so: the `Production` enum order, and the
decision-slot order (`psuffix`'s choice holds the last slot because v0.22
appended it instead of renumbering).

The regenerated v0.22 tables differ from the committed ones in exactly two
ways, both inherited from 0031 and both isolated to this commit so the
v0.23 delta lands against a clean base:

  - 70 predicate pairs across 27 decisions are dropped. Each placed `]` at
    a position the grammar cannot derive: decision 8 is
    `variant := TYPEID "(" vfield_list? ")" ";"` and carried
    (arm 1, RightBracket, Semicolon), but the parser's next action after
    that arm is Match(RightParen), which `]` cannot satisfy.
  - 57 rows have their provenance corrected. The committed rows named the
    first node bearing the predicate (192 = region_params' `]`, 41 =
    variant's `)`, 125 = law's `,`, 170 = generics' `>`); the derivation
    names the real site (478 = psuffix's `]`, 421/432/470 =
    call/construct/deref `)`). Provenance feeds diagnostics only.

SELECT_ROWS 2003 -> 1893; the count pin moves with it as it does for every
grammar change. No parser, diagnostic, finalize or conformance test changes
verdict. The stale enum doc comment ("the two productions v0.18 added" —
claim_stmt arrived in v0.21) is corrected in passing.

## 11513c51 2026-08-07 compiler: remove two spec-identity checks that compared a value with itself

Both operands of the `whitefoot-spec` frontend-identity branch, and both
operands of the same assertion in the grammar inventory test, were the same
constant. `SYNTAX_DATA_SPEC_HASH` and `TERMINAL_CONTRACT_SPEC_HASH` are
declared `= ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_HASH` (compiler/src/syntax/grammar.rs:15,
compiler/src/syntax/terminal.rs:4), so neither comparison could ever fail and
neither said anything about the committed frontend data. Verified before the
change by printing all three: identical, and definitionally so.

Both constants stay. They carry a real runtime check elsewhere — the caller's
spec identity is compared against them in `classify_terminals` and the parser
engine, where the other operand is a runtime value.

The binding these checks claimed to make is already machine-checked, and much
more strongly, by `committed_tables_are_derived_from_the_active_grammar`: it
regenerates the whole of `syntax/grammar/generated.rs` from the active
specification's EBNF and compares byte for byte. A provenance check here would
be implied by that one, so this deletes rather than reimplements.

The third tautology in this family, the hand-typed hex literal that
`compiler/src/spec.rs` compares against `ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_HASH`, is left in
place: it becomes a real check of two independently-derived quantities in the
next commit, which makes the constant a computed digest. Its exact text is the
check, so removing and re-adding it would be churn.

## 6266ea35 2026-08-07 compiler: derive the active specification identity from its own bytes

Adds a dependency-free SHA-256 (compiler/src/spec/sha256.rs) and
`computed_active_spec_hash`, which hashes the embedded specification. The
`whitefoot-spec` gate now rejects any disagreement between that and the
recorded `ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_HASH`, so the constant is checked against the
bytes instead of trusted, and an activation that installs a specification
without moving the identity fails immediately.

The implementation is held to outside values, not to itself: the unit tests
carry four published SHA-256 vectors plus the one-million-byte vector, each
reproduced with `shasum -a 256` before being written down, and the identity
test compares the computed digest against the hex the owner approved for v0.22
in governance/APPROVALS.md. Every message length from zero to two full blocks
is also compared against a separate naive implementation that shares no padding
arithmetic, so no padding boundary can be quietly wrong.

DEVIATION FROM THE TASK CARD, for review. C1b asks for the constant itself to
be a const-fn SHA-256 over ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_BYTES. Measured on this
specification (274,650 bytes), that costs too much to keep:

  - a `const` is re-evaluated in every crate that reads it, and the constant
    evaluator needs about 12s per crate for this input (31s using
    `u32::rotate_right`, which the evaluator interprets far more slowly);
  - the library build alone goes from 1s to 12s, and the whole compiler gate
    from roughly 40s to 87s without yet reaching green;
  - `long_running_const_eval` is deny-by-default and its level resolves in the
    crate doing the evaluation, not where the code lives, so silencing it needs
    an `#![allow]` in the lib and in each of the four binary crate roots.

Hashing at runtime costs about a millisecond and closes the same failure mode,
so the constant stays and the gate checks it. Reverting to the card's literal
form is a one-line change here plus those allow attributes.

Two more tautologies of the C1a class turned up in the identity test while
editing it, and are repaired here rather than left beside the new check:
`ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_BYTES` was asserted equal to `ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_TEXT
.as_bytes()`, which is its definition, and `ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_VERSION` was
asserted equal to its own literal. The version now has a real check in the next
commit; the path is checked against the version label, which is maintained
separately, so a half-finished version bump fails.

## 85d3e04e 2026-08-07 governance: record the specification activation chain and check it

Adds one exact line per activation to governance/APPROVALS.md —
`ACTIVE-SPEC: <version> <sha256-installed> <sha256-superseded>` — and makes
`whitefoot-spec` parse them. It rejects a build whose embedded specification
does not hash to the digest the chain records for it, whose version disagrees
with either `ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_VERSION` or the specification's own title line,
or whose chain has a link that does not name the digest installed before it.
A line carrying the prefix without the exact four-field shape is an error, not
a line to skip, so a typo cannot silently shrink the chain.

The card asks only for the active version's line. The whole exact-approval era
is backfilled instead, v0.9 through v0.22, because a chain of one has no link
to check: with fourteen lines the predecessor rule has thirteen real links from
the first commit. Every digest is the exact-byte value the owner already
approved in an entry above — cross-checked by grep, all fourteen present — and
each was read from `shasum -a 256` of the installed file rather than retyped.
v0.9 is where exact-byte approval began, so its predecessor field is `-`;
v0.19 uses the superseding approval, which is the one installed. The section
says in prose that these lines restate approvals and grant none.

Checked by failing, not only by passing: three mutations of the real record
each take the gate red — a wrong digest on the active line, a broken link in
the middle of the chain, and a deleted active line — alongside unit tests for
the malformed, short, over-long, empty, and version-disagreement cases.

## 366a7c99 2026-08-07 governance: check every released specification against its recorded digest

Adds `spec-archive-integrity` to `make check`: for all 23 recorded
`(version, digest)` pairs the file must exist and hash to the digest, and every
`spec/kernel-spec-v*.md` on disk must have a record. Both directions matter —
the first catches a released specification edited after the fact, the second
catches one added or renamed with no identity at all.

`spec-append-only` only sees the paths one commit touches, and the `pre-commit`
hook is skipped by `--no-verify`, by merge commits, and by a clone whose
`core.hooksPath` points elsewhere. This target reads landed state, so none of
those routes gets past it. `governance/hooks/pre-merge-commit` closes the merge
route earlier by running the same target beside the staged append-only check;
the hook is convenience, and the comment says so.

The nine versions before exact-byte approval began, v0.0 through v0.8, had no
recorded digest anywhere. They are backfilled under a deliberately different
prefix, `ARCHIVE-SPEC:`, in a section that says these are a measurement taken
today with `shasum -a 256`, are not approvals, and pin whatever was on disk —
including, if it came to that, bytes that were already wrong. Recording them as
approvals would have been a lie the format itself could not correct later.

The check uses `shasum -a 256` rather than the compiler's SHA-256 on purpose:
it shares no code with the implementation added two commits ago, so the two
cannot be wrong together. The runner's `hashlib` pin is a third agreeing path.

Checked by failing: five mutations each take the target red — a released
specification gaining a byte, a recorded digest altered, a record naming a file
that does not exist, a specification file whose record was deleted, and every
record removed at once, which the reverse direction catches instead of passing
an empty loop.

## d5ca6d7f 2026-08-07 compiler: give the grammar verifier both specifications as arguments

`verify_candidate` compared a candidate against the compiled-in
`ACTIVE_KERNEL_SPEC_BYTES`. The workflow's mandatory pre-activation check runs
it on the candidate that is about to become the active specification, so on the
run that matters most the comparison was a file against itself and passed
whatever it was given. It now takes a baseline and a candidate, both read at
run time, and `whitefoot-grammar` takes both paths.

The binary no longer imports the active bytes at all, which is the point: there
is no compiled-in copy left for the comparison to collapse onto. Checked on
real files — v0.21 as baseline against v0.22 correctly reports a changed
frontend contract, a comparison the old form could not express.

Tests are rewritten against the two-argument form, not dropped. The five
fail-closed cases now name the baseline explicitly, and a new test asserts the
argument is what is compared: two copies of a mutated specification verify
against each other, and the active specification then fails against that
baseline. `exact_active_frontend_contract_verifies` became
`active_compiler_grammar_is_consistent` and calls `verify_compiler_grammar` and
`run_parser_probes` directly, since the production counts and the probes were
always its real content and the contract comparison never could fail.

docs/WORKFLOW.md step 3 and compiler/README.md give the two-path command. Three

## 29ab4328 2026-08-07 compiler: render if/else through FORM-2's join line

The finalized topology held one brace pair per node, assigned from the
last brace the node owned, so an `if` with a braced `else` kept only the
else block and lost the then block. Braces now pair in source order into
a second optional pair that only if_stmt and value_if use; every other
block-bearing production still owns exactly one, because a nested block
belongs to a nested production node.

Both pairs break and indent, so an else block's children get their
format depth. The close-and-open line `} else {` is new -- no v0.22
production rendered one -- and follows the `requires` block's `} {`
precedent by suppressing the break after a close brace that joins a
continuation. An `else if` chain reaches the same rule through the
`else` terminal the outer node owns while the nested if_stmt owns the
block.

The new test asserts the exact canonical bytes for all four shapes and,
through only_these_trivia_bytes_render, that removing any single trivia
byte makes them non-canonical.

## f38e5bf0 2026-08-07 compiler: pin the flat else-if chain as a structural property

An else-position if_stmt begins after the then-block's closing brace, so
it is inside no brace pair of its parent and inside_body leaves it at the
outer format depth. FORM-2's rule that an else-position `if` is never a
nested introducer line therefore costs no special case.

A three-deep chain is pinned so that adding one is caught: depth would
accumulate and indent each arm one level deeper.

check_construct resolves prelude Option/Result constructors by reading the
expectation and never consults written targs, so None<buffer<u8>>() does
not rescue the site either. let_stmt was the only construct position whose
expectation came from an annotation, so A3 removes the sole supply.

Measured: 1 corpus site, 4 compiler inline fixtures. The rule is the
problem, not the count -- after A3 `let x = None();` has no legal spelling.

The coherent repair adds the prelude variant constructors to TYPE-5's
retained-argument class, which is what the delta's own rationale ("because
no operand can supply them") already argues for. That moves the candidate
and re-keys three digest pins, so it is a ruling, not an executor call.

## 64303497 2026-08-07 syntax: render canonical bytes beside the auditor, and gate the corpus on it

`canonical/` could only answer "are these bytes canonical?". Rendering was
the missing direction, and without it a corpus migration would have to
compute every byte of spacing and indentation itself — including the
`} else {` join line no v0.22 production produced.

The renderer reuses the auditor's rules rather than restating them. The
gap descriptor is factored out of `gap_matches` into `canonical_gap`,
which turns a `GapStyle`, a format depth and the two neighbouring
predicates into exact bytes; the auditor compares source against it and
the renderer emits it. There is one layout rule, not two that agree.

Rendering has no source verdict: handed a finalized tree it produces the
bytes that tree denotes, so it either succeeds or hits a ceiling.

Wired to a gate, per the hygiene rule that a tool ships with a caller.
`compiler/tests/canonical_corpus.rs` runs inside `make check` and holds
every corpus file to FORM-2: a canonical file re-renders to itself, a
deliberately non-canonical one renders to different bytes, and whatever
went in, what comes out is canonical and idempotent. That makes the
corpus canonical by construction and lets a migration emit any layout
that parses.

118 of the 420 corpus files round-trip byte-exactly today; the other 302
carry v0.22 spellings and do not yet derive under the v0.23 grammar, so
the gate stays red until the migration lands. The two FORM-2 negative
cases are named rather than pattern-skipped so a third cannot appear
unnoticed.

Lib failure set unchanged against the round-4 baseline: zero added, zero
removed. Passing 257 -> 259 for the two new renderer tests.

## 4a40be78 2026-08-07 semantic: derive let binders and delivery sets instead of reading them

[TYPE-5] a `let` binder's mode and type are derived from its selected
right-hand side, so `check_let` no longer reads the `Mode` and `Type`
children the v0.23 grammar deletes. Each arm checks its right-hand side
first and takes what it produces: an `ordinary_let_rhs` from the
expression, a `propagate_let_rhs` from the operand's own Ok payload
[ERR-3], and a value initializer from the delivery set. The OWN-5 slice
guard, the borrow-mode support guard and `borrow_for_destination` re-key
onto the derived mode rather than a written one.

[GIVE-1] inverts with it. `GiveContext` no longer carries an expectation
built from the annotation; it carries the mode and type the first
delivering `give` produced, every later `give` must agree with them
exactly, and a delivery set that stays empty rejects at the `let_stmt`
node.

That leaves no consumer of an expected type in the expression checker, so
the channel goes with it. `check_construct` read it to name the prelude
generic nominal; under the amended [TYPE-5] the variant constructors
`None`, `Some`, `Ok` and `Err` write their nominal's arguments in every
position, and those written arguments are read here exactly as
`generic_substitution` reads a source generic's, so both classes cite
TYPE-5 at the complete `construct`. `ensure_source_constructor_instance`
interns the instance they name; the propagate pre-pass that interned one
from the deleted annotation is removed, because that instance is the
callee's and its signature already interned it. [TYPE-6] already said
construction never consults an expected nominal type, so this is the
implementation catching up with the rule rather than a new judgment.

Eight regressions in `semantic::tests::derivation` pin the derivation on
v0.23-spelled source, including `let absent = None<buffer<u8>>();` — the
witness for which no legal spelling existed before the amendment.

Lib: 267 passed / 271 failed. The failure set is byte-identical to the
recorded baseline, zero added and zero removed; passing moved 259 -> 267,
which is exactly the eight new tests.

## 0661c641 2026-08-07 semantic: select every deleted-class operation row from its operands

[OP-2] the selected type is derived from the operands, never written. The
integer path takes the first operand's exact type as the selection, checks
`accepts_operand_type` against it, and then holds every later operand to
the row's argument type for that selection — which for the two-operand
arithmetic and comparison rows is the selected type itself, so "both
operands must have one identical exact type" falls out and cites TYPE-5 at
the second operand atom, as the rule names. A written type argument now
cites OP-1; v0.22 cited FN-2 for its absence, so this judgment inverted.

The same inversion covers the rest of the deleted class: the Bool rows,
enum equality, the float rows, `len`, `box_new`, and `buffer_new` — the one
row that selects from its *second* operand, since its first is the u64
element count. `cvt`, `reinterpret`, `array_new` and `arena_new` are
[TYPE-5]'s retained class and are untouched; `finf` and `fnan` are nullary,
so they keep their written result type and are the one float row that
reads one.

[STOR-5]'s box-content judgment moved rather than went away. It rode on the
written referent type; it now tests the derived referent and cites the
operand that supplied it. A directly slice-typed operand is the only path:
struct fields and enum payloads are held to STOR-5 at their own
declarations and `CheckedFlatElement` cannot be a slice, so no array,
buffer, or nominal referent can smuggle a region in.
`box_content_that_bears_a_region_still_rejects_under_stor5` pins it to the
cited bytes.

Six more regressions in `semantic::tests::derivation`, two of them pinned
to the exact cited bytes rather than to the rule alone, because [OP-2] and
[STOR-5] each name which operand they land on.

Lib: 259 passed / 285 failed. Fourteen tests moved green -> red and NONE is
a regression in the ordinary sense: every one fails with `Op1 /
InvalidOperation` on a v0.22-spelled inline fixture that still writes
`len<u8>(...)`, `ieq<i32>(...)` or `box_new<slice<'r, u8>>(...)`. That is
the new written-argument rejection meeting un-migrated sources, so this
half is coupled to the inline-fixture migration exactly as GRAM-6's
Bool-scrutinee rejection is coupled to the 87 `True() =>` arms. The set was
diffed, not counted: those 14 are the only additions and there are zero

## aea2f580 2026-08-07 semantic: check the Bool conditional, reject the forms GRAM-6 refuses, and migrate the fixtures

[GRAM-6] conditional control is type-driven with one form per class. A
Bool-scrutinee `match` becomes a hard error at the scrutinee node, and the
`if` spelling it points to is checked here for the first time: the semantic
layer carried no `IfStmt` or `ValueIf` at all, `check_statement` had no arm
for one, and `SemanticRule` had no `Gram6` to cite. The rule's definition
rank is 2 in the active text, which moves every later rank up one; the
machine check against the specification bytes now covers 40 rules, not 39.

`check_if` cannot call `check_match`: that reads `arm` nodes and resolves
each one's variant by constructor name, and an `if` owns none. It builds the
two arms itself from the same Bool descriptor — `True` tagged 1, `False`
tagged 0, extracted rather than duplicated — so both spellings produce one
`CheckedStatement::Match` over `CheckedEnumType::Bool`. Lowering,
entailment, cleanup and drops therefore need no change, which the new
backend test demonstrates by executing every branch instead of asserting it.

The two blocks are `Stmt` children of the one conditional node, separated
only by the brace pairs `if_stmt` and `value_if` alone own, so `TreeView`
grows the accessor that splits them and names the three alternative shapes.

Three rejections, each at the node the rule names and each pinned to its
cited bytes: the Bool scrutinee, an empty `else` at its own `if_stmt`, and
an unflattened `else if` at the NESTED `if_stmt`. Two carve-outs belong to
[GIVE-1] and are not taken, because a `value_if`'s `else` is mandatory by
grammar: an empty one is an empty delivery set, and an else block holding
one else-free `if` can neither deliver nor be spelled as a chain.

[GIVE-1] gives an else-if chain one delivery set belonging to the chain's
binding, so `opens_delivery` is not "this is a `value_if`" — only the
outermost one opens the context and each chained one contributes to it, the
way a statement `match` propagates its `give`s. Discovering that cost a
compiler failure: the chained node is a `ValueIf`, which `check_statement`
has no arm for, so the shared body recurses instead.

All 105 Bool matches in the compiler's own fixtures move to `if` — 210 arms
across 13 files, the True and False counts equal in every file. 95 take the
statement form and 10 the `value_if`; an empty `False` arm becomes the
else-free `if`, an empty `True` arm becomes the empty then-block [ERR-2]
admits, and a value initializer keeps its `else` even when empty so it stays
a `value_if`. The one file left alone is `tests/conditionals.rs`, whose
fixture must remain a Bool `match` to prove GRAM-6 rejects it.

Those fixtures cannot turn green here: they still carry the v0.22
annotations, deleted type arguments and prefix spellings M3 owns, so this
is judged by the failure SET, which is byte-identical — zero added, zero
removed against 285 — and by no test's failure moving to an earlier stage,
which none does. Lib goes 259 -> 271 passed on the 12 new tests.

## 3a409d7c 2026-08-08 semantic: intern the box nominal a box_new derives

[STOR-2] `box_new(v)` returns `own box<T>` for `v`'s exact type, so once A3
deletes the `let` annotation a purely local box names `box<T>` nowhere. The
one interning site reads a *written* `box<T>` type and function checking is
`&self`, so the lookup simply missed and the program died with
`InvalidResolution` — a compiler failure deciding what source was
acceptable. The control pair differed only in whether some other
declaration happened to spell `box<u64>`.

The repair is the ruled one: the checker interns what it derives, and no
normative byte moves. `check_box_new` records the missed referent and
returns a private `CheckStop::DeferredBoxNominal`; the `&mut self` driver
drains the pending referents, interns them, and checks that one function
again. Each attempt must intern at least one new nominal, which bounds the
loop by the finitely many referent types a function can name, and the
signal is repaired where it is raised so it never reaches a diagnostic.

The phase order moves with it. `executable_nominal_count` used to close
before `collect_contracts`, which ran before function checking; a nominal
discovered while checking a function would therefore have landed outside
the executable prefix and never been lowered. Contracts are collected after
function checking now — nothing in the function path reads them, since a
source contract is rejected as a generic bound [FN-3] — so the prefix
closes after the derived boxes, which executable code allocates and drops,
and before the contract metadata, which no executable path reaches.

The guard that function checking interns nothing becomes a guard that it
interns only boxes, which is the invariant it was really protecting.

Two regressions: the control pair, asserting both programs check and that
the derived nominal is inside the executable prefix; and an executing test
that allocates a `box<Bool>` spelled nowhere, reads it back, and releases
it. The second uses a Bool because `ieq` no longer resolves and `==` is not
checked yet, so no integer comparison can be written on this branch.

## 08504ce2 2026-08-08 docs: record the box_new repair and the phase-order move it required

Ruling (b) is discharged in `4e68436`. The record carries the part a
successor most needs: the executable-nominal prefix closed before contracts
were collected and before function checking ran, so anything the function
path discovered would never have been lowered. Contracts move after
function checking, which is safe only because a source contract is rejected
as a generic bound.

## 27316895 2026-08-08 semantic: resolve the infix spelling to its operation row

[OP-1] (ii) infix resolution. The v0.23 catalog respell landed in round 1
and deleted the named spellings, but nothing ever taught the checker to
read the infix form, so arithmetic and comparison compiled under NEITHER
spelling: `iadd.wrap` failed resolution with an empty candidate set while
`a +wrap b` parsed and then died at `InvalidCanonicalTree`. The cause was
one line — `check_expression_in_context` took `only_child`, and [GRAM-5]'s
`expr := atom infix_tail?` is the one shape with two children.

The operator token selects the row by its exact bytes: bare `+ - * / %` are
the trapping rows unchanged, the suffixed forms carry wrap, checked and
saturating, and `== != <= >=` respell the four nonstrict comparisons. `ilt`
and `igt` keep their named spelling (O1) and no token maps to them.
[GRAM-9] admits one operation per expression, so there is no precedence to
apply: the left operand is the expression's own atom and the right is the
tail's.

Both spellings then share one judgment. The row check is extracted rather
than copied, so [OP-2]'s operand-derived selection, the trap site and the
checked-error result are decided in one place and the two spellings cannot
drift apart.

**Five operators needed the box_new repair generalized.** `+checked`,
`-checked`, `*checked`, `/checked` and `%checked` produce `Result<T,
Overflow>` and `Result<T, DivError>` over a *derived* `T`, and after A3
deletes the annotation nothing writes that type either — the identical
defect the `box_new` blocker named, in a second nominal family, and equally
a compiler failure on valid source. `prelude_nominal` now defers the same
way a missed box referent does, so `CheckStop::DeferredBoxNominal` becomes
`DeferredNominal` over a pending list of both kinds. The invariant guarding
function checking becomes the one it was really protecting: no *source*
nominal instance is discovered while checking a function.

Six regressions: all twenty operator tokens selecting their rows and
deriving their type from the operands, with the effect row each one owes;
the disagreeing second operand at that operand [OP-2]; an operand type
outside every row at the whole expression; the traps contribution of bare
arithmetic; an executing test whose every result is checked so a
mis-selected row traps; and the runtime overflow trap, which proves the
required check survives the shorter spelling.

## 43f9e6fd 2026-08-08 repository: ignore the compiler's own default executable name

`a.out` reached a commit once (`2b55a46`, removed by `1e3d401`) and was
caught by hand three times after that. The writer is not a test: the whole
suite runs clean, because `backend/tests.rs` and `tests/programs/support.rs`
each build into a unique temporary directory and delete what they wrote.

It is `whitefootc` itself, which names its executable `a.out` when no `-o`
is given — the cc convention, and the right default for a compiler. So
compiling a scratch program from the repository root drops one here, which
is exactly what happens while probing a language change by hand.

Ignoring it turns a discipline control into a machine one without touching
the CLI: the artifact can no longer reach a commit regardless of who runs
the compiler from where.

## 9c58406e 2026-08-08 docs: enumerate the derived-nominal class and close it at two sites

Two members were found by tripping over them, so this enumerates the class
instead of continuing to discover it. The enumeration is complete because
it runs from a closed set: every intern table is a field of `struct
Checker`, and the 25 fields partition cleanly.

The criterion turned out sharper than "the key is a derived type" — what
exposes a table is whether the interning pass keys off a written TYPE,
which A3 deletes, or off a written CALL or DECLARATION, which it does not.
`system_nominals` is keyed by a derived value and is nonetheless immune,
because its pre-pass walks call nodes; that also explains why `cvt`'s
Result never had the defect while the checked arithmetic rows did.

Exactly two tables were ever exposed, both are handled, and there is no
third.

## ebfaa171 2026-08-08 tools: the v0.22-to-v0.23 migration tool, with its parse-blocking class

[O1] condition 4: a re-runnable bin under `compiler/src/bin/`, the home the
grammar-tables generator set. The shape is the forced one — a textual
pre-pass produces *parseable* v0.23, then the source is parsed and
re-rendered, so the pre-pass owns spelling and never layout while
`render_canonical` owns layout and never spelling.

The pre-pass walks the compiler's own lexemes rather than raw text, which
is what makes it safe: a spelling inside a string or a comment is a single
lexeme and the walk only ever edits token spans. That is the same hazard
the inline-fixture migration hit from the other direction, and reading
tokens removes the whole class rather than defending against it.

This lands the one class that blocks parsing — A3's `let` annotation — and
the prelude-constructor class coupled to it, because the constructor's
arguments are exactly what the annotation carried and must be captured
before it is dropped. The remaining classes are semantic rather than
syntactic: A1's deleted type arguments, C1's operator respells and A4's
Bool matches all parse today and fail later, so they can land next without
reopening the parse gate.

Six tests: the deletion, layout normalization from deliberately odd input,
idempotence on already-migrated source, the coupled constructor rewrite,
a constructor whose annotation names no generic prelude nominal staying
bare, and a v0.22 spelling inside a string surviving untouched.

reordering, not renaming: `iadd.wrap<i32>(x, y)` becomes `x +wrap y`, which
deletes the call form and its written argument together. [GRAM-9] makes that
safe — the operands are atoms, so the infix form is exactly the two of them
with the operator between. `ilt` and `igt` keep their names (O1) and lose
only their arguments, and the closed retained class keeps everything, since
no operand can supply what it names.

Respelling is asked before de-argumenting because it subsumes it for the
rows it covers; that ordering is what the interaction test pins.

**The prelude class is not where the brief said it was.** Round 5 recorded
that a constructor takes its arguments from the `let` annotation A3
deletes. Measured over the corpus, that describes **1 of 107** uses: 98 are
returned, 2 given, 2 passed. So the arguments come from the enclosing
function's declared result type, which A3 does not delete and which the
pre-pass reads textually — no inference, just the signature. Implementing
the `let` rule alone wrote 1 constructor; adding the returned rule writes
99.

Measured over the 400 corpus files that parse: 312 changed, 1992
annotations, 886 respells, 691 argument lists, 99 constructors written and
0 left bare. The 691 and the 886 reconcile the brief's 1588 written
arguments: 1577 of them are deleted by these two classes, since a respelled
row carries its argument away with the call form it dissolves.

## 0b7aca6d 2026-08-08 tools: rewrite the Bool matches, completing the migration classes

[GRAM-6]'s class, and the only one that reshapes a tree rather than
respelling tokens. On the token stream the reshape is far smaller than it
was by hand, for the reason the tool's shape exists: layout is not its
problem. The arms' own braces become the conditional's, so only the match's
outer braces and the two arm headers move, and no indentation is computed
anywhere.

[ERR-2]'s asymmetry falls out: an empty `False` arm becomes the else-free
`if`, because GRAM-6 rejects the empty `else`, while an empty `True` arm
keeps its block, because the empty then is admitted. A value initializer
keeps its `else` even when empty — dropping it would silently demote the
initializer to a statement. An `else` holding exactly one conditional
flattens to `else if`, which GRAM-6 requires.

A `False`-first match would need its bodies exchanged rather than its
headers rewritten, so the tool reports one instead of guessing. The corpus
writes `True` first in every case measured.

Over the 400 corpus files that parse: 260 conditionals, 5 flattened — both
figures matching an independent count of the shapes. Five tests, one per
branch of the rule.

## b12dc8a5 2026-08-08 semantic: answer structural expr queries for the infix shape

`return a == b;` failed with `Semantics/Compiler: InvalidCanonicalTree` — an
internal compiler failure where the workflow requires a source rejection or an
accepted program. Two `return`-position queries reach into the `expr` node with
`only_child`, and [GRAM-5]'s `expr := atom infix_tail?` is the one alternative
with two children, so both fail the tree on every infix return.

Enumerated from the grammar rather than from the failing tests: eleven
productions take a bare `expr` — `if_stmt` and `value_if` conditions,
`ordinary_let_rhs`, `propagate_let_rhs`, `set_stmt`, `return_stmt`,
`check_stmt`, `claim_stmt`, `give_stmt`, and the `match_stmt` and `value_match`
scrutinees. `expr_stmt := call ";"` takes a `call`, so infix is unreachable
there. Ten of the eleven route through `check_expression`, which has handled
infix since 3af8478; `return_stmt` is the sole gap, and it has two independent
broken sites reached under complementary conditions:

- `check_return_implicit_read` ([TYPE-7]'s implicit read), reached only when the
  result mode is `own`. An infix reads its operands as operands, so there is no
  implicit read of a returned place.
- `complete_borrow_expression` ([OWN-14]'s returned reborrow), reached only when
  the result mode is a borrow — so a borrow-returning function with an infix
  return expression failed internally instead of citing FN-1. Its control, the
  same function returning a plain non-borrow atom, cites FN-1 cleanly.

Both are structural queries asking which of `atom infix_tail? | call |
construct` an expression is written as. Infix is none of the three, so the
answer is "no such child" rather than a failed tree. One shared
`sole_expression_child` beside `only_child` gives that answer once, so a future
query cannot get it wrong by copying the old idiom.

## 7e8c2a85 2026-08-08 semantic: gate infix at all eleven expression positions

The enumeration is the test. [GRAM-5]'s positions taking a bare `expr` are
read off the grammar — `if_stmt` and `value_if` conditions,
`ordinary_let_rhs`, `propagate_let_rhs`, `set_stmt`, `return_stmt`,
`check_stmt`, `claim_stmt`, `give_stmt`, and the `match_stmt` and
`value_match` scrutinees — and every one is a table row, so a position cannot
be missed by fixing whichever test happened to fail. `expr_stmt := call ";"`
takes a `call`, so infix is unreachable there and it is deliberately absent.

Two assertions per position. The first is that an infix there checks
completely, which is what the defect broke. The second is stronger: a position
that merely stopped failing the tree could still be skipping the operand
judgment, so each source is rewritten to disagree on its second operand and
must cite TYPE-5 at exactly that operand — the citation the `let` path already
produced, which a position that does not check the infix cannot produce. The
rewrite asserts it matched exactly one line, so a later edit to a source cannot
silently disable its negative case.

The `return` position's second site gets its own test: [OWN-14]'s returned
reborrow runs only for a borrow result, the complement of [TYPE-7]'s
own-result implicit read that the table row covers. An infix can never produce
a borrow, so it is an FN-1 rejection, and its control — the same function
returning a plain atom — cites FN-1 too.

Verified to discriminate rather than assumed: with the fix reverted and these
tests kept, exactly these three fail, each reporting
`CompilerFailure { failure: InvalidCanonicalTree }`, and the table names
`return_stmt` as the failing position. The other four infix tests are
unaffected either way.

## 0ff24272 2026-08-08 semantic: stop requiring the deleted let annotation in a requires clause

A v0.23 clause `let` carries no written mode or type, so the FN-8
semantic-subset pass must not demand either child. [FN-8] fixes the mode
itself ("each let introduces a fresh clause-local own copy value") and
[TYPE-5] derives the type from the initializer in `check_statement`, which
runs immediately after this pass.

Before this change every requires-block `let` reached
`InvalidCanonicalTree`, so the construct had no legal spelling at all:
without the annotation the checker failed internally, and with it the
source no longer parsed.

## 482c397d 2026-08-08 semantic: admit the infix spelling of a row inside a requires clause

v0.23's [FN-8] admits a clause computation written as "an ANF [GRAM-9]
call to, or infix spelling of, a non-trapping, total operation-table row
with effect `pure`", but the subset pass only recognized the call
spelling. That rejected the migrated corpus's `let permitted = x >= 0_i32;`
and, worse, let an infix condition through on its left operand alone: the
operator row and the right operand were never examined, so a trapping
operator or a `move`, borrow, or subscript operand escaped in the check
position.

Admission asks the same `CheckedIntegerOperation::traps` the ordinary
checker asks. The bare `+ - * / %` forms carry the trapping mode with no
`.trap` suffix, so the existing spelling filter cannot see them; sharing
the predicate avoids a second reading of the operator table.

## a031f9e6 2026-08-08 resolution: give each conditional branch its own lexical scope

The migration turned every Bool `match` into `if`/`else`, and two corpus
cases stopped agreeing with their manifest rows: a positive ENT-5 join case
began rejecting `TYPE-6 DeclarationCollision`, and an ENT-2 case rejected the
same way instead of citing its recorded OP-4. Neither is a migration defect.
`ScopeBuild` opened a `NestedBody` for `loop_stmt`, `region_stmt`, and `arm`
and nothing for `if_stmt` or `value_if`, so a branch `let` declared into the
enclosing block.

[GRAM-4] is why this construct is the exception: it hangs both `stmt*`
sequences off one `if_stmt` node, so a walk keyed on child productions cannot
tell a then-statement from an else-statement. The brace pairs already
recorded on the node can — the same `body_ranges` the checker's
`conditional_blocks` reads — so each block gets a scope and each statement
joins the block whose pair contains its terminal run. The condition and a
chained `else if` stay in the enclosing scope: neither is inside either pair.

Four sources, two of them controls, because the accepting halves prove
nothing alone. Sibling branches reusing a spelling now resolve, and so does a
branch binder followed by the same spelling in the enclosing block after the
`if` — both [TYPE-6] disjoint scopes. The `match`-arm spelling of the first
program, whose arms are separate productions, must reach the same answer and
does. A branch binder shadowing a *live* enclosing binder must still be
rejected, and is: per-branch scopes could easily have hidden it.

Measured: lib 308 -> 309 passed with the failing set byte-identical at 262,
