## 686b290d 2026-08-08 conformance: restate the FORM-2 layout case and derive its class by rule

The case's whole content under test is an isolated four-space indentation.
Rendering normalizes it, so the migrated file compiled cleanly where its row
demands a rejection; left unmigrated its v0.22 `let` annotation earned GRAM-4
instead. The restatement takes the migrated line and puts the indentation
back, so the file carries exactly one violation again and rejects
`CanonicalSource/Source [FORM-2]` — observed, not predicted:

  $ ./compiler/target/debug/whitefootc --emit-llvm \
      tests/conformance/cases/form2-neg-noncanonical-ws.wf
  CanonicalSource/Source [FORM-2]: CanonicalIssue { ... }
  exit=1

Its manifest row is unchanged, because FORM-2 is what the specification
assigns to what remains: "Every nonempty physical line begins with exactly two
ASCII spaces for each enclosing brace block."

The class is then closed by rule rather than by name. This case was missed
because the exclusion was a list of 20 file names, and it is not derivable
from tool behaviour: unlike the other nineteen, this file parses and renders
happily — that is precisely how it got destroyed. It IS derivable from the
manifest. Section 2 of the specification, "Canonical form", is exactly FORM-1
through FORM-7 plus the LEX-1 policy rule no case can assert, so a case whose
required verdict cites a FORM-* rule is a case about bytes, and the tool now
reads that off the manifest and keeps those files.

Measured over the 401 case files, one invocation each so the exit code is read
directly rather than through a pipe: 16 kept by the rule, 8 refused because
they do not parse, 377 already migrated and unchanged, 0 rewritten. The rule
covers all 12 FORM-family members of the old hand list, adds the one it
missed, and adds the three FORM-7 cases — which rendering does preserve, since
terminal interiors keep their bytes, but whose subject is still a literal's
spelling. Splitting the family to exclude them would be a per-rule hand list
again, which is the defect this replaces.

The reader takes only the two fields the question needs and refuses a row it
cannot read, because under-excluding is the direction that destroys a case. An
annotation row has no `id` and asserts no source; a positive row states no
rule. Two tests: the real manifest yields exactly the 16 named ids, so a
seventeenth cannot arrive unnoticed, and the four row shapes are told apart.

## 330bda0f 2026-08-08 conformance: restore each masked case's own rule, and move two citations

Nine of the ten findings the migration left. Every verdict below was observed
by running the case, never predicted, and every citation was checked against
the specification text rather than against what the compiler prints.

FIVE RESTATED, manifest row unchanged. Each lost its violation to a deleted
annotation or gained an earlier-firing one, and each concern is still
expressible, so the source moves and the recorded rule fires again:

- `x-typ-bool-cmp-result-as-int` (TYPE-5). A binder's type is now its
  initializer's, so nothing can disagree there. A `set` target's type still
  comes from a written declaration, and TYPE-5 owns it verbatim: "the
  right-hand side of `set p = e;` must produce exactly `own T` ... a different
  right-hand-side mode or type is a hard error citing TYPE-5". Committing
  `a == b` to a written `i32` field earns TYPE-5.
- `type7-neg-implicit-read` (TYPE-7). Its `let v: own i32 = p;` was the
  expectation; without the annotation `v` is simply the borrow, and what
  remained was the unreachable trailing statement FN-1 owns — an incidental
  defect, not this case's subject. A declared parameter type is still an
  expected value type, so passing the borrow to `takes(value: p)` earns TYPE-7
  with the `deref(.)` fix.
- `x-typ-match-foreign-variant` (TYPE-6). GRAM-6 now rejects a Bool-scrutinee
  `match` at the scrutinee before variant resolution runs. Same witness change
  the ERR-2 case already took: a source enum scrutinee, prelude `Some` arm,
  and TYPE-6 `ForeignMatchVariant` again.
- `op1-neg-eeq-payload-enum` (OP-1). A payload-carrying enum is affine under
  OWN-1's classification, and the deleted type argument left its operands bare,
  so OWN-1 fired first. Moving both operands lets OP-1 own the domain
  rejection it was written for.
- `form2-neg-noncanonical-ws` — landed earlier in this branch.

TWO CITATIONS MOVED, source unchanged, because the specification assigns the
rejection to a different rule than the row recorded:

- `own1-neg-match-move-through-borrow` OWN-1 -> OWN-5. OWN-5 states it
  verbatim: "Content reached through any borrow may never be moved: `move`
  requires a place rooted at an own-mode binding." OWN-1 defines when a move is
  legal and never states this prohibition. This row was wrong before the
  migration too — it is main's single red case.
- `x-match-give1-wrong-type` TYPE-5 -> GIVE-1, carrying out the recorded
  2026-08-08 amendment. Its premise was the deleted annotation; the surviving
  concern is delivery-set agreement, which the rewritten GIVE-1 owns: "a
  delivering `give` whose exact mode or type differs from an earlier delivering
  `give` of the same initializer is a hard error citing GIVE-1 at the later
  `give_stmt`". The scrutinee is a source enum so GRAM-6 forms no candidate.

TWO NEEDED NOTHING. `ent2-neg-expired-spelling-inherits-nothing` cites its
recorded OP-4 again and `ent5-pos-join-keeps-common-bound` compiles, both from
the branch-scope fix rather than from any edit here. The brief listed ent2 as a
moved citation to TYPE-6; writing that would have recorded a compiler defect
in the manifest.

ONE REFUSED. `fn2-neg-eeq-implicit-type` is unchanged and still accepts. FN-2
does retain negative content, so this is not the specification finding the
brief asked me to stop on — but reaching it is blocked by a compiler defect,
reported in the task record.

## 1dc0a4f1 2026-08-08 migrate: reach the corpus rewriter from Rust string literals

M3c needs the same transform the 400-file corpus got, applied to the
Whitefoot fixtures embedded in `compiler/src`. A second rewriter would be
the defect pattern this batch has spent the week removing, so `--rust`
extracts each literal, hands the decoded bytes to `migrate` unchanged, and
re-encodes the result in the literal form it came from.

Two gates, both load-bearing. A literal is rewritten only when the pre-pass
changed its bytes, so a fixture already in v0.23 is never re-rendered and a
deliberately non-canonical FORM-2 source is never canonicalized. And a
rewrite lands only when decoding its own re-encoding reproduces the migrated
bytes, so an escaping the module cannot round-trip is reported, not guessed.

Eight tests: every literal form located with its content, quotes inside
comments and character literals not mistaken for delimiters, a lifetime not
swallowing the literal after it, `bar` not read as the `b` prefix, escapes
decoding to the bytes a test feeds the compiler, an unmodelled escape
refusing rather than guessing, encoding round-tripping every form, and a raw
literal refusing content that spells its own terminator.

## 31cd96bf 2026-08-08 semantic: derive slice_of's region and element instead of demanding them

[TYPE-5] names the retained-argument class exactly — cvt, reinterpret,
array_new, arena_new, finf/fnan — and slice_of is not a member, so A1 deletes
its written arguments. check_slice_of still required a Targs node and cited
FN-2 when it was absent, which [DIAG-1] reserves for a user-generic call and
never for a table operation.

The fix is a deletion, not new machinery: both facts were already derived and
then merely re-checked against the written form. The region is the one the
operand's borrow writes (it was read at `borrow_region` and compared for
equality); the element is the viewed place's (read from `check_indexed_place`
and compared for equality). Removing the written arguments removes both
comparisons — each fact now has exactly one source rather than two that had
to agree.

A written argument is now the rejection rather than the supply, citing OP-1,
the same footing derivation.rs already pins for a written argument on `imin`.

Measured, with the control that distinguishes the cause:

  slice_of(&'v data)           FN-2   -> exit 0
  slice_of<'v, u8>(&'v data)   exit 0 -> OP-1
  len(data)                    exit 0 -> exit 0   (de-argumenting was never broken in general)

Library gate 537 passed / 36 failed -> 559 / 14: 22 tests cleared, zero newly
failing. The ten cost_shape tests are among them — they reach this through the
migrated tests/programs/wfgrep.wf.

The four format! templates in semantic/tests/slices.rs land here as planned,
since they could not be verified while the defect stood; every rewritten line
is the tool's own output for the assembled fixture.

One limitation, stated rather than papered over: the derived-element OP-1
branch could not be shown reachable. Four probes — a non-copy struct element,
a generic element, a nested array element, and an array_new of a struct — are
each rejected earlier by TYPE-2 or OP-1 on the array type itself, and a
control with the slice_of line deleted fails identically in every case, so no
source reaches it. The branch is kept because a source rejection is the
correct outcome if it ever is reachable, but it carries no test, and
slice_of_keeps_nonflat_element_arguments_in_the_op1_domain — whose subject was
a *written* nonflat element — is left failing and reported rather than
restated onto a violation that cannot be expressed.

## 36202d90 2026-08-08 resolution: re-scope the two family tests around the respelling

(f) Both were built from OPERATION_FAMILIES, which is now v0.23 and holds
`+wrap`, `==` and eighteen more as family spellings, so `  +wrap<i32>(1_i32);`
is not a call and the shared premise — that every family resolves through the
callee path — is false by design for twenty of the eighty-three.

Re-scoped into two properties rather than migrated or deleted:

- `every_distinct_op1_family_resolves_through_the_normal_callee_path` runs
  over the families that keep a name, and asserts the split is exactly
  83 - 20 so a family silently crossing from one half to the other cannot pass
  unnoticed. The identity check is against each family's own position in the
  inventory rather than the order it is written in, so filtering the source
  cannot make the ordinals agree by accident.
- `a_respelled_family_produces_no_lexical_use_at_all` is new, and states the
  property the respelling introduced: [OP-1] says infix resolution consults no
  name domain and an operator token is never a declaration, callee IDENT, or
  OPNAME, so these rows did not move to another name — they left the name
  domain. It carries its own control: a named row in the same function must
  produce exactly one operation use, so the two infix rows being absent is the
  property and not an empty search.
- `dotless_and_dotted_operations_resolve_by_exact_op1_spelling` keeps its
  subject — one dotted spelling and one dotless — on `ineg.trap` and `imin`,
  two rows that keep their names.

## 14975f77 2026-08-08 semantic: cite by the callee's class, not by the argument problem

[DIAG-1]: "The cited rule is the rule selected by the callee's class: [FN-2]
for a user-generic call, [SYS-2] for a system operation's region arguments,
and, for a table operation, the rule [OP-2] selects — OP-1 or TYPE-5." The
compiler selected from the *kind* of argument problem instead, so it was wrong
in both directions at once.

Measured before and after, with a correct call as the control in each class:

  pick(value: move a)        user-generic, missing     TYPE-5 -> FN-2
  pick<Held, Held>(…)        user-generic, wrong count TYPE-5 -> FN-2
  pick<Held>(value: move a)  user-generic, correct     exit 0 -> exit 0
  cvt(value)                 table op, missing         FN-2   -> TYPE-5
  cvt<i32>(value)            table op, wrong count     OP-1   -> OP-1
  array_new(0_u8)            table op, missing         FN-2   -> TYPE-5
  finf()                     table op, missing         TYPE-5 -> TYPE-5
  Pair(v: 1_i32)             construct, missing        TYPE-5 -> TYPE-5

`finf`/`fnan` were already right, and `retained_operation_type_argument`'s
doc comment already gave the reason, so the two wrong table-operation sites
are brought to the reading their sibling already carried rather than to a new
one.

The user-generic half needed the rule threaded rather than replaced.
`generic_substitution` reads one argument list for two callee classes that
[DIAG-1] assigns different rules — a user-generic call cites FN-2, a generic
nominal's construct cites TYPE-5 "at the complete construct" — so the rule now
arrives from the caller that knows its own class instead of being chosen
inside from the shape of the failure. That is the whole fix: one parameter,
two call sites, no new machinery.

Two recorded expectations move, and both were flagged in advance as witnesses
to this exact question rather than discovered convenient here:

- `operation_call_shapes_…`'s `cvt(value)` FN-2, which the round-14 record
  named as "one of the witnesses that must move if the citation question is
  settled the other way".
- `generic_argument_kinds_…`'s two wrong-kind arguments on a user-generic
  call, which recorded TYPE-5. [DIAG-1] gives a wrong-kind argument to the
  callee's class, so FN-2 is what they should always have asserted.

Neither is an expectation edited to match a moved violation: the 2026-08-08
ruling settled which rule is correct and no specification change is owed, so
these tests were encoding the defect.

New test `the_cited_rule_follows_the_callee_class_and_not_the_argument_problem`
holds one argument problem fixed across the classes so only the callee varies —
missing arguments and a wrong-count list, each on both a user generic and a
table operation — plus the generic-nominal construct as the control that the
rule is not simply keyed on the shared argument-list reader.

Measured: lib 568 passed / 6 failed -> 569 / 6, zero newly failing, the same
six remaining. clippy -D warnings and cargo fmt --check both exit 0.

NOT fixed, and reported rather than forced: [DIAG-1]'s third clause. A system
operation's region arguments must cite SYS-2, and `system.rs` cites TYPE-5,
but `SemanticRule` has no `Sys2` variant at all — adding one touches the rule
inventory and its coverage accounting, which is outside this defect's scope.
No conformance case expects a SYS-2 rejection today; SYS-2 appears only in an
accept row's rule list.

## 0cbaeb3f 2026-08-08 migrate: teach the tool the give and propagate constructor positions

Authorized 2026-08-08. [TYPE-5] mandates written prelude-constructor arguments
in every position; the tool wrote them in two — an annotated `let` and a
`return` — so constructors in a `give` or a `propagate` were left bare by the
migration and are now illegal. Fixing the two sites without teaching the tool
would leave a re-run to re-break them, which is why both land together.

The two positions differ, and only one is a copy of the existing rule.

A `give` inside a value initializer takes exactly what a directly assigned
constructor takes: the binder's annotation is the delivered type. The direct
rule never reached it only because the constructor sits inside an arm rather
than after the `=`.

A `propagate` is the one position whose arguments come from two places. For
`let x: own T = propagate Err(error: e);` inside a function returning
`Result<_, E>`, the constructor needs `Err<T, E>` — the Ok half from the
binder's annotation, the error half from the declared result. Neither source
alone is enough, which is why it is a separate rule rather than another call
to the annotation-copying one, and why `result_type` is now threaded into
`annotated_let` alongside its existing use for `return`.

Verified against the pre-migration bytes of the two real sites, which is the
input the tool should have handled the first time:

  let result: own Result<u64, u64> = match b { … give Ok(value: 1_u64); … }
    -> give Ok<u64, u64>(value: 1_u64);      migrated file compiles, exit 0
  let accepted: own i32 = propagate Err(error: error);
    -> propagate Err<i32, StepError>(error: error);   exit 0

Two tests, the second carrying its own control: the returned constructor in
the same function still takes both arguments from the signature, so the two
rules are not reading each other's source.

The two live sites are then repaired with exactly those bytes —
`x-give-result-aggregate.wf` and `semantic/tests.rs`'s propagate fixture — not
by hand-derived spellings.

Measured:

  library  570 passed / 5 failed -> 571 / 4; result_construction_… clears
  adapter  Pass=384 Fail=4 Skip=13 -> Pass=385 Fail=3 Skip=13
  coverage 128/128 rules, 0 uncovered
  tool     31 tests pass

Nothing newly failing. The four remaining library failures are the two
activation-gated spec checks and the two capability gaps; the three remaining
adapter failures are `own3-pos-outlives-store`, `own5-neg-slice-value-match`
and `fn8-neg-requires-eeq-payload-enum`.

## 4c3de719 2026-08-08 semantic: judge OWN-5's slice-valued delivery before the branch join

Authorized 2026-08-08 as an ordering change. [OWN-5]'s prohibition on a
slice-valued delivery was judged in check_let, one step after the branch-state
join that runs inside check_match and check_if. join_states stops with
Unsupported { OwnershipJoin } whenever two branches leave their bindings in
states differing by more than region claims — which is exactly what a
slice-valued join looks like when it is written on purpose — so a capability
stop stood in front of a source rejection.

The discriminator, holding everything fixed but the join:

  both branches move the SAME binding      OWN-5      -> OWN-5
  branches move DIFFERENT bindings         Unsupported -> OWN-5

The rejection moves to the delivery site and keeps one home: the later copy in
check_let is deleted rather than duplicated, so the rule is judged once.

One consequence beyond the reported case, stated rather than left to be found:
a slice delivery in borrow mode previously reached the RegionsAndBorrows
capability stop first and now reaches OWN-5, because the prohibition holds
whatever the mode. That is the same masking removed in the same place.

ACCEPTANCE IS UNCHANGED, which the ruling required be verified rather than
argued. This converts Unsupported into a rejection and never Accept into
anything: measured over all 401 corpus cases with the parent binary and this
one, no case that compiled before fails now.

  library  571 passed / 4 failed -> 572 / 3
  adapter  Pass=385 Fail=2 Skip=13 -> Pass=386 Fail=2 Skip=13

## 31941c65 2026-08-08 docs: record round 20 — SYS-2, and what the coverage metric counts

The measurement the task cared about: covered = tagged | annotated, where
tagged is every rule merely NAMED in some case's rules list. So a rule counts
as covered without any case whose expected verdict cites it, and with no
notion of separate content pieces. 83 of 128 have no negative case at all; 19
have neither a positive exercise nor a negative citation.

The packet-usable form: a negative case fails if a rule stops rejecting, so
for those 83 a rule that silently stopped rejecting would not be caught. With
the fair qualification that many of the 83 have no negative FORM — grammar
productions, diagnostic-shape rules — so the claim is about what the metric
asserts, not that 83 rules are unguarded.

SYS-2 itself: rank fixed at 38 by the specification's definition order rather
than chosen, citation moved at the three argument-list sites, and a first
negative case with its control.

Also reports one thing found in passing: SemanticRule::Gram6 has a rank but is
absent from the rank test's ALL array, so its rank is unverified while every
other variant's is checked.

## eef0c463 2026-08-08 semantic: walk the enum for the rank check instead of listing it

Part 1, the finding-bearing half: `Gram6` is added to the checked set and
**the check passes**. Its rank was correct all along, so the omission was
benign for this instance — but the hole was real, and a check that reports
every rule verified while one is not is worse for that rule than no check.

Part 2 makes the omission structurally impossible rather than fixing the one
instance. The set under check is now walked from the enum through
`next_in_definition_order`, an exhaustive match, rather than read from a
hand-maintained array. There are now two exhaustive matches over the rules —
that one and `definition_rank` — and the test makes them check each other:
walking the chain must yield the ranks 0, 1, 2, … in order. A new variant
therefore does not compile until it appears in both, and appearing in both is
exactly what being checked means.

`definition_rank` is unchanged and stays `pub const fn`, because it is used in
const assertions in borrows.rs and control/results.rs. The chain is a second
ordered source rather than a replacement for that reason.

Measured both ways rather than assumed, since a check that cannot fail is the
thing this slice exists to remove:

  Sys2's rank changed 38 -> 7   test fails: "SYS-2 sits at chain position 38
                                but ranks 7"
  Sys2 dropped from the chain   COMPILE ERROR: non-exhaustive patterns,
                                `SemanticRule::Sys2` not covered

The second is the guarantee that was asked for, in the compiler's own words.

`FIRST` and `next_in_definition_order` are `#[cfg(test)]`: their only purpose
is to make a check's set complete, and without the gate `-D warnings` fails
the production build on dead code. The compiler's demand therefore arrives
when the tests compile, which is inside `make check` — the gate that would
catch a new variant either way.

  library  572 passed / 3 failed, unchanged; the same three
  coverage 128/128 rules, 0 uncovered

## a8f0ee82 2026-08-08 migrate: comparisons keep their names, and un-spell the ones already infix

Two changes to the one rewriter, plus the candidate's new digest.

INFIX_RESPELL loses ieq/ine/ile/ige and DEARGUMENTED gains all six
comparisons, so the v0.22 -> v0.23 direction now produces ieq(a, b)
rather than a == b. That direction stays live for the frozen corpora
that reconcile at promotion.

COMPARISON_UNSPELL is the reverse class, and it exists only because the
corpus was already migrated to the spelling the owner cancelled. It is
reached from the same pre-pass as every other class, so the .wf corpus
and the fixtures embedded in Rust literals share one implementation.
Unlike every other class it has no callee token to key on, so the
operator is the anchor and both operands are recovered by walking the
atom forms GRAM-9 admits -- place suffixes, a deref group, move, and a
borrow prefix. A statement keyword is not one of those forms, which is
the boundary a keyword blacklist would have got wrong and which is
asserted in check, if, and return position.

The operator is matched on its bytes rather than on one token kind, so
the class survives the lexer reverting: == <= >= then arrive as two
byte-adjacent punctuation tokens, and FORM-2's mandatory spacing is
what makes that reading unambiguous.

## 310beaa0 2026-08-08 conformance: cover FN-8's move prohibition, which had no negative

FN-8 names "User-function calls, construction, move, borrowing,
subscripting, mutation, control flow, allocation, and any trapping
operation". Of those, the corpus had negatives for user calls, mutation,
control flow, and trapping operations. `move` had none.

The case is a one-token differential and the control is the point: the
same clause with `ieq(left, right)` COMPILES (measured, exit 0), and
with `ieq(move left, move right)` rejects FN-8 InvalidRequires. The
operation, the domain, and the clause shape are all legal, so the moved
operand is provably the sole violation rather than the one that happened
to fire first.

Deliberately a copy type. The move rejection is type-independent --
`own u32` operands reject identically -- so using a payload-carrying
enum here would entangle this with the affinity question and leave the
enum decorative.

Addition only: no existing case, row, or verdict is touched.

## 83b95eca 2026-08-08 conformance: add the declared-verdict diff, the one thing nothing watched

Ruled at 2a16530, corrected at 0027e8e after measurement showed the
re-run version was the conformance adapter and would have caught
neither case it was justified by.

The adapter compares each case's ACTUAL verdict against its DECLARED
one, so a verdict that moves while its manifest row is edited to follow
leaves it green. CLAUDE.md names that a governance breach precisely
because nothing mechanical stops it. This compares the declared
verdicts themselves across a revision range: no compiler invocation, no
case execution, no knowledge of any case's subject.

`runner.py verdicts <revision>`. It lives beside the coverage check
rather than in the compiler because it reads the corpus, not the
language, which is the boundary this file already draws. It is NOT
wired into `make check`: a legitimate restatement makes it red, and a
mechanism for letting a red gate pass is exactly what this project
forbids. It is an operator check for migration and review time, read
against governance/APPROVALS.md.

First run, vs the batch base 8df0e29: one moved and one removed. Both
already known -- the move is authorized at APPROVALS.md:517, and the
removal is the one the lead disclosed by conscience earlier today. A
first run that is quiet except for items a reader can confirm is what
makes a later hit worth reading.

Its limit is on the function and asserted by a test rather than only
documented: it cannot see an emptied case. A positive whose subject was
deleted still declares, and still reaches, the verdict it always did.
A verdict is the wrong instrument for a question about subjects.

Four tests, and one of them nearly did not run: appended after the
`__main__` guard they were never collected, and the suite still said
OK. The count moving 18 -> 22 is what caught it.

## 3d7fcca3 2026-08-08 conformance: name all three migration-damage classes on the check itself

The ruling's refinement: describe the check by the class it catches, not
by the cases that prompted it. "The migration damaged a case" is three
classes and this owns exactly one, so all three are now on the function
where a reader meets it.

(A) a negative whose violation was a construct the migration deletes --
it then compiles where its row demands a rejection, so the ADAPTER
already catches it and always did. (B) a positive whose subject was
deleted -- it keeps passing, its verdict never moves, and nothing
verdict-based reaches it. (C) a declared verdict moving with its row
following -- this check.

Stated because the dangerous reading is the one a green run invites:
"the migration broke nothing" is wrong in (B)'s direction, and (B) is
the direction that has actually cost this project cases.

## b353a1d7 2026-08-08 spec: name A3's removed region-annotation form, and say what is not known

The last candidate change before byte approval. Two prose edits, plus
the delta kept in step and the digest re-pinned.

TYPE-5's premise gains a clause. As written it says a binder's mode and
type are exactly what its right-hand side produces, and that is false at
one v0.22 form: a body `let` could annotate a borrow with a region its
right-hand side did not name, stating a DESTINATION the right-hand side
satisfies by outlives rather than equals. A derived type is always the
region the right-hand side itself produces, so the form is removed
rather than reconstructed. A reviewer checking the premise would have
found the counterexample; now the premise states its own limit.

The accepted-set accounting names it, and deliberately does NOT call it
a fourth narrowing. Whether any program is thereby rejected is not
established -- a borrow at an enclosing region satisfies an inner
destination by the same outlives judgment, so the equivalent program
may always be writable, and nobody has shown a program v0.22 accepts
and v0.23 rejects for this reason. Naming a form that turns out not to
be a narrowing costs a sentence; failing to name a real one is the
class this batch spent a day finding.

Measured at one site corpus-wide: 1954 annotated bindings, 68 naming a
region, 1 naming a region its right-hand side does not.

Figures, verified rather than assumed:

The section said a check for further unnamed citation moves was owed
before approval. That check cannot be run: a full audit asks, for every
pair of edited rules that can co-fire, whether the cited rule moved,
and there is no corpus to diff against because the corpus itself was
migrated. An obligation that cannot be discharged should become a
stated limit, since an open one in an approval packet reads as work
someone will do.

FOUR citations moved and were disposed: own1-neg-match-move-through-
borrow OWN-1 -> OWN-5, x-match-give1-wrong-type TYPE-5 -> GIVE-1,
type5-neg-wrong-region-arg-count TYPE-5 -> FN-2, and the region-bearing
buffer element STOR-5 -> OP-1, which has no manifest row and is the
reason the section existed. Two of the four were wrong BEFORE this
batch and independently of it, which is worth separating: a batch that
moves citations and a batch that reveals wrong ones look identical from
outside.

Eight more had the compiler cite a different rule and were disposed by
restating the SOURCE so the recorded rule fires again -- following the
compiler would have deleted their coverage silently -- and one
apparent move was refused because its cause was a compiler defect.

THE MECHANISM IS THE LIMIT: a citation move is observable exactly where
some case asserts the rule that moved. 83 of 128 rules have no negative
citing them, so a move into or out of any of those is invisible here.
Four is a floor, complete over the population that could speak.

Raising it needs a negative for each of the 83, or a corpus compilable
by both versions -- and none exists, since tests/codegen is frozen at
v0.22 and cannot compile under v0.23 without the migration that would
destroy the comparison.

Packet text only. The candidate is untouched and still hashes to

## 3eded456 2026-08-08 mcts: record v0.23's three surface-form re-decisions

The tree said v0.22 after the activation landed. It should have moved in
a01bc707 with the code; it did not, because I missed it and no gate
watches the tree. One commit late is still divergence, and it is stated
here rather than covered.

Three re-decisions, each with paired Moves whose why is verbatim on both
sides:

- [[match-form]] replaces [[match-only-conditional]]. A Bool scrutinee's
  two arm labels are always True() and False() in fixed order, so the
  arm ceremony carried no information the condition did not.
- [[operation-spelling]] replaces [[prefix-table-calls]], promoted to a
  child node first so the rejected form has a home. Retained
  three-address form admits one operation per expression, so infix costs
  no precedence surface and no lookahead.
- [[binding-annotation]] replaces [[written-mode-and-type]], likewise
  promoted. A body binder's mode and type are uniquely reconstructed
  from its right-hand side.

TWO PROMOTIONS RATHER THAN ONE NODE MOVE. The brief said the superseded
form moves to surface-form.alt/, which would freeze three Items that are
still true. What was re-decided is two internal aspects of that node, so
the skill's promotion rule applies: each aspect became a child whose
.alt/ holds its rejected form, and the parent's Items now name the
children instead of asserting what they own.

ITEM 5 IS NOT FALSE and was left alone. The brief listed Items 3, 4 and
5; Bool as a prelude enum and decimal-only literals with mandatory
suffixes are untouched by v0.23, and the installed spec still says both
verbatim. Checked rather than accepted.

The two pitfall facts land on [[match-form]], which now owns the
conditional: the grammar hangs BOTH statement sequences off one node
unlike loop, region and arm, so a pass enumerating bodies by child
production skips both branches -- which cost a scope defect and an
only-child read of the one expression alternative with two children,
one cause and two symptoms.

`npx mcts-mem lint` exit 0, read directly: 75 nodes. It caught five
violations of mine first -- four rationale facts restating a move's why,
and an item carrying a because-tail -- all fixed rather than worked
around.

## 9a658703 2026-08-16 spec: one sentence per line (Stage 1, commit 2 of 5)

Candidate bytes; no approval is claimed or recorded by this commit.
Reflows every rule body, prose paragraph, and bullet outside fenced
blocks and markdown tables to one sentence per line, per the adopted
profile (research/investigations/spec-representation/DOSSIER.md 3(b)
item 2). 1,277 -> 3,080 lines; 384,140 -> 384,140 bytes, because every
split replaces the space after a sentence-ending period with a newline.

Content preservation is proved, not asserted. compiler/src/bin/
stage1_verify.rs (one-shot, deleted in the final commit of this
migration) normalizes both files by joining every non-fenced line into
one stream and collapsing whitespace runs, then byte-compares. Verdict
against the pre-reflow bytes: normalized old 383,102 bytes, normalized
new 383,102 bytes, identical, with ZERO enumerated insertions. It also
re-derives the structure independently of the gate: 133 rule
definitions, no duplicates, 133 distinct references, none unresolved.

Two deliberate departures from a naive reflow, both recorded because
they are the only places where mechanical splitting would have changed
content or broken a consumer:

1. The rule id keeps its first sentence on the id line
   (`[OP-4] A subscript ...`) instead of standing alone. Five active
   compiler tests anchor on rule id plus prose and would fail closed
   otherwise: bin/grammar.rs:485 and :499 (FORM-4, FORM-6 fixtures),
   resolution/catalog.rs:1219 and :1452 (SYS-2, PRE-1 extraction
   locks), and tests/canonical_corpus.rs:304 (EX-1 anchor). Those files
   are outside this task's edit scope, and weakening a test to fit a
   formatting choice is not available. Every line-start `^[ID]` anchor,
   the rule scanner, and runner.py's regex behave identically either
   way.
2. Five sentences that open with a bracketed reference stay joined to
   the preceding sentence rather than being reworded to "Per [X], ...":
   [FN-2], [GIVE-1], [FORM-2], [DIAG-1], [SCOPE-2]. Each is a subject-
   position reference ("[FN-2] separately rejects ..."), so the rewrap
   would produce broken English, and rewording normative text is not
   part of a mechanical migration. A body line starting with `[` would
   also register as a duplicate rule definition in bin/spec.rs.

Sentence splitting is conservative: only a period followed by one space
outside a backtick code span, where the next character opens a new
sentence, and never after a known abbreviation. Colons are left in
place; a colon that ends a sentence already ends its line. Verified
that no split falls inside an open double quote or an open parenthesis.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The specification's data payloads become fenced blocks with `wf-` info
strings, and the grammar extractor keys on those info strings instead of
prose anchors (DOSSIER 3(b) item 4, and the trap its own doc comment
confessed: "scraping only fenced blocks silently loses those four").

Spec side, 33 inserted and 7 deleted lines in total:

  strings; their bodies are untouched;
- the four productions that lived inline in prose move into their own
  `wf-ebnf` fences beside their rules, byte-identical after the `:=`,
  with the prose keeping a one-line pointer. The three rewritten
  sentences are CONST-1 ("The grammar production `const := ...` is
  usable" -> "The grammar production `const` of the fence below is
  usable"), CONST-2 ("with `cvalue := ...`" -> "with the `cvalue`
  production of the fence below"), and EFF-1 ("Row grammar: `effects
  := ...` with `effect := ...`" -> "Row grammar: the `effects` and
  `effect` productions of the fence below"). No other prose changes;

  cell changed: OP-1's operation table (`wf-ops`), SYS-2's component
  class table (`wf-prov`), and the SYS-4, SYS-5 and SYS-6 tables
  (`wf-sys`). Each table's existing header row is its column schema and

are replaced by one `ebnf_blocks` scan over `wf-ebnf` fence info
strings; the seven-fence, seventy-three-production assertion replaces

THE PROOF that only the housing moved: the regenerated tables are

## 196ce0f9 2026-08-16 GATE-WIRING CANDIDATE (P1, awaiting owner approval): recognize declared specification candidates in the identity gates

A stable file whose status line reads
`Status: CANDIDATE vM supersedes vN <sha256-of-vN>` now passes the identity
gates exactly when (a) every self-consistency check holds (rule references,
ledger rows, status markers, title/status agreement, compiled-version
agreement), (b) the declared supersedes digest equals the activation chain
tail in governance/APPROVALS.md, and (c) vM is the tail's successor. A

## 4d4195c2 2026-08-17 backend: preserve exact UTF-8 bytes in DIAG-3 record fields

json_string iterated bytes and mapped each through char::from, which
reinterprets a UTF-8 continuation byte as the Latin-1 scalar of the same
value and re-encodes it. Every non-ASCII byte in a trap message was
therefore doubled: "é" left the encoder as 4 bytes, "日" as 6. ASCII was
unaffected, which is why no existing record test saw it.

Iterating scalar values fixes it: pushing a char writes its complete
UTF-8 encoding, so a multi-byte scalar survives intact and no record can
end inside an encoding. The record's length and its \XX LLVM escaping
were already byte-exact and are untouched.

The defect is latent today because FORM-5 still admits no non-ASCII byte
in a STRING, so the regression exercises trap_record directly rather
than through a source program. It asserts exact bytes, not a length: a
length check passes on mojibake of the right size.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 89596d65 2026-08-17 compiler: reject polymorphic recursion under FN-6

FN-6 permits recursion and rejects polymorphic recursion by a syntactic
rule: in any call cycle among generic functions, every call must
instantiate the callee at exactly the caller's own type parameters. The
checker had no FN-6 judgment at all and reported every generic call cycle
as an unimplemented capability, so a program the language rejects was
misreported as a compiler gap.

The cycle judgment now asks the source rule first. An edge is judged when
its caller and callee are both generic and the callee reaches the caller
again; the written `targs` must be the caller's own type parameters, in
order, as bare TYPEIDs resolving to those declarations. A violation is a
FN-6 rejection at the offending call carrying the cycle and the
restructuring the rule requires the diagnostic to name.

A cycle FN-6 permits, and a cycle through a nongeneric participant (whose
written arguments are fixed, so its instance set is finite), both keep the
existing explicit unsupported report rather than becoming rejections.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## c53f1372 2026-08-17 compiler: pin OP-3 strict addition against reassociation

The float suite already asserted that no `fast` flag reaches the emitted
module, which is a claim about the module rather than about the program that
runs. This adds an executed witness at the same optimization level every
Whitefoot executable links with: an addition that is not associative in
binary32, where stepwise and regrouped evaluation must disagree.

Verified discriminating: inverting the comparison to `feq` makes the program
trap at OP-5 and the test fail, so a run that reassociated, contracted, or
widened the additions would be caught rather than passing silently.

No compiler behavior changes; fadd.strict already lowered correctly.

## e1b23329 2026-08-17 semantic: lock every wf-ops column against the compiler's own decisions

Only the op column was extraction-locked. domain, signature, and effects
were re-encoded by hand in semantic::model, and the measured cost of that
one-sided mirror was sixteen unreachable match arms in calls.rs naming
spellings the table had stopped containing.

Four locks close it, keyed on the ```wf-ops fence info string rather than
a prose anchor:

- effects decides traps(), for all forty-five integer rows plus the
  float and Bool rows; a trapping-row count keeps the loop from passing
  on an empty extraction.
- signature decides operand_count(), argument_type(), and the result:
  scalar rows against scalar_result_type(), Result rows against a
  scalar_result_type() of None plus the error type's own spelling.
- domain decides accepts_operand_type(), sampled at the boundary each
  token draws rather than swept.
- the modelled spelling set equals the table's, so a new compiler
  operation must name its row and a row nothing claims fails.

checked_error moves from an inline match in calls.rs onto the operation
so one place decides it and the lock can read it; the variant-to-spelling
maps are exhaustive matches, so a new variant is a compile error.

## 699c7ec0 2026-08-17 semantic: lock the ENT-3 source envelope against FlowEventKind and ProofView

v0.30 gave the twelve L0 fact sources real sub-rule ids and a machine
readable retired: key. Nothing read them, so the ids were addressable but
not load-bearing.

Three locks make them load-bearing: the defined [ENT-3.Sk] set equals the
compiler's Sk flow events, with S12 the one deliberate exception because
FN-9 publishes it through the postcondition group; a retired label is
neither redefined as a sub-rule nor modelled by any event; and FN-1's
complete/unasserted/S4-blinded vocabulary equals ProofView, with the two
view sentences partitioning every flow source between removed and
retained.

so a new event kind or view cannot be added without deciding where it
belongs. The behavioural half of the unasserted split is already gated by

and is not duplicated here.

## c44fdfeb 2026-08-17 compiler: execute region-confined arenas and judge STOR-4 confinement

Implements the arena cluster end to end: `arena_new<'r, T>` allocates
content onto the owning region's compiler-owned allocation list, `deref`
reads it, and every normal edge leaving the region block releases the
whole list [STOR-2, STOR-3]. STOR-4 confinement is judged at the two
destinations that would carry the value out of `'r`'s block — a callable
result type (top-level and contract member) and a value delivery whose
destination binding lies outside the block.

The region owns its list, so `arena_new` selects it by resolved region
rather than by the nearest enclosing block: an allocation naming an
enclosing region survives the inner region's exit and is freed only by
the outer one. Loop re-entry resets the cell, so a re-entered region
starts empty.

Two temporary capability stops keep unimplemented arena runtime out of
lowering instead of miscompiling it: arena-typed parameters, and views
formed over a local arena's content. Both are judged after the source
rejections they must not mask, which is what lets the FN-1 return-origin
verdict reach a view over an arena parameter.

Missing `main` is now reported after per-declaration source rejections.
DIAG-1 leaves the order among rejection events at distinct nodes
implementation-defined, and a declaration's own established violation is
the more useful report. Verified against the base compiler: none of the
eleven main-less conformance cases changes its reported rule.

Evidence, with the manifest and conformance cases untouched:
- stor4-pos-arena-confined compiles and runs, exit 0
- stor4-neg-arena-escape rejects citing STOR-4
- fn1-neg-returned-slice-arena-origin rejects citing FN-1
- stor5-neg-arena-new-region-bearing still rejects citing STOR-5

Gate profile green: 902 lib tests and every target suite, 0 failed.

## 21434167 2026-08-17 PROTECTED CANDIDATE (awaiting owner batch approval): migrate 14 cases to the v0.31 arithmetic rule

The v0.31 arithmetic-mode dissolution attaches an overflow obligation to the
bare `+`, `-`, `*` constant-operand class and removes those sites' `traps`
contribution. That narrows acceptance for 14 existing cases: 9 rejected
citing OP-2 with an undischarged residual, 5 citing EFF-2 because a row's
only trap contributor was a dissolved class site. No `expect` moves; every
case keeps its declared verdict. Only sources change.

The migration is split by what each case EXISTS to show, because the two
halves need opposite treatment.

(a) Cases whose subject IS the trap keep it, via the retained two-non-constant
form. A bare site with two non-constant operand atoms is outside the class,
attaches no obligation, keeps trapping semantics, and keeps contributing
`traps`. Binding the literal to a term is not evasion here: it is the exact
form the rule retains, and dissolving these sites would delete the behavior
the case was written to pin.

  err4-pos-contract-trap                       `peak + step`   (still traps)
  x-form-form7-overflow-trap-canonical         `a + one`       (still traps)
  x-arith-loop-imul-trap-folds-overflow-traps  `acc * factor`  (still traps)
  eff2-pos-propagate-declared-trap             `x + step`      (row keeps traps)

(b) Cases whose subject is NOT arithmetic discharge the obligation instead,
so they exercise the new rule rather than dodging it. Two routes, both named
by the delta as mechanical fixes:

  dominating branch (the guard was already nearly right, and in both
  recursion cases the old `ieq` guard also left negative inputs recursing
  forever, which the new obligation is what exposed):
    fn6-pos-recursion           `ieq(n,0)` -> `ile(n,0)`; row keeps traps
                                because the two-variable `n + r` remains
    x-fn-mutual-recursion-runs  same in both functions; both rows drop
                                `traps` to `pure`, their only contributor
                                having been the now-discharged class site

  dominating claim of the exact residual the diagnostic renders (a claim
  carries its own runtime check, so these rows keep `traps`):
    fn5-pos-match-dispatch       x <= 2147483646, -2147483647 <= x
    prog1-pos-closed-unit        x <= 2147483646
    x-struct-set-field           c.n <= 2147483646
    x-enum-payload-give          v <= 2147483612
    x-enum-stmt-payload-check    v <= 1073741823, -1073741824 <= v
    x-enum-borrow-payload-live   deref(x) <= 2147483646, and both conjuncts
                                 for the multiply
    x-enum-multiwidth-dispatch   n <= 2147483646
    x-borrowed-pool-tree-run     parent, left_child, children upper bounds

A multiply's obligation normalizes to two conjuncts, so a `* 2` site needs
both the upper and the lower claim; claiming only the upper leaves the lower
residual, which is how the two multiply cases above ended up with a pair.

Verified: every one of the 14 reaches its unchanged declared verdict through
whitefootc at this tip.

## ba69dfdb 2026-08-17 fix: judge arena and box content borrows as ordinary borrows

`check_borrow` dispatched every deref-rooted borrow to `check_child_reborrow`
on the `deref` spelling alone. `resolve_dereference_holder` then demanded a
borrow holder and cited TYPE-7 `MissingDereference` when the root had none.

[OWN-14] defines a reborrow form by its root binding's *mode*: a `borrow_expr`
whose place is rooted at a binding of borrow mode. A `let`-bound `arena_new` or
`box_new` result is own mode, so `&uniq 'r deref(a)` over it is an ordinary
borrow, not a reborrow. Spec-legal programs were rejected citing OWN-6, OWN-14,
or TYPE-7 — a compiler capability gap misreported as invalid source.

The dispatch now routes a deref rooted at an own-mode `box` or `arena` binding

capability gate — ArenaRuntime for arena, RegionsAndBorrows for box — the same

unlowerable checked program.

it is fixed here in the same motion because it is the same dispatch.

## 29dab6d6 2026-08-17 fix: judge box and arena content set targets as own-rooted targets

`check_dereferenced_set_target` resolved a borrow holder for every `deref`
mutation target. `resolve_dereference_holder` then demanded one and cited
TYPE-7 `MissingDereference` — "deref requires a borrow holder" — when the
root had none.

[SET-1] makes a `deref` target writable through either of two roots: an
explicit `deref` of a live usable `&uniq` holder, or a live own-mode value
binding whose storage is box-owned or arena-owned [STOR-1]. Only the first
has a holder. A `let`-bound `box_new` or `arena_new` result is own mode, so
`set deref(b) = 7_i32` over it is the second root, and spec-legal targets
were rejected as TYPE-7 — a compiler capability gap misreported as invalid
source. This is the mutation-target twin of the borrow-dispatch defect fixed
in ba69dfdb, reached through the same `deref`-spelling assumption; both were
pre-existing on main.

The dispatch now routes a `deref` target rooted at an own-mode `box` or
`arena` binding to the ordinary own-rooted judgment, reusing that fix's root
resolver: [OWN-1]'s liveness, the written suffix chain against the content
type, [OWN-5]'s loan state over the owning root plus the selected field path
— the same place the read path resolves for a `deref` of this binding — and
then the final selected type's class, [STOR-1] for `set` and [SET-2] for
`replace`. Past the judgment nothing stores into owned indirection content:
the target names the root binding, which lowers to the content pointer under
the box's own IR type, and arena storage has no runtime. Lowering such a
target would store the value into the pointer slot, so the target stops at
an explicit capability gate — ArenaRuntime for arena, RegionsAndBorrows for
box — rather than publishing an unlowerable checked program.

Genuinely illegal shapes keep their real rules: a `deref` of a scalar local
still cites TYPE-7, and a shared holder's referent still cites OWN-5.

Regressions cover both probe shapes reaching their explicit stops, the
affine-content `replace` target reaching the box stop, and the source
rejections the routed target still makes — STOR-1 for an affine `set` target
and OWN-1 for a dead root.

## e9037cf1 2026-08-18 programs: add the byte-string layer over the growable buffer

One real .wf program over the v0.31 collection layer: a ByteString of
buffer<u8> plus fill, built from const literal arrays, appended and
concatenated by buffer growth ([SET-2] affine replace of the superseded
buffer), measured, read through a bounds-safe Option<u8> accessor,
searched by a naive substring scan, and formatted to decimal — ending in
one real publication of exactly `length=43 brown=10 cat=none\n` to
standard output.

The read side (bs_len, bs_byte, bs_find) is `deny_claims`: the accessor
discharges its bounds obligation by a value branch rather than an
assertion, so the whole search path is proved. Two negative directions
derived from the same program bytes pin that both constructs are
load-bearing — deleting the capacity branch is an [OP-4] rejection with
residual `index < len(deref(s).buf)`, and injecting one provable claim
into the strict search is a [CLM-3] rejection at the claim node.

`compile_rejection` is the negative-direction counterpart of
`compile_sources`: it returns the compiler's own rendered diagnostic so a
case can pin the rule and the residual instead of panicking.

## d501b362 2026-08-18 research: record the wfgrep traversal system-surface gap

Reconnaissance for batch 0071 W1: what the landed wfgrep receives and
emits today, the complete v0.31 [SYS-2] inventory it draws on, and a gap
table of eleven capabilities a real recursive traversal needs against
what v0.31 declares.

The verdict is negative and stated plainly: real recursive directory
traversal is not expressible in v0.31. No operation returns a second
`DirectoryRead`, nothing enumerates a directory, and `RelativePath` can
only be built from a command argument because [HOST-3] fixes host-string
backing as the command-lifetime argument snapshot. What exists today is
harness-simulated traversal — an outside walker supplies the file list on
argv — which the frozen wfgrep-baseline protocol already labels "no
traversal". Calling it recursive search would be a false claim.

The design sketch is grounded in what is already in tree: the command
bootstrap already opens the working directory with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY
and `emit_open_read` already emits openat plus a cold errno mapper, so a
child-directory open reuses both. Delivering entry names by an [SYS-8]
transfer into a caller-owned buffer, and never forming a path value,
keeps [HOST-3], [PATH-1], and [QUAL-2] untouched.

No declaration is proposed or added; every gap is a specification surface
for the lead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 0d253937 2026-08-18 research: complete the traversal recon against the SYS-10..SYS-13 contracts

## fc4c8887 2026-08-18 feat: judge the divisor-class division obligation behind a default-off switch

Implements the v0.32-candidate division dissolution [OP-2, ENT-6] behind
DIVISION_OBLIGATIONS, false under active v0.31 so the shipped judgment is
byte-identical.

With the switch on, a bare / or % whose selected type is unsigned or whose
dividend or divisor reads as an ENT-2 constant is a divisor-class site: one
shared classifier drops its TrapSite and traps contribution, the flow
attaches a two-conjunct obligation — the zero-divisor disequality at ordinal
zero and the signed-overflow conjunct at ordinal one — and judges it in the
complete, unasserted, and S4-blinded views. Undischarged sites reject citing
OP-2 with the exact residual; strict components re-judge in U. A signed site
with two non-constant operands stays outside the class and keeps its
complete trap, because its safe condition is a disjunction the ENT-4 closure
cannot state.

The backend emits the plain udiv/sdiv/urem/srem for a trap-free class site.
BoundsRequest gains a `distinct` cell because the new family's normalized
conjunct is a disequality rather than a difference bound, and the claim
ledger records a division-supporting claim use as NotApplicable exactly as
it already does for the overflow family, since neither forms a protected
leaf.

and a constant divisor; rejection with the exact residual for an
unconstrained divisor, a constant zero divisor, and an unbounded dividend
over -1; the remainder row; the retained signed two-variable class and its
EFF-2 row; /checked untouched; two default-switch controls; and backend
evidence that the discharged site loses its guard while the retained one
keeps all three.

## bfb8ce89 2026-08-18 compiler: add the v0.32-candidate directory traversal surface

Batch 0071 W1. New default-off switch TRAVERSAL_SURFACE admits the
[SYS-14] enumeration surface the recon report found missing in v0.31:
one opaque nominal DirectoryList, one outcome enum ListOutcome with
ListBytes/ListEnd/ListFailed, and three operations open_directory,
open_list, list_once. Off, the inventory is v0.31 byte for byte.

list_once is an [SYS-8] one-attempt transfer rather than an iterator:
the target's own facility writes its native records into the caller's
validated range and the shim rewrites them in place as the portable
[kind][name length][name bytes] form. A portable header is smaller than
any native one, so the rewrite only moves bytes toward the front and
overwrites no unread byte, the handle needs no window of its own (it is
one descriptor, like ReadFile), and one call reaches one host call as
[QUAL-3] requires. Names travel as bytes at the open sites too, so no
path value is ever formed and [HOST-3], [PATH-1], and [QUAL-2] are
untouched.

Darwin binds __getdirentries64, measured on the build host: getdirentries
does not link with 64-bit inodes and opendir/readdir is two calls with an
allocation. Linux is deliberately unmapped — getdents64 has a different
arity and layout and nothing here can exercise it — so a Linux build
fails qualification for the two enumeration IDs rather than promising a
transcribed row.

tests/programs/dir_walk.wf walks a real fixture tree recursively,
collects each entry's kind and relative path into the growable
byte-string layer, and publishes a sorted listing; every bound derived
from an enumeration record is discharged by a real value branch, because
[PRV-3] refuses a claim about external data. Nine cases in
compiler/tests/programs/traversal.rs pin both directions.

The exact delta text, the portability note, and the PROPOSED conformance
case list are in research/investigations/wfgrep-traversal/SPEC-DELTA.md.
No spec, conformance, governance, roadmap, or plan byte changes here.

disposition in research/investigations/check-dissolution/conformance-inventory.md
to the 11 cases the inventory marks `subject` and the 6 it marks

1936cd2ed3dd2f237b7ef80c200bd5549a3c538c93b9e39301b35199b30cad5a) are the
sole normative authority; every verdict below is reproduced against the
real toolchain, not asserted.

DECISION ROWS (old verdict -> new verdict), 17 cases:

  op5-pos-check-pass                            run 0     -> run 0
  op5-neg-check-fails                           trap      -> trap
  trap-op5-check-fails                          trap      -> trap
  scope4-pos-check-traps                        trap      -> trap
  x-arith-check-catches-wrapped-overflow-traps  trap      -> trap
  prv3-neg-external-check                       reject PRV-3 -> reject PRV-3
  ent3-pos-band-check-decomposition             run 0     -> run 0
  clm3-pos-transitive-value-branch              run 0     -> run 0
  clm3-neg-body-check-bounds                    reject OP-4  -> reject CLM-3
  clm3-neg-body-check-requires                  reject FN-8  -> reject CLM-3
  clm3-neg-transitive-check-summary             reject OP-4  -> reject CLM-3
  clm1-trap-runtime-violation                   trap      -> trap
  eff4-pos-trap-aborts                          trap      -> trap
  err4-pos-contract-trap                        trap      -> trap
  x-arith-loop-imul-trap-folds-overflow-traps   trap      -> trap
  x-integ-loop-product-overflow-traps           trap      -> trap
  x-arith-idiv-trap-zero-divisor-traps          trap      -> (flips in slice 3)

Three verdicts change, all under CLM-3. Fourteen are preserved.

WHY THE THREE CLM-3 FLIPS. v0.32 fixes the unasserted state U as the
ordinary flow "recomputed with S3 establishment disabled" and "removes
exactly S3 claim establishment". With S2 retired, a strict closure that
contains no claim therefore has U identical to its complete state, so no
protected obligation or call goal can discharge in complete and fail in U.
The strict OP-4/FN-8 rejection these three cases pinned is reachable only
through a claim, and CLM-3 judges the claim event first ("a nonempty
DirectClaims set in its own SCC rejects at the least direct claim node";
"claim import is tested before a strict FN-8 judgment at the same call").
Each case therefore now pins that ordering, which no other case pins:
bounds pins direct claim before strict OP-4, requires pins direct claim
before strict FN-8, transitive pins the imported-claim event before the
downstream strict leaf. Reproduced: StrictDirectClaim, StrictDirectClaim,
StrictImportedClaim respectively.

INVENTORY-VS-BYTES DISAGREEMENTS FOUND (the bytes win):

1. The inventory states of the 6 trap-expecting rows that no migrated
   predicate is expected to be refuted "because every such predicate is
   runtime-computed". eff4-pos-trap-aborts is not: its predicate was
   `ieq(1_i32, 2_i32)`, two constants, and the mechanical migration
   produces `[CLM-2] RefutedClaim{predicate: "1 = 2", negation: "1 != 2"}`.
   The same holds for op5-neg-check-fails (`ilt(3_i32, 2_i32)`),
   trap-op5-check-fails and scope4-pos-check-traps (`ieq(2_i32, 3_i32)`).
   All four keep their declared trap verdict by taking the one predicate
   form CLM-2 names as neither redundant nor refutable — a constructed
   `False()` — so the failure stays a runtime event, which is the subject
   each case declares. Only x-arith-check-catches-wrapped-overflow-traps
   and clm1-trap-runtime-violation are genuinely runtime-computed and take
   the plain leg-A migration.

2. The inventory's CLM analogue for prv3-neg-external-check is
   byte-for-byte the already-present prv3-neg-external-claim. Rather than
   land a duplicate or delete protected evidence, the case is re-authored
   one step out: the claim now asserts a `band` of two bounds and two
   protected subscripts follow it. The S3-blinded state removes the
   establishment and its signed decomposition together, so PRV-3 still
   rejects at the first `bytes[index]` with residual `index < len(bytes)`.
   This is the negative twin of ent3-pos-band-check-decomposition.

OTHER NOTES.

- op5-pos-check-pass under plain leg-A draws a CLM-2 redundancy advisory
  (the fragment already derives `1 +wrap 2 = 3`), which duplicates
  clm2-pos-redundant-claim-advisory and contradicts the case's own doc.
  The index now passes through a pure call, so the claim is neither
  redundant nor refuted and its passed fact is the sole discharge of a
  following subscript — the "creates the checked fact on the dominated
  path" the case declares.
- clm3-pos-transitive-value-branch takes leg B (a real branch), because a
  claim in the marked root would be a CLM-3 direct seed. With the body
  assertion gone the body exhibits no `traps`, so its row narrows to
  `pure`; the requires-block contract final is untouched.
- x-arith-idiv-trap-zero-divisor-traps takes the leg-A source migration
  here and is red until slice 3 lands its manifest flip to
  `reject OP-2` (residual `0_i32 != 0`) per the division-dissolution
  disposition. Reproduced now: OP-2 UndischargedDivisionObligation.
- Manifest rows citing OP-5 for a migrated body assertion move to CLM-1.
  OP-5 keeps case coverage through fn8-neg-requires-non-bool-check, whose
  contract final is untouched.

Every disposition here is a proposal awaiting the owner's exact-byte

## 55e94798 2026-08-18 PROTECTED CANDIDATE (awaiting owner batch approval): repair the 7 refutation-guard conformance cases for v0.32

Batch 0071, task #47, executor E8c, slice 2 of 4. The mechanical leg-A pass
(commit 819850e9) reverted seven files because migrating them produced a
compile-time CLM-2 refuted-claim rejection instead of the manifest-declared
verdict. Each carried an unreachable-branch guard of the shape
`check ieq(0_i32, 1_i32) else trap "...";` — two constants whose relation
the closed fact state derives, so the migrated claim's exact negation is
derivable and CLM-2 rejects.

DECISION ROWS (old verdict -> new verdict), 7 cases:

  ent4-pos-contradictory-state-discharges  accept -> accept
  err3-pos-propagation                     run 0  -> run 0
  type2-pos-twostate-enum-i1               run 0  -> run 0
  x-enum-stmt-payload-check                run 0  -> run 0
  x-give-result-aggregate                  run 0  -> run 0
  x-ownmove-copy-reused-affine-consumed-once  run 0 -> run 0
  x-ownmove-owned-temporary-scrutinee      run 0  -> run 0

No verdict changes. No case is deleted and no guard is dropped.

THE REPAIR. CLM-2 states that a conforming claim whose predicate has no
comparison origin — "a constructed `True()`, a `band` result" — is neither
redundant nor refutable, is accepted, and traps whenever it evaluates false
at runtime. An unreachable-branch tripwire is therefore spelled
`claim NAME: False() because "MSG";` under v0.32. Six cases take exactly
that for the guard that must never run and the plain leg-A migration for
every guard that carries a real predicate, so each case keeps the full
discrimination its subject needs: err3 still detects a wrong propagation
arm, type2 still detects an even flip count, x-give still detects a wrong
Result variant, and the two ownmove cases still detect a wrong match arm.
Verified: the constructed-predicate claim compiles, survives CLM-2, and
aborts with the CLM-1 DIAG-3 record when its statement is reached.

ent4-pos-contradictory-state-discharges is the one case whose guards were
its subject rather than its scaffolding: it built a contradictory state out
of two executed checks that cannot both pass. Two claims cannot do that —
the first establishes `i > room` and the second's predicate `i < room` then
has its exact negation derived, which is the CLM-2 rejection. The case now
builds the same contradiction from one executed claim followed by one
executed branch condition, which is legal and keeps an executed runtime
check as one of the two sources. Two consequences, both stated in the case
doc:

- Order is load-bearing. With the two sources exchanged the claim is
  refuted, so this case also pins that CLM-2 refutation is a flow judgment
  rather than a whole-body one.
- The subscript is now `b[j]`, a second index nothing else bounds, instead
  of `b[i]`. Reproduced control: with the claim removed the same body
  rejects `[OP-4] UndischargedBoundsObligation{residual: "j < len(b)"}`,
  and with it the program accepts. The original `b[i]` would have accepted
  from the branch condition alone, so the case declared ENT-4 while
  testing nothing about contradiction; this is the smallest change that
  makes the declared subject the reason the case is green.

VERIFICATION. `cargo test --test canonical_corpus` returns to 3/3 (485
corpus files: 457 round-tripped, 1 manifest-declared non-canonical, 20
manifest-declared underived, 0 unexpectedly non-canonical, 0 unexpectedly
underived); `tests/conformance/test_runner.py` 28/28.

Every disposition here is a proposal awaiting the owner's exact-byte
approval on the protected conformance surface.

   the row is pure". Under the candidate a body check does not parse, and its
   successor the claim exhibits `traps`, so a claim cannot produce a pure row.
   The case takes a dominating branch instead, which is the fact source that
   leaves the row pure. The claim route is exactly what the list's separate
   op2-pos-division-claim-backstop covers, and that case is `traps`, so the
   two together state the distinction the list intended.
3. sys14-list-handle-unique is proposed as SYS-4. The reproduced rejection is
   `[OWN-5] BorrowConflict`: two live unique borrows of one handle are
   ordinary exclusivity, and the family contract needs no rule of its own.
   Declared reject OWN-5, with SYS-4 retained in `rules` as the reason the
   case exists.
4. sys14-no-path-from-bytes is proposed as PATH-1. The reproduced rejection is
   `[TYPE-5] TypeMismatch` at the `relative_path` argument: the gap is closed
   by the argument type, not by a path rule. Declared reject TYPE-5, with
   PATH-1 retained in `rules`.
5. sys14-list-outcome-exhaustive is proposed as one case that is both a
   positive exhaustiveness case and an ERR-2 rejection. A case carries one
   verdict; this is the positive half. sys14-directory-release is proposed to
   assert that "the emitted program contains no second close", which the
   corpus cannot observe -- the adapter reads exit status, not emitted text.
   The case pins the runnable half and its doc says so.

## 5b137e98 2026-08-18 compiler: judge the body-syntactic effect contribution on the written body

[EFF-2]'s body-syntactic contribution is judged once on the written body, and
the v0.32 candidate says what that means where a class reads the selected
type: a bare `/` or `%` whose written selected type is a generic type
parameter and whose operand atoms are non-constant is outside [OP-2]'s divisor
class for that contribution and exhibits `traps`, while the obligation and its
discharge stay per concrete instance.

The checker judged the row separately at every instance, so one written body
demanded two different rows: `traps` at a signed instance, whose two-variable
site keeps its trap, and `pure` at an unsigned one, whose class site
contributes nothing. No written row satisfied both, and every generic
divisor-class body was unwritable — the symbolic instance rejected `pure` while
the unsigned instance rejected `traps`.

The written body is exactly what the symbolic validation instance checks, so
its syntactic contribution is recorded there and reused by every instance of
the same declaration; the release contribution is not syntactic and stays per
instance [STOR-3]. This cannot change an accepted program's verdict: today the
declared row must already equal both the symbolic row and every instance's row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## d8f24df9 2026-08-18 compiler: intern the written constant zero as the zero term

[ENT-6]'s zero-divisor conjunct is stated against the distinguished zero term
Z, while a written `0_i32` interned as its own `Constant(0)` term. The two
denote the same mathematical value, and [ENT-2] relates values, but the
fragment could only cross between them through the constant's implicit
equality when a bound was already available on that side. At an unsigned type
the type's own lower bound supplied it, so `claim ine(d, 0_u32)` discharged; at
a signed type nothing did, so `claim nz: ine(d, 0_i32)` and the dominating
`if ine(d, 0_i32)` both left `d != 0` undischarged — [OP-2]'s own mechanical
fix was unwritable at every signed divisor-class site.

Interning canonicalizes the constant zero to Z, so one term carries one
mathematical value. Z holds exactly the bounds the constant zero contributed
(its implicit equality to Z was the reflexive bound), so no fact is lost; the
offset split now reads Z as the constant it is. Two derivation-inventory tests
change with it: a `values[0_u64]` subscript proves itself from its array-length
bound against Z directly, with no constant fold in between.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 78943dad 2026-08-18 compiler: make the traversal inventory differential a real comparison

Both traversal inventory tests compared one inventory with itself. With

`compile_program_with_traversal_surface` resolve to the same call, so
`assert_eq!` of the two held by construction: neither an ordinal move nor a

against the base tables and against the tables with the traversal rows

## 39746f41 2026-08-18 PROTECTED CANDIDATE (awaiting owner batch approval): cover the strict-in-U call and the borrowed arena result

case, verdict, rule list, status, expectation, or doc changes.

  + stor4-neg-borrowed-arena-result (reject STOR-4)

reach. Its CLM-3 cases drive claim import into a marked root and its FN-8 cases
drive ordinary requirement proof; neither reaches the judgment where an outside
caller must re-prove a marked root's requirement in its own unasserted view.

carry, so FN-8 rejects the call and names the unasserted view.

stated: the existing escape case returns an owned arena, so a compiler that read
"may not be returned" as owned-only would still pass. A borrow-mode arena result
is the same escape, rejected at the complete `rtype` with no call, and STOR-4 is
the rule cited there because this specification defines it before FN-1, whose
borrow-result provenance judgment applies to a region-free result type.

Report only, opened by batch 0072 W4 and closed by the lead's sequencing:
no conformance case is added and no citation is changed here.

Both gaps have one cause. A rule's declared coverage is a writer-chosen
`rules` list, so when a spec delta moves the reported rule at a site the
corpus follows the report, the vacated rule loses its evidence, and
`coverage` stays 135/135 because some other case still names it. The
adapter cannot see it: on a citation flip the declared and the actual
verdict move together.

OWN-6 has zero reject-citing cases. Its one negative became a FN-1
rejection when the declaration-site provenance judgment landed, while the
compiler still raises InvalidChildReborrow under SemanticRule::Own6 at
three separable conditions in semantic/check/borrows.rs (:737 non-candidate
argument position, :770 non-statement-scoped child region, :793 holder
role / kind / outlives). All three are pinned only by library tests. The
record proposes three cases, one per condition, each transcribed from the
green library test that already asserts that exact rule and issue kind --
plus a correction to own6-pos-callscoped-temp's `reason`, which asserts
OWN-6 "is never separately cited" and is what makes the gap read as
deliberate.

OP-5's nine non-reject citations went to zero when check dissolution
retired the body statement they exercised, but the rule itself became the
condition judgment, reached from `if`, loop, [CLM-1], and the contract

## c735a0d6 2026-08-18 research: proposal D for the contract surface — the contract is one expression

One of four independent proposals in the contract-surface design study. It
argues that the statement block is itself the defect: a contract clause is a
statement context that is not a function body, which is why a statement
construct got borrowed and half-neutered (the inert `else trap "msg"`), why
FN-8/FN-9 need a structural pass to police the borrowed vocabulary back down,
and why the clause locals need their own copy judgment and an alpha-expansion
pass. The proposal makes a contract one nested proposition expression with no
binding facility, reachable only from the two clause positions.

Includes the corpus measurement that decides the stance (108 clauses, 64 of
them under the current grammar: mean 0.9 locals, median 18-character
predicate, maximum 62 characters, every `ensures` in the tree collapsing to
one binding-free line), the ANF/GRAM-9 answer, exact rule text for
GRAM-2/4/6/9/12, FORM-2/3, OP-5, FN-7, FN-8, FN-9, ENT-2, ENT-3.S4, GIVE-1,
EFF-2, OWN-1, PROG-3 and DIAG-1/2/3, the entry restriction stated as an FN-7
rule, the FFI and S4 composition, and a self-attack section.

Corrects two measured facts supplied to the study: 532 `fn main`
declarations, not 77 or 525, and three of them carry a `requires`, not none
or one. Migration cost is 45 protected conformance files, ten of which retire
or change verdict class.

## df4b1994 2026-08-18 research: recommend keeping Linux enumeration unmapped, and say why honestly

Batch 0072, W3. The disposition question was map Linux with getdents64
or keep it unmapped and state the stop in the spec's own terms. The
recommendation is to keep it unmapped, because a qualification row is a
promise and this one cannot be kept from a macOS-only tree: [QUAL-3]
conditions qualification on inspecting emitted code that would never be
emitted for a runnable target, `linux_dirent64` carries no name-length
field so its portable rewrite needs a bounded in-record scan rather than
a different constant table, and the call's own shape (three arguments,
no position slot, a glibc 2.30 wrapper floor) needs a Linux host to
settle rather than a guess.

The investigation also found the tree gives the wrong reason for the
stop. Linux does supply [QUAL-2]'s third guarantee — getdents64 is
exactly one host call reporting a bounded batch and advancing the
directory's own position — so what is absent is the approved
implementation row, which [QUAL-1] makes a different stop. The compiler
reports UnmetGuarantee where it should report MissingMapping, its own
code comment already says MissingMapping, and the derivation ledger
repeats the conflation. The delta adds the one [QUAL-2] sentence that
teaches a reader the difference without naming a target, which QUAL-1
forbids, and specifies the compiler correction and its first regression
for the lead to land with the spec bytes.

No specification byte, no conformance byte, and no compiler byte changes
here.

## 39dcf1a3 2026-08-18 research: proposal D for the contract surface — the contract is one expression

One of four independent proposals in the contract-surface design study. It
argues that the statement block is itself the defect: a contract clause is a
statement context that is not a function body, which is why a statement
construct got borrowed and half-neutered (the inert `else trap "msg"`), why
FN-8/FN-9 need a structural pass to police the borrowed vocabulary back down,
and why the clause locals need their own copy judgment and an alpha-expansion
pass. The proposal makes a contract one nested proposition expression with no
binding facility, reachable only from the two clause positions.

Includes the corpus measurement that decides the stance (108 clauses, 64 of
them under the current grammar: mean 0.9 locals, median 18-character
predicate, maximum 62 characters, every `ensures` in the tree collapsing to
one binding-free line), the ANF/GRAM-9 answer, exact rule text for
GRAM-2/4/6/9/12, FORM-2/3, OP-5, FN-7, FN-8, FN-9, ENT-2, ENT-3.S4, GIVE-1,
EFF-2, OWN-1, PROG-3 and DIAG-1/2/3, the entry restriction stated as an FN-7
rule, the FFI and S4 composition, and a self-attack section.

Corrects two measured facts supplied to the study: 532 `fn main`
declarations, not 77 or 525, and three of them carry a `requires`, not none
or one. Migration cost is 45 protected conformance files, ten of which retire
or change verdict class.

Research only: no specification byte, test, or compiler file changes.

Replaces the four-proposal framing in
research/investigations/contract-surface/ with a derivation: the eight owner-
named axes, the determinations the fixed constraints already force, the axes

points, and the exact observation or ruling that would settle each open axis.

Six determinations survived adversarial challenge: expression-local binding
(GRAM-9:299-300 with FORM-1:29 and META-2:3258), unit-level propositions in
the opaque reading (ENT-3:2799, ENT-4:2882), the trap STRING as prose channel
(its four readers are unreachable after the owner rulings), redundancy as a
hard rejection (ENT-1:2741), erasure wherever a clause-local binder exists
(ENT-2:2759 with TYPE-6:394 and FN-8:1247), and the ensures half of the
goal-template axis (FN-9:1305-1313). One determination was overturned: the
goal-template axis is live for requires under unit-level propositions, and is
restated as structural-versus-nominal proposition identity.

## ac34410b 2026-08-19 programs: keep wfgrep's one-write diagnostic and its A10 delivery route

Batch 0072 W1, answering the lead's option (a). report_failure assembles
`wfgrep: PATH: reason` in one reusable buffer and publishes it with one host
write, so it must clamp the assembled length against the buffer's capacity,
and a `value_if` over the fits test is how that clamp is written. That is the
better code on its own terms — one host write per diagnostic instead of
three, and no chance of the three pieces being separated in a shared sink —
and it keeps the A10 postcondition-delivery route with its real-program
witness rather than leaving the frozen-source gate with a synthetic one.

The invalid-relative-path reason comes back with it: the single-file fallback
can be handed a root `relative_path` rejects, and that is now named rather
than reported as an unreadable file. The two diagnostics the argv-list
version published without a path — broken pipe and write error — are gone
with the loop that published them; a failed publication now reports through
the same `wfgrep: PATH: reason` channel, so their constants are deleted
rather than left unread.

Re-derived from source with the same rule the module states: one receiver
route per `append_slice` call site, eleven of them (report_failure's eight,
main's three), where the argv-list version had twelve (main had four).
Publications to the standard-error owner are two, not four, because the
diagnostic is one write again.

cargo test --lib backend::tests::cost_shape + frozen_real_sources: 11 passed,
0 failed. cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings: clean.
