repair is to collect through the growable layer, which is the next
batch's first item. The flagship corpus puts 4,096 files in one
directory, so W2's re-attribution is blocked until then.

## 93aedd79 2026-08-21 docs: move governance to branch autonomy with merge-time approval

Agents now work on branches with no mid-flight approval waits: spec
candidates, protected-compliance evidence, plan updates, root entries,
code, tests, and docs all iterate autonomously on a branch. The single
owner boundary is the merge to main, whose packet presents every
reviewable class (candidate SHA-256/diff/impact/verifier results,
protected-evidence before/after audits, plan revisions, root entries)
alongside the batch records, branch-tip gate result, and audit
dispositions; spec activation becomes the approved merge's activation
commit. Batch records may open under a recorded chartering owner
direction, enabling overnight multi-batch branch delegation.

AGENTS.md becomes the Codex variant: same project rules, Claude-Code-only
tooling references replaced with in-repo equivalents; the byte-identity
gate retires in favor of audit-enforced synchrony, with the Makefile
invariant reduced to presence checks.

## 623660da 2026-08-21 compiler: judge which sibling call pairs may be overlapped

Adds the permission judgment P (batch 0074, DESIGN.md section 3): for an
ordered pair of adjacent `let x = f(...);` statements in one block, P holds
when there is no dataflow from the first to the second, the two callees'
boundary-projected read/write footprints are disjoint under [OWN-7], neither
row carries `external` or `blocks`, and no exit edge of the first statement
bypasses the second. Actualization additionally requires that the transitive
call closure of both callees reach zero `claim` sites. The result is a
read-only per-function table of analyzed pairs and eligible chains carried on
the checked program; acceptance never reads it.

P consults typing, declared rows, resolved places, statement exit edges, and
the concrete call graph, and never the entailment fact state, so the table is
identical facts-on and facts-off by construction.

Rather than copy the machinery it needs, this lifts the shared half out of
the entailment engine: `semantic/places.rs` now owns the resolved-place
types, the [OWN-7] overlap relation, the binding holder prepass, and the
actual-side [EFF-2] projection, with `entailment/flow.rs` delegating to it,
and `expression_children` moves to `model.rs`. Entailment behavior is
unchanged.

Two footprint rules go beyond the four conditions, both fail-closed: an
`allocates(arena 'r)` row contributes its caller region as a written element,
because two overlapped calls would both mutate one allocation list; and an
actual whose caller place cannot be resolved while its row projects an access
denies the pair.

Tests: three grant shapes (two-child unique fold, read-only sibling
recursion, reads-only siblings over one place), one control that a chain
stops where a non-adjacent pair conflicts, one denial per condition each
asserting the cited condition, and one permitted-but-not-actualizable case
with its claim count and witness.

## 85702e6f 2026-08-21 compiler: report the permission judgment as a developer ledger

The permission judgment decided which sibling call pairs may be
overlapped, but decided it silently. A writer whose two calls were
sequentialized had no way to learn that they were, or which of the four
conditions refused them, or which two places to separate to get the
overlap back. Sequentialization that is invisible is indistinguishable
from a compiler that never looked.

So render the finished table as one developer-channel line per analyzed
source site and put it behind `whitefootc --par-ledger`. A line names the
verdict, the source site, the two callees, and then either `eligible`,
the claim count and the function that carries the claim, or the numbered
condition that refused the pair together with the source text that
refused it. The condition number is read from the denial itself rather
than re-derived, so the reported condition cannot drift from the judging
one.

The ledger is presentation and nothing else. It participates in no
mandatory record, changes no accepted program, and selects no lowering;
it is rendered in the checker only because that is where the syntax tree
the citations name is still alive. `compile_with_permission_ledger` is
the one pipeline and the existing entry points became projections of it,
so there is no second compilation path to keep in step.

Two judgment calls the audit should look at. Byte-identical lines are
collapsed, because the table is dense by function id and one generic
monomorphized twice would otherwise report a single source site twice.
And `--par-ledger` with `--emit-llvm` and no `-o` is refused rather than
interleaving two streams into one stdout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 2b8e8f7a 2026-08-21 compiler: actualize permitted overlap groups on worker lanes

The permission judgment says which sibling calls may be overlapped; this
is the half that takes the permission. Lowering carries each permitted and
eligible chain into the IR as an overlap group over the values its calls
define, narrowed to what one straight-line edge can carry. The backend
hands every member but the last to a worker lane: the arguments go into a
stack frame, the call is outlined into an internal thunk over that frame,
and the lane offer returns a handle or a refusal. The last member runs
inline, and each hand-out is joined right after it, so no group value is
read and no exit edge is reached before every lane has returned.

Both edges of a hand-out call the same monomorphized function on the same
arguments, so one source call still has exactly one lowering: a refused
lane computes the sequential result on the sequential schedule.

The runtime is one C translation unit: a lazily started pool sized by
WF_WORKERS, whose lanes are claimed atomically and never queued, so an
offer never blocks and never oversubscribes. Unset, unparsable, or below
two leaves the pool unstarted and every offer refused, which is exactly
today's schedule.

A module that hands work out carries weak definitions of both runtime
entry points that refuse every lane, and the runtime's strong definitions
replace them at link. The permission is never an obligation, so neither is
its runtime: a program that could overlap still links and still runs
correctly with no runtime present, and every link path that wants lanes
adds the unit on the one condition the driver uses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## ca9bf206 2026-08-21 compiler: test that overlapping moves no observable byte

Seven tests over the actualization path. The codegen test reads one
permitted pair's emission: the outlined thunk over its frame, the lane
offer, the inline second member, and the join whose refusal edge runs the
same thunk on this thread, in that order, with the offered value read only
in the block the join branches to. The denial test reads the other side: a
pair the judgment refuses names no part of the runtime at all.

The narrowing test pins the one rule lowering adds to the judgment. A
permitted pair whose first member is a borrowed binding is not handed out,
because promoting that binding reads the call's value between the offer and
the join; the same pair with only its last member borrowed is handed out,
because the last member always runs on the calling thread.

The repeat test runs the overlapped fold five times at each of four worker
counts and byte-compares every run against each other and against the same
module linked with no runtime at all. Its negative control proves the
comparison reports an injected difference, so a green repeat is a claim
about the program rather than about the comparison.

The load-bearing one is the override test. Every other test here passes
just as well when the module's weak refusal wins the link and nothing is
ever overlapped, because refusing every lane is a correct execution. It
links the real runtime beside an observer that reports the runtime's own
grant count at process exit, and fails when the count is zero at four
workers or nonzero at one. The counter is the runtime's, exported for
exactly this reason: no Whitefoot construct can name it.

## da175351 2026-08-21 compiler: demonstrate the permission path on a real layout workload

par_layout.wf folds one box tree twice. The two folds have the same
recursive shape, write the same kind of per-node slot, and read the same
shared metric table; they differ only in where the per-node measure gets
its bound. layout walks the whole table, so the index obligation is
discharged and the closure is claim-free. layout_banded walks a
caller-supplied prefix, so the obligation is carried by one claim.

That single difference is the whole experiment. The ledger reports both
child pairs permitted and only the claim-free one eligible, and the
emitted module carries the thunk, the offer, and the join in @wf_layout
and no part of the runtime in @wf_layout_banded. The program publishes
the exact bits of both fold results, so a divergence anywhere in either
tree is a divergence in the published bytes.

The three cases pin that split, read the compiler's own ledger lines
rather than re-deriving them, and byte-compare the published output with
the worker setting absent and at two and four lanes. Whether the pool
actually grants a lane stays pinned by the in-crate runtime test that
reads the grant counter, and the module comment says so rather than
leaving the reader to assume this file covers it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 3d08e2d5 2026-08-21 docs: report the measured parallelism results and land its deciding probes

RESULTS.md is the evidence half of DESIGN.md: the protocol, the machine,
the numbers, the phase decomposition, and eight stated limitations. On an
M4 the whole demo runs 1.46x, 1.79x, 1.79x faster at two, four, and eight
lanes, and the same module linked with no runtime at all is
indistinguishable from one lane, so the default-off path costs nothing
measurable. Decomposed, the eligible fold alone scales 2.98x on four
performance cores while the claim-bearing fold alone stays flat within
five percent, and composing the eligible phase's own scaling with the
observed 66 percent Amdahl share predicts the whole-program figure to
within one percent at every worker count.

Two limitations are load-bearing rather than decorative. The lane budget
refuses 95 percent or more of all offers, so the wins come from the few
lanes near the root; and an earlier draft of this same program with a
cheap per-node body measured a 2.1x slowdown, which is the concrete case
for the deferred heartbeat policy rather than a hypothetical one.

The ten probes are the sources that actually decided something during the
three research rounds. They were written outside the repository and were
dying artifacts, and the design's load-bearing claims cite them, so they
land here as archived evidence with a README stating what each settles.
Two of them produce no ledger line at all, and the README says why rather
than letting them read as denial witnesses they are not.

## 34d92856 2026-08-21 compiler: judge the caller-side operand reads an overlap moves

The permission judgment modelled only what the two callees reach through
their declared rows. It modelled nothing about the storage a statement's
own operand expressions read on the calling thread, and the lowering
emits s2's operand evaluation after s1 has been offered to a lane. Every
such read was therefore moved across s1's call on every edge, including
the refused-lane fallback and a build with no runtime linked at all.

    let a = bump<'r>(slot: &uniq 'r cell);
    let b = take(v: cell);

was permitted and eligible, and published the pre-write value: 1 instead
of 15, with WF_WORKERS unset and no runtime present. With lanes granted
the same shape is a load on the calling thread racing a store on a
worker, observable as a varying published byte sequence at one fixed
worker count.

Condition 2 now carries a caller-side operand footprint for the second
member and requires it disjoint from the first member's writes. Forming
a borrow takes an address and reads no content, so it contributes
nothing; a read through a slice descriptor cannot be resolved and denies.
The walk is exhaustive over the checked expression forms, because a
missing operand read widens permission.

Also in the same direction of failure:

- collect_claim_sites and push_nested_blocks lose their wildcard arms. A
  body-bearing statement form this walk did not descend into would hide
  the claims inside it, and a hidden claim widens eligibility.
- The runtime's symbols move to the reserved wf__par_ prefix. Source
  functions are emitted as wf_ plus their IDENT, which [FORM-3] spells
  [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, so no source name can reach a symbol whose first
  character after wf_ is an underscore. Before this, a program declaring
  fn par_try_fork was accepted by the checker and then rejected by the
  host toolchain with a raw invalid-redefinition error.
- A worker stack is now at least the calling thread's own stack, and a
  refused pthread_attr_setstacksize stops the pool instead of silently
  handing out 512 KB lanes.
- A condition-2 denial states which two halves conflicted, so a
  read/write conflict is no longer reported as two writes.

Tests: the operand-read hazard and its subscript form, the
read-then-write direction of condition 2, a program named like the
runtime, and a differential that compiles one source twice — once with
the permission table emptied — and byte-compares the two programs. That
last one is the only comparison on this path whose reference is not the
same emitted module linked differently, which is why nothing here
noticed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## e2f497c0 2026-08-21 compiler: make the parallel lowering compile-time opt-in

The closure audit measured the overlap lowering itself, with no runtime linked
and WF_WORKERS unset, at about 1.2x on the layout demo and 2.1x on fib(38). An
outlined call passes its arguments through a memory frame and is reached
through a function pointer, so it cannot be inlined, and the weak
wf__par_try_fork cannot be folded away because a linker may replace it. That
cost is unconditional, which contradicts the design's own default: byte-
identical behavior to a compiler without this path.

Actualization therefore becomes a compile-time choice. whitefootc gains --par;
the library gains OverlapLowering, threaded through compile_with_overlap,
compile_with_permission_ledger, and lower_checked. With the option off -- the
default of every entry point, including the one the conformance adapter calls
-- lowering never reads the permission table, so no group reaches the IR, no
thunk is outlined, no module names a runtime symbol, and no link path can add
the runtime. Verified against the compiler from main: all twenty single-source
corpus programs emit byte-identical modules apart from the one-line v0.33/v0.34
qualification stamp.

The judgment itself is unchanged and still runs on every compile: it is pure,
it changes no accepted program, and --par-ledger reports the same verdicts
either way. A developer reads what the compiler decided about a program
without changing the program that gets built.

Tests: the_default_compilation_hands_nothing_out pins that a fixture full of
eligible sites emits no wf__par_ symbol and no thunk by default while the same
source with the option on hands work out; the corpus gains the same check for
par_layout.wf; the driver pins that both ledgers are equal while only the --par
module names the runtime; whitefootc pins that --par-ledger does not imply
--par. The in-crate differential's non-outlined reference is now the default
compilation itself rather than a checked program with its permission table
emptied, which deletes emit_without_overlap and its adjust hook.

Verification: make -C compiler check exit 0, 1014 library tests (+2), 52
real-program tests (+1), 4 whitefootc tests (+1); every other target's count
byte-identical.

## b6f496b4 2026-08-21 compiler: claim a lane before building the hand-out frame

A handed-out call used to store its arguments into a stack slot of the
*calling* function, so every activation of an eligible recursive function
carried that slot and its spills whether or not a lane was ever granted.
The measured price was four times the stack per frame on a small
activation and a bare SIGSEGV where the sequential build ran fine — the
same schedule under a different resource envelope, with the pool off.

The frame belongs to the lane now, and the claim comes first. The runtime
contract becomes claim/publish/join/release: a claim takes an idle lane
and returns its frame, the caller fills that frame and publishes the
thunk to it, the join waits, and the release gives the lane back only
after the caller has read the result out — a lane handed on at the join
could refill the frame under that read. The stores and the publish sit
inside the granted edge, so a refused activation executes a null test and
its own ordinary call and builds nothing. That refused edge calls the
callee directly rather than running the thunk over a caller-owned frame;
both edges and the thunk still call one monomorphized function on one
rendering of the same operands. A lane's frame is bounded, and a call
whose frame is larger is simply never granted a lane.

Measured, bisected first-failing depth with WF_WORKERS unset. On the
realistic left-spine fold the --par build goes from 103 827 to 128 750,
the same bisection bracket as the sequential build: a 19.4% depth loss
becomes parity. On the minimal probe it goes from 130 663 to 173 876
against a sequential 522 460. That probe does not reach parity and no
hand-out lowering can: its sequential build keeps a 16-byte frame only
because interprocedural constant propagation proves one argument
constant at every level, and a thunk — a second caller whose argument
comes out of memory — destroys that fact. Restoring the constant by hand
inside the thunk returns the frame to 16 bytes, which is what isolates
the residue; a prototype outlining the whole overlap group still lands at
32.

The default compilation is untouched: 36 modules emit byte-identical
LLVM before and after. Output stays byte-identical at every worker count
and the grant counter still counts. Two cases guard the fix: one compares
alloca counts between the two lowerings of one source, one runs both
lowerings of a deep recursion under a stack limit it sets, at a depth
measured to lie between the old ceiling and the new one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 408dd34e 2026-08-21 compiler: replace the lane scan with per-thread work-stealing deques

An offer used to be a search: `wf__par_claim` walked the lane array with an
acquire-CAS per lane, on lines the lanes themselves were using, and a grant
cost a mutex round trip plus a condition-variable wake. That price fell on
every offer, granted or refused, so a program that offered faster than the
pool could absorb paid the whole search for nothing — 48.8 ns per fork point
at the coarsest cell in the oracle, against rayon's 4.5, and up to 48.6x
slower than sequential where the grain was fine.

An offer is now a push onto the offering thread's own deque: one buffer store
and one release store of `bottom`, no read-modify-write, no other thread's
memory, no syscall. Idle threads steal the oldest entry, which on a recursive
descent is the shallowest fork point and so the largest remaining subtree, and
`wf__par_join` pops its own offer back and runs it as an ordinary call rather
than blocking on a lane. The expensive operation is a steal, and a steal
happens only when a thread runs out of work, so its count follows how
unbalanced the program turned out to be instead of how often it offered.

The four entry-point signatures, the weak fallback text, and every emitted IR
byte are unchanged: the whole diff is the runtime and its tests.

Full protocol rotation, N=9, 144 cells, 1296 runs, every run byte-identical
within and across both languages. No cell with workers>=2 is slower than its
own w=1 column any more (worst 1.16x); bal_d8_w16/8 goes 4.3245s -> 0.4905s
and bal_d12_w192/8 goes 0.3052s -> 0.1272s, 4.71x against rayon's 4.54x. In
absolute wall time WF is faster than rayon outside the 0.83-1.20x band in 14
of 36 cells and at parity in the other 22; no cell has rayon faster. Per-fork
excess at bal_d12_w192/4: 48.8 ns -> 4.80 ns, against rayon's 5.80 ns in the
same pass. Probes, min-of-7, byte-identical: q4.wf W=64 25.55s -> 0.2530s
(48.6x slower -> 1.99x faster), bt.wf W=64 4.0218s -> 0.0550s.

Dig 1's depth property survives: min_stack.wf first failing depth under a
1024 KB stack is 22000 pool-off, unchanged, and 22500 at W=4/W=8 — the
slot bound stops the reclaim path after the first levels and handed-out work
runs on worker stacks.

wf__par_grants still counts exactly one thing, a frame executed by a thread
other than the one that offered it. Counting pushes would have been the false
green the counter exists to catch. Its test is untouched, but the guarantee
moved from structural to timing-dependent; the batch record carries the
measured margin and the sensitivity for the merge packet.

The record also carries the disposition of the chartered second stage,
two-version sequential-clone compilation: built, measured, and not landed.
Its premise does not hold here (the pool-off `--par` build is already faster
than the sequential build on 9 of 12 configs, so there is no un-promoted-path
tax to remove), its ceiling is below the instrument at every cell it could
have changed, and the demand signal it needs cost 0.4905s -> 0.9254s at
bal_d8_w16/8 — attributed by discriminator to contended read-modify-writes on
a shared word, not to the refusal. The emitter was never touched.

## fdbb6c02 2026-08-21 docs: attribute the skew sequential gap and dissolve the outlining paradox

Dig 3 was chartered to lift the skew sequential floor. The floor reproduces
under an isolated rotation that removes the fixed-rotation slot confound
(1.118x/1.206x/1.267x at w16/w64/w192, balanced flat at 0.981x), but it is
not a codegen defect and no static compiler change can remove it, so none
landed.

It is a pure stall: Whitefoot retires fewer instructions than the Rust twin
in every matched cell (0.980x-0.997x) while IPC collapses on skew only
(2.628 against 3.399 at w192) and is at parity on balanced. All twelve
binaries carry the identical 136-instruction _wf_layout, -O2 already narrows
the whole-node load, and the node write-back is dead-store eliminated
outright.

The cause is traversal order and it is data-dependent. Swapping the two child
calls turns a 1.23x loss into a 1.02x win with bit-identical output; balanced
trees show zero order effect from d8 to d14 while skew shows a constant
1.28x from d12 to d20, including at 45 KiB where the whole tree is
L1D-resident; and mirroring the tree flips the sign exactly. The rule is
"visit the smaller subtree last", a runtime property of the heap. Reordering
siblings statically would win here and lose on the mirror image, which is
keying codegen to one corpus's source shape.

Node size, allocator zone, recursion depth, code alignment, rotation slot,
minimum-vs-minnum, and two Rust replicas built to reproduce the pathology are
each falsified by measurement in the batch record. The microarchitectural
root is reported unlocated rather than named beyond the evidence.

The premise the dig was dispatched under is false: the --par build does not
pay the floor (0.733x of wf_seq on skew w192 against 1.005x-1.016x on
balanced), so the parallel cells never carried it. Against a directly
measured hardware ceiling (1.90x/3.69x/4.74-5.71x at 2/4/8, since eight
threads are four performance plus four efficiency cores), 16 of the 30 parity
cells are at or above ceiling and unwinnable by any scheduler; the residual
is at eight workers and fine grain.

Dig 4 folds in resolved. The par_layout outlining tax was F1, not outlining:
742.6ms against 902.5ms then, 0.7486s against 0.7481s now. The opposite-sign
"win" is only the skew traversal penalty the --par build avoids. fib(38)'s
12.6x-slower lane row is now 1.33x at four workers and 0.91x at eight.

Corrects the two derived claims this dig falsified: the --par doc comment's
1.2x fold cost, and the superseded RESULTS.md tables. No lowering byte
changed; 8 of 8 modules emitted by the before and after compilers are
identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 46e9bbe1 2026-08-21 docs: attribute the eight-worker residual to synchronisation, not the scheduler

Dig 6 was chartered to convert the 14 cells sitting below 92% of Dig 3's
measured ceiling — concentrated at eight workers and the fine w16 grain —
into wins. None converted, and the reason is that the ceiling excludes the
one cost this workload is made of.

The oracle builds its tree once and folds it `reps` times, so every
repetition is a fork-join episode of 5.7us to 854us that ends in a join.
Holding the tree and the fork count fixed and varying only per-node work
moves the eight-worker score 23.2% -> 45.6% -> 70.7%: a fixed cost per
episode, not per fork. Dig 3's N-copies figure is a fair throughput bound —
timing the copies separately shows all eight finishing together, 0.875-0.946s
each, so there is no straggler artifact — but it is measured with no
synchronisation at all. A scheduler-free probe, P threads meeting at a
spinning barrier with no deque and no stealing, measures the barrier alone at
0.340us on four threads and 0.839us on five, reaching 1.399us on eight: a
quarter of a 5.7us episode spent meeting before any work is distributed.

The knee is the fifth worker, the first that must live on an efficiency core.
This machine is 4P+6E; the Dig 3 entry's "four plus four" is corrected in the
record, and the ceilings are unaffected because they were measured rather
than derived from the count. The knee is not Whitefoot's: rayon goes 0.3578
-> 0.9370s from four workers to eight and its recorded t=8 is 0.51x of its
own sequential build, rayoncut goes 0.2485 -> 0.6132s, and the scheduler-free
probe turns over at exactly five. Against a reference handed its work up
front — a flat loop with dynamic self-scheduling — the residual cells read
65% to 95% instead of 23% to 92%, and what is left is work discovery, which a
tree fold cannot avoid and which no measured tree-recursive scheduler does
better than this one.

Every named candidate was built and measured, and each is rejected by
measurement rather than by argument. Sleeping: ten parks in a whole run and
zero system time. The deque bound: zero refusals anywhere. Steal volume:
219.6M probes for 2.09M steals, but a backoff that cuts the rate is
monotonically worse. Victim affinity: loses at every eight-worker cell.
Draining more than one entry per steal: unsound, and it hangs, because a
single CAS on `top` cannot claim a range of a Chase-Lev deque while the owner
pops from `bottom`. Darwin QoS: all four classes within noise. The grant
counter's own global read-modify-write: priced by moving it onto the lane,
and it does not pay for itself.

fib(38)'s 2.96x opt-in tax is attributed exactly and is not the runtime's.
The sequential build turns the second recursion into a loop carrying an
accumulator and executes 63.2M calls; the refused --par edge makes two real
calls and executes 126.5M. Linking with -flto so the refusal can inline
recovers 5%. The transform is foreclosed because the emitter rejoins both
edges through a phi at %par.done, so a measurement convicts the emitter and
this dig stops and reports rather than changing it.

The gate case for the grant counter is untouched and its margin is now a
number: 1000 runs at four workers, none with grants == 0, minimum observed
count 7. The rotation at HEAD is 12 outright wins, 24 parity, and no cell
where rayon is faster; the win count is boundary-sensitive, since eight of
the thirty-six cells sit within 0.02 of the 0.83 line.

No runtime byte and no emitter byte changed, so this commits the record only,
the exception the batch rules allow and the one Dig 3 took.

## 629fad88 2026-08-21 compiler: compile both worlds and pick one at the bootstrap

A `--par` build paid for parallelism it never activated. Dig 6 measured
2.96x on `fib(38)` with the pool off and convicted the emitter: the
hand-out rejoins its granted and refused edges through a phi at
`%par.done`, so the callee's result flows into a phi rather than the
caller's return, which takes the second recursion out of tail position
and forecloses LLVM's accumulator tail-recursion elimination. `-flto`
recovers 5%, so it is a foreclosed compile-time transform, not a runtime
cost, and no rearrangement of one lowering can serve both: the phi is
what actualization is, and the transform requires its absence.

So the module carries both. For every function on a path from the entry
to a handed-out call it also emits a sequential clone under
`wf__par_seq_`, whose calls to other cloned functions name their clones.
The clone is the sequential lowering byte for byte, and the set is a
property of the call graph and the judgment — the functions reachable
from the entry that can reach a hand-out — never of a name or a source
shape. The bootstrap asks `wf__par_pool_active` once and enters one
world; neither ever calls the other, so nothing below that branch tests
anything again, and no per-task signal exists to contend on.

The query reads WF_WORKERS and starts nothing, so the pool is still
created lazily by the first claim. Answering by starting it was built
and cost 17% and 18% on `par_layout` at four and eight workers.

fib(38), min-of-11, byte-identical: pool-off 0.2349 -> 0.0791 s against
the sequential build's 0.0794. `min_stack` pool-off depth 21 683 ->
65 132, the sequential build's own bracket. The overlapped lowering is
untouched — `wf_fib` and `wf_layout` are identical instruction for
instruction — and a full N=9 rotation moves no cell outside the band,
with rayon still winning none. The default build is byte-identical.

`par_layout` pool-off reads 1.19x at equal instruction count and IPC
2.89 -> 2.43; the same module linked with its two inputs in the other
order reads 1.00x, so it is whole-binary placement, not the clone. It is
recorded in the batch record rather than tuned away.

## ae7be029 2026-08-21 compiler: judge the window between two calls, not just the pair

One ordinary statement written between two calls made the pair silently
unjudged: the enumeration collected consecutive call statements and any
other form ended the group, so the two calls on either side never formed a
pair, got no verdict, and produced no ledger line. The same operation
wrapped in a pure function left the calls adjacent and kept its parallel
chain, so two programs with byte-identical output differed 1.9x in wall
time on nothing but statement adjacency. [PAR-1] says s1 *precedes* s2 in
one block, and permission may not turn on where a writer put a line.

The judged unit becomes a window: the ordered pair together with every
statement between them, with all four conditions quantified over the
interposed statements. The clauses are derived as the intersection of the
two schedules a conforming implementation may pick, never the weaker set
the current backend alone would survive, because no rule may be stated in
terms of a schedule. That yields one asymmetry worth naming: an interposed
write is judged against s2's caller-side operand reads and not against
s1's, since s1's operands are read before the fork under one schedule and
s1 has completed under the other. Dropping the s2 side admits a race;
adding the s1 side only costs grants. Both directions are pinned by tests.

Interposed forms are classified by an exhaustive match, so an unclassified
form cannot contribute an empty footprint and widen permission. Exit-
bearing forms deny under condition 4, which closes a hole eligibility
cannot see: it walks callees, so a claim in the caller's own block between
the two calls was invisible to it. Forms with no computed footprint deny
under condition 2. Both now deny *with a report* rather than ending the
enumeration, which is the disclosure half of the finding.

Each block is classified and projected once rather than once per judged
window, and claim reachability is answered by one reverse call-graph walk
instead of a whole-program search per pair, so the wider candidate groups
cost nothing measurable: the suite runs 167.80s against 167.92s before.

The ledger gains a chain line per eligible run, because three permitted
pairs and one three-member run read identically as pairs and are entirely
different work.

Measured: p1a's fold goes from flat at every worker count to 1.91x at four
workers and 2.03x at eight, reaching parity with its wrapped-function twin.
The twelve oracle modules and all 24 oracle binaries are byte-identical
before and after, as are all 28 default-compilation modules.

Defender was controlled rather than assumed: three exposure configurations
of a full wfgrep compile give 45.686 s, 46.102 s and 45.671 s, so real-time

That is the signature of the ENT-4 closure's Floyd-Warshall fixed point in

left and re-hashed for every left.

The branch did not cause it: state.rs is untouched across all nine branch
commits, and the fork point compiles wfgrep in 46.347 s against 45.074 s at

## ded209b9 2026-08-22 compiler: close the ENT-4 fixed point over a dense matrix

The bound relation the closure computes saturates. Instrumenting wfgrep
showed the inner loop running 1.444e9 times and all 1.444e9 probes finding
the edge already present, yet the relation was held in a pair-keyed HashMap
beside a second HashMap of proofs under the same key, so the innermost step
hashed a term pair twice to read something it always had. TermId is already
a dense ordinal, so the working relation becomes one Vec indexed by
left * width + right with the bound and its proof in one cell, rebuilt into
the published maps once per closure. That is linear against a fixed point
that is cubic in the same width.

With the hashing gone the next cost was building a derivation node for all
1.444e9 candidates and rejecting nearly every one on the two numbers alone.
A route strictly weaker than the bound already held is rejected whatever its
derivation, so that test runs first; the node is still built for every
candidate that can win, including the equal-bound case candidate_better has
to inspect.

Nothing about the judgment moves. All 25 programs in both modes -- 50
(program, mode) pairs -- emit byte-identical modules with identical stderr
and exit codes against the preceding commit.

wfgrep frontend 45.007 s -> 9.782 s (4.60x); utf8parse 5.10x, sha256_abc
4.55x, dir_walk 3.80x. make -C compiler check green, 348.44 s -> 146.85 s at
the same 1030 lib + 52 program tests.

## 4b44295b 2026-08-22 compiler: skip a closure middle whose row and column are unwritten

The rounds after the first re-sweep the whole cube to discover that almost
none of it moved. A term is now marked when a bound is written into its row
or its column, and a middle carrying neither mark is skipped.

Why that is sound. Routes through an unmarked middle take their left leg
from its column and their right leg from its row, so they carry the same two
bounds and the same two proofs they carried when it was last swept, and via
is unchanged; the target they would lower can only have fallen since. A
route refused for being weaker than the held bound is refused again. A route
that tied and lost to the held proof also loses to whatever replaced that
proof, because candidate_better orders on (depth, structural tie) and that
order is strict, so losing to P while P is beaten by Q puts the route behind
Q as well. A route that won last time now meets its own proof, which cannot
beat itself. So the sweep can accept nothing.

Marking on the write rather than on a changed bound is what makes this hold:
insert_closed_candidate also accepts a candidate that keeps the bound and
only replaces the proof, and such a write still marks, so the middle whose
legs it feeds is still re-swept.

wfgrep frontend 9.393 s -> 8.417 s on a quiet machine, and 10.620 s ->
9.319 s interleaved while loaded, which is the load-independent form of the
same 1.11x-1.14x. 30.5% of middle-sweeps are skipped for that 11%: sweep
cost is skewed and the skipped ones are the cheap tail, since a middle goes
unwritten when it has few predecessors and its sweep already bailed early.

All 50 (program, mode) pairs byte-identical against the preceding commit.
make -C compiler check green; its test phases fall 52.44 s -> 48.92 s (lib)
and 29.34 s -> 26.76 s (programs).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 5be4f208 2026-08-22 compiler: read a conjunct through the binding that proved it

A `band` claim lost the bound on any conjunct whose subject was a let-bound
derived value, while the same two bounds claimed separately both discharged.
The named goal is a bare place, so only its full expansion had anything to
decompose, and expansion rewrites `next < room` into
`at +wrap 1 < len(deref(input))`, whose arithmetic root has no term form — so
that conjunct's projection was None and the fact was silently dropped. The
loop the report blamed was incidental; the trigger is the derived term.

Decomposition now reads through an unprojected `own Bool` leaf to its
still-valid ordinary-let Boolean origin, and a member that is a bare
comparison binding takes its relation from `state.origins` — the same map,
the same terms and the same validity discipline the equivalent single-bound
claim already depends on.

The checker gets smarter, never more permissive. An index the band never
bounded, a `bor` in place of the `band`, the else edge of `if both`, and
`bnot(band(..))` all still fail their proofs, and a claim that is false at
run time still traps, which is what makes admitting the subscript sound.

Over 697 sources only this dig's four probes change verdict, all
REJECT -> ACCEPT; 276 programs accepted by both binaries emit byte-identical
IR and 417 rejected by both keep the identical rule. The promoted probes
carry the eligibility delta: the branch-guarded form is `eligible`, its
claim-bearing twin is `not-actualizable: 1 claim site via window`, and
before this fix neither of them compiled at all.

The O11 decomposition inventory now also records the binding-rooted parent,
so four existing count assertions were updated; every member and projection
assertion they carried is retained and each gained assertions on the new
entry.

## 3d310311 2026-08-22 compiler: ask a callee's writes row before advising a split

The 0075/0076 batch audit's refuters confirmed a false safety claim in the
counted-loop hint. `CalleeFacts::admits` consulted `reaches_claim`, `external`
and `blocks` and never `writes`, while `Survey` classifies only the `set`
statements written in the loop body — so a callee writing caller storage
through a `&uniq` parameter carried state across iterations that nothing saw.
A loop folding an `f64` under `fadd.strict` one call frame away, beside an
ordinary `+wrap` counter, was told its range would split safely "combining
under +wrap". Taking that advice moves a published byte, which is the one
failure this path exists to make impossible. A row that writes anything now
refuses, and `a_counted_loop_whose_callee_writes_carried_state_is_told_nothing`
pins it against a control that differs only in the callee's row. One root cause
closing three of the audit's findings.

The change is diagnostic-only. All 698 `.wf` sources outside `archive/`, swept
under `--par-ledger --par --emit-llvm`, are byte-identical before and after:
every module hash, every exit status, and every ledger line, the two `PAR hint`
lines the corpus emits included.

Beside it, `the_shipped_default_keeps_a_deep_recursion` closes the blind spot
the audit found next to it. `run_with_stack` pins `WF_WORKERS=1`, so no test
measured recursion depth in the world an unconfigured `--par` binary actually
runs — the world the original frame-slot defect lived in. It pins a floor, not
a parity: at an 8 MB limit the default reaches past 160 000 frames and fails by
180 000, so the case asks for 60 000, clear of drift and well under what a
fourfold frame regression would leave.

The records carry the rest. Batch 0076 now states the invariant breach it
disclosed but did not name as one — `wf_par/1` moved outside the 1.20x band on
three w192 cells, 1.239x to 1.267x — and attributes it to L1's runtime edit
rather than the counted-loop landing, which byte identity excludes. 0075's
superseded Dig 7 headline, its withdrawn grant-counter margin and its inverted
pool-on ceiling are corrected in place. Four durable documents that later
landings falsified are superseded where they stand, the gap-hunt verdict table
gains dispositions, and the repository gate's disposition and the audit summary
close 0076's bookkeeping.

## f7127c03 2026-08-23 compiler: actualize a permitted counted loop as a range split

A counted `for` the [PAR-2] judgment permits now lowers, in the overlapped
world only, to a recursive split of its own index range over the runtime
that already exists. Two synthesized functions carry it: a chunk, which is
the loop itself seeded by its first parameter, and a splitter, whose two
recursive halves are an ordinary overlap group. Nothing about the hand-out
changed — the claim, the frame, the thunk, the deque, the join, and the
two-world selection are the ones a permitted pair already used.

The leaf of the split is the loop and never one iteration. Emitting the
recursion literally costs the body the vectorization and unrolling the loop
gave it and pays 2N-1 activations for N iterations: measured 7.6x and 3.6x
slower than the plain loop on light and mid bodies, at every worker count.

The sequential world calls the chunk's own clone, so it runs the code the
loop always had, behind one call its only caller inlines back. Each world
resolves its labels against its own overlap set, which is the eabefcc8
lesson honoured by construction rather than repeated.

How far the split descends is one runtime query per loop *entry*, never per
iteration: `wf__par_split_budget` answers from a lane count settled once per
process, this thread's own deque occupancy, and the caller's static weight
estimate over the emitted IR. That a schedule may depend on any of it rests
entirely on every admitted combine being exactly associative, so the number
of chunks is not observable; a table test states the two-sidedness of every
identity element the seeding uses.

Two declines are compile-time and reported rather than silent: a lane frame
that cannot hold the captures, and an accumulator whose site value is an
address. `hi <= lo` is tested before any width arithmetic, at the site and
in the splitter both, so an inverted range folds nothing instead of
descending into a range near 2^64.

The recursion depth is the allowance and not the range: ten frames for any
loop up to 2^64 iterations.

Verified: 74 of 74 standalone corpus, bench, and probe sources emit
byte-identical modules against 0314c01e in the default compilation and under
`--par`; the four that differ are `--par` only and are exactly the programs
carrying a loop the rule permits. No default compilation moved one byte.

## d7098ffe 2026-08-23 compiler: overlap a correct program, latch a defective one's trap

A claim is the writer's lemma, not a runtime test a program is expected to
fail: a false executed claim is the sole writer-reachable language runtime
contract violation, so an execution reaching one is erroneous and the program
is defective. Both permission judgments were refusing to overlap correct
programs in order to keep such an execution's [DIAG-3] record stable, which is
the wrong side of that trade. The owner's chartering direction of 2026-08-23
withdraws it.

The claim-free actualizability gate is deleted from the window judgment and
from the loop judgment, and with it the whole call-graph machinery it needed:
the closure walk, the reachability precomputation, the claim witness, and the
PermittedNotActualizable verdict class. Every other condition is untouched,
including the one place a claim still refuses — written between the two calls
of a window, where it is an exit-bearing interposed form.

What replaces the gate is a mechanism rather than an argument. wf_trap takes a
process-wide latch before its first byte; the winner writes its complete record
and aborts, and a thread that loses parks. So an erroneous execution still
produces exactly one well-formed record under any interleaving, and which claim
it names is the only thing a schedule may now select. The control in
trap_latch.rs defeats that branch and gets two records, so the cases have teeth.

Eleven pairs across 776 sources move from not-actualizable to eligible, three
of them in tests/programs; no denial moves and no loop verdict moves anywhere.
par_layout is granted 12 617 lanes at four workers where it was granted 6 128,
publishes the same bytes at every worker count, and runs 2.4x faster at the
shipped default. Its --par build at one lane is 1.19x slower, which the record
flags with what the experiments ruled out; the default build is unmoved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## dc84ce52 2026-08-23 bench: attribute the nine-cell bal regression to code placement

The 2026-08-23 rotation's nine slow `bal` cells are not added work. Two
things the prior entry got wrong: the tips it compared, and the mechanism.

`baseline-20260822/`'s recorded HEAD is `1e103492`, not the pre-rebase tip,
so the rebase was never the span in question — across it the linked `bal`
executables are byte-for-byte identical. And over the real span the emitted
`--par` modules for `bal`, `skew`, and `grid` are identical except one
comment line carrying the specification version.

What changed is 196 bytes of never-called runtime that `ddf1d139` appended
to `par_runtime.c`, which shifted every hot symbol by exactly +196 and left
every data symbol in place. Linking the older runtime with 196 bytes of
unexecutable `.space` padding reproduces all nine cells and every control
inside 3%; the reverse padding returns the tip to the old times. A 4-byte
pad sweep puts 2 of the 16 alignments in the pathological set, worth
1.18x-1.28x, so each link draws a 12.5% chance of the slow one.

The five matched-worker losses are that draw: at the fast alignment all
five read inside the unresolved band. The zero-losses invariant therefore
gets the band caveat rather than a repair — there is no defect to fix, and
padding the runtime back to a lucky offset is the corpus-keyed codegen
batch 0076 already declined. `-falign-functions=64` removes the
sensitivity and is recorded as an available remedy, not adopted.

## f089aa4f 2026-08-23 backend: probe every generated frame on its way down

A frame larger than the guard region must touch each page as it descends.
Without that the first store of a large frame can land past the guard, in
whatever is mapped below it — and under the pool, lanes are packed 36 KiB
apart, so what is mapped below is another lane's live stack. The write then
succeeds silently. That is memory corruption reachable from an accepted
program, which is a stronger defect than the bare segfault the exhaustion
work set out to address.

Clang gives every C function it compiles the target's `probe-stack`
attribute; the emitted Whitefoot module carried no function attributes at
all, so `par_runtime.c` was probed and every Whitefoot function was not.
This gives every generated definition that attribute, naming the host C
compiler's own helper.

The pass runs over the assembled module rather than at each `define` site.
Containment is a completeness property — one unprobed large frame is enough
— so the emission establishes "every generated function" structurally,
including definitions added later, instead of relying on each site's author
to remember.

Measured on this Darwin host, where the ABI mandates probing and the helper
is therefore already linked: all 42 corpus executables and all 176
observable rows are byte-identical to the pre-change compiler's, because
the backend emits the walk only past the page threshold. On a program with
a 338 KiB frame the prologue gains the `___chkstk_darwin` call the
pre-change binary lacked.

Also lands the batch record and promotes the six-dossier research synthesis
as the floor's design authority.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 178d4f69 2026-08-23 backend: give exhaustion a stack of our own and a defined death

Two halves of one floor, which ship together because a handler without a
per-thread alternate stack made the worker case worse rather than better.

The ceiling was the environment's. A program's depth limit was whatever
`ulimit -s` happened to leave it, so the same binary on the same input
succeeded in one shell and died in another. `wf__floor_run` now runs the
entry on a thread this compiler sizes, and `@main` is a trampoline that
hands the program to it. Measured: with the environment's limit cut to a
megabyte, a two-million-frame recursion completes; the pre-change binary
dies at exit 139 with nothing on stderr.

Running out was a bare host signal. A guard-page hit now writes one fixed
record and aborts. Both fault signals are taken, because an entry overflow
arrives as SIGSEGV and a lane overflow as SIGBUS — a SIGSEGV-only
disposition would have missed every worker overflow, which is precisely the
class the parallel default introduced.

The record is the resource class and nothing else. Two unrelated
constraints force that and agree on it: a signal handler may reach only
async-signal-safe facilities, and [PAR-1] requires observables to be
identical under every permitted schedule. The absent fields are the point —
no rule_id, no function, no node path — because exhaustion violates no
contract the writer could have kept, and a record that attributed it to
source would be claiming something untrue.

Every fault that is not ours is put back exactly as it was: default
disposition restored, instruction re-executed, same signal, same status,
same core dump. A diagnostic that made a wild pointer and a deep recursion
look alike at the point of death would be worse than none.

The entry moves to `@wf__main_body` so the floor's translation unit can
call it, and the tests that read the entry's optimized shape follow it
there with their assertions unchanged. The module keeps a weak fallback so
`--emit-llvm` output is still a complete program; the call in it carries
`noinline`, without which a small enough program is pasted into the
fallback as a second copy of itself.

All 176 corpus observable rows are byte-identical to the pre-change
compiler's across both modes and four worker settings. The floor costs
+0.078 ms per process and +65,560 bytes of peak footprint, none of it the
reservation: an 8 MiB thread and a 4 GiB thread measure the same, and so do
a 16 KiB and a 64 KiB alternate stack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## feef8658 2026-08-23 backend: say which resource ran out when an allocation is refused

An allocation the host refuses was a bare abort with zero bytes on stderr —
the same observable event as a false claim and as a corrupted-heap abort
inside the allocator, with nothing to tell a reader which had happened. The
four refusal edges now reach one `@wf_resource_abort`, which writes
`{"resource":"heap"}` and aborts.

Nothing new carries the bytes. The trap writer was already a general "write
these, then abort, exactly once in this process" primitive, so the heap
record reuses it and its latch; what widens is the condition for emitting
them, from "this module has claims" to "this module writes a record". The
two classes sharing one writer is what makes "no execution produces both
records" a mechanism rather than an argument.

The record names the resource class and nothing else, for the same reason
the stack record does: no rule_id, no function, no node path, because an
allocation the host refused is the trusted computing base reaching its
limit and not a contract the writer failed to keep.

Nothing is added to any success path. The branch was already there; only
the target of its cold arm changed.

Two edges are deliberately left alone. The enum-discriminant abort is a
compiler-invariant failure rather than a resource one, and sweeping it in
would blur the distinction this record exists to draw. Each buffer site also
carries a target-domain ceiling guard, which the specification already
calls a resource-failure path but which is a different condition from an
allocator refusal — naming its class belongs with the clause work, not here.

Measured with an allocation the optimizer cannot delete, since at the
shipped level it otherwise removes the request and the refusal edge with it:
the record is exactly its twenty bytes, and a forced-false claim in a module
that also allocates still writes exactly its own record.

## 23279a52 2026-08-23 backend: pin the behaviour the frame probe buys, not just its presence

The existing cases check that every definition carries the attribute and
that ordinary programs are byte-identical without it. Neither says what
happens when a frame actually is larger than the guard region, which is the
whole reason the attribute is there.

This adds that case, and with it closes the reproduction the research left
open. That work demonstrated the hazard on IR whose only difference from
clang's own output was the stripped attribute, and said plainly that it had
not driven it from Whitefoot source. Now it has been: the same program, at
the same depth, compiled by the shipped compiler and then rebuilt with the
attribute ablated from the one recursion, carries identical frame
arithmetic to the instruction — three hundred kilobytes per activation in
two `sub sp` — and differs only by the page walk before the drop. Probed, it
dies at the guard with its record, ten times out of ten. Ablated, it exits
0, ten times out of ten: it runs with frames past the end of its own lane
stack, finds what it touches mapped, and returns a normal answer for a
computation that never fit.

That is the failure the attribute closes, and it is worse than the segfault
this batch set out to replace, because nothing about the run says anything
happened.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## dc8cf1a3 2026-08-23 backend: take the compiler's own recursion off the destruction path

A recursive nominal implied recursive drop glue. `wf.drop.tN` called
itself once per level of the value, so a program with no recursion in its
source could build a structure successfully and die destroying it — after
it had already spent its stack, in code the writer never wrote, cannot
see, and cannot instrument. Three of the five recursive corpus programs
dragged it.

The rule is a property of the type graph, not of a name or a shape. Build
the cleanup graph — a type's drop reaches its fields' drops, its box
referent's, its buffer element's — take its strongly connected
components, and a drop is recursive exactly when its type sits in one. An
edge that leaves a component can never come back, so its depth is bounded
by the type and it keeps the straight-line expansion it has always had.
Only the owning-indirection edges *inside* a component move to a heap
worklist, which is why every program whose ownership is a chain emits the
module it emitted before: 19 of the 22 corpus units are byte-identical,
and the three that change are exactly the ones with recursive `box`
types.

Design, argued rather than assumed:

The worklist is heap-resident because the heap is what the traversal is
releasing. One entry is a kind and a pointer; the block it names is at
least as large and is released as the entry is taken, so the list cannot
outgrow the structure it is dismantling. A host that refuses to grow it
writes the heap record through the latch every other refused allocation
already uses.

An entry releases its block *before* dropping the content it took out of
it. That is the one deliberate reordering and it is what keeps the
pending list the size of the traversal's frontier rather than the depth it
has reached — a left spine holds one entry, not one per level.

Reclamation order is checked against [STOR-3], not asserted. The
specification fixes order in exactly two places: reverse declaration order
among the bindings a scope exit releases, and ascending index order among
buffer elements. Neither moves — the call sites and the buffer helper are
untouched. Within one value the release action is compiler-owned semantic
data, and every memory-reclamation action carries the empty effect row, so
what does move is unobservable. One reachable shape is the exception and
is recorded in the batch record rather than hidden: an enum that declares
a system-resource field after a recursive box field has its [SYS-5]
releases run shallowest-first instead of deepest-first.

A `buffer` in a cleanup cycle would need a second traversal shape and no
program can reach one — a nominal recursive through a buffer has no
selected target layout and is refused before emission, on this compiler
and on the one before it. `DropPlan::of` refuses that case as a compiler
invariant, so lifting the layout limitation cannot quietly bring recursive
glue back.

Measured on `drop_deep.wf`, whose source contains no recursive function:
at 35,000,000 levels the pre-change build writes {"resource":"stack"} and
aborts; this one completes in 1.5 s at 2.25 GB. At 100,000,000 levels it
still completes. All 96 observable rows across eight programs, two worlds
and six worker settings are byte-identical to the pre-change compiler's.

The regression walks the emitted module's own drop-glue call graph and
fails on any cycle, so a new nominal shape is covered without extending a
table; it fails against the pre-change compiler. A second case fails an
emitter that put every program on a worklist, and a third runs the
traversal end to end.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 1a9b4c45 2026-08-23 backend: give a lane the stack the entry got

A stolen call is an ordinary Whitefoot call. It may recurse exactly as
deep as it would have on the thread that offered it, and it starts at the
bottom of the stealing lane's own stack rather than continuing the
offerer's. So the size of a lane's stack decides, on its own, whether a
steal is headroom-positive or headroom-negative — and lanes were asking
`RLIMIT_STACK` with an 8 MiB floor while the entry had been given a stack
the runtime owns. A steal lost two orders of magnitude of room, and the
same binary on the same input either finished or died depending on which
thread got there first: measured on a two-million-deep recursion, 11 of
30 runs at two workers, 3 of 30 at eight, 4 of 30 at the shipped default.
[PAR-1] survives that — overlap-resource exhaustion is outside its
observables — but "does my program run" is not a thing a schedule may
decide.

A lane now takes the entry's own constant, exported from the floor rather
than repeated, so "the same number" is a fact about the program instead of
a comment in two files. No thread has less room than the entry has, the
deepest any schedule reaches is at least what the no-steal schedule
reaches, and the probe above is 30/30 at every worker count 0/1/2/4/8/16
and at the default.

Asking the environment was the other half of the defect: it put a `--par`
binary's ceiling back in the hands of the shell that launched it, which is
exactly what the entry's own stack was introduced to end. `RLIMIT_STACK`
is now consulted nowhere.

The residual was looked for, not assumed away. A schedule that splits a
deep chain across two lanes has more total headroom than one that does
not, so a band could exist above the single-thread ceiling where liveness
is still a race. Bisected at a million levels: 22M completes 10/10 and 23M
fails 0/10 at four workers and identically at sixteen, and 23M fails 0/30
at two and at sixteen. The boundary is (1 GiB - 6 KB)/48 B — the
overlapped clone's own frame, a division rather than a distribution — so
no band appeared on this shape. A lane holds a bounded number of
outstanding offers, so the top of a recursion is stealable and the rest of
its depth belongs to one thread by construction.

Sixteen lanes reserve 16 GiB of address space between them and it costs
nothing measurable: `par_layout` at sixteen workers reads 1.95 MB peak
against 1.80 MB, at identical wall time, and at four workers the two are
within fifty bytes. The pages are untouched.

Two cases said something that is no longer true and now say what is. The
lane-record case identified a lane death by depth, which only worked while
the two ceilings differed; it runs past the common ceiling instead and
holds every run to the same standard. And the shipped-default depth case
has been vacuous since the entry stopped honouring `ulimit -s`: its
comment now says so and names the instrument that replaces it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 87afd8db 2026-08-23 backend: report what a level of stack costs and how many the program gets

A frame size is a whole-program, optimizer-chosen property. Nothing about
reading a function tells anyone what one activation of it costs, and
nothing about reading a program tells anyone which of its functions can
still reach themselves once the inliner has finished. The flagship program
in this repository is the evidence: `walk` caps its directory recursion at
sixteen levels and documents that the truncation is indistinguishable from
a complete search. Its frame is 1744 bytes and the stack holds 615,677 of
them. The bound was not careful, it was blind.

`--stack-ledger` prints one line per frame, one per cycle, and one per
acyclic chain, on the same non-normative developer channel as
`--par-ledger`: no acceptance judgment, no lowering change, and nothing
that can touch a mandatory record.

It is measured after codegen because nowhere earlier has the numbers. The
compiler does accumulate a frame size during target qualification, and on
the deepest recursion in the corpus that accumulator reports zero bytes for
the function that ends the program: its real cost is the ABI frame record a
non-leaf is forced to keep plus the spills the register allocator chose,
and neither exists before LLVM runs. So the bytes come from
`-fstack-usage`, the call graph from the assembly of that same compilation
— the post-inline graph the numbers belong to — and the cycles from Tarjan
over it.

A `--par` module carries two lowerings of every recursion and its bootstrap
picks between them at startup, so one number would be wrong in one of the
two worlds. Both get rows, paired through the emitter's own clone spelling
rather than a guess: `wf_spine` at 48 bytes a level against
`wf__par_seq_spine` at 16. That side-by-side is where a default-build depth
regression is visible before it ships rather than after.

Compiler-generated drop glue is in the ledger like anything else, and it is
now a negative result: a recursive-nominal program has `wf.drop` frame rows
and no `wf.drop` cycle row. A cycle row coming back means the destruction
path is descending the stack again, and a case fails on it.

The regression is the ledger against the machine. It takes the depth the
report claims, builds the program at 0.999 and 1.001 of it, and runs both:
the first must complete and the second must not. Measured across frames of
16, 10,272, 34,848 and 291,760 bytes, the first failing depth sits at most
1,136, 2, 0 and 0 levels from the report, the largest being 0.0017% of its
own ceiling. The research's `(stack - 6144)/frame` model has lost its
constant term along the way and the ledger does not carry it: 6144 was
argv, environ and auxv at the top of the process stack, and the entry does
not run on the process stack any more.

Two things are deliberately not what the design sketched. The ledger runs
its own clang instead of putting `-fstack-usage` on the link, because that
flag writes its report beside the file it compiled and would drop a `.su`
into whatever directory the writer asked for output in — and the call graph
needs assembly the link does not produce. One compilation into a directory
the driver owns and removes gives both, consistent by construction, and
none of it runs unless the flag is passed. And the loop splitter's rows
read as ordinary cycles rather than as the bounded ten frames they provably
are, because saying so would need the compiler to annotate the recursions
it creates, and inventing that channel for a report costs more than the
report is worth. It is the one place this ledger is wrong in spirit, and
the module says so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 5c95580d 2026-08-23 backend: say which limit refused a buffer, not just that one did

Both `buffer.rs` sites carry two abort edges. F4 routed the allocator
refusal to a record and left the other one — the dynamic target-domain
guard — calling `@abort` with zero bytes, because naming its class is a
specification decision and not an executor's.

It gets its own class rather than the heap's. The specification keeps the
two apart wherever it names them: [DIAG-1] lists resource failure and
target-layout failure as separate members of one non-rejection sum, and
:719 routes this guard down the same non-continuing path without merging
it into the resource class. Same death, different condition — the byte
count has no exact value in the target's domain, and a host with more
memory refuses it identically, so a reader told `heap` would go and look
at the machine's memory for a failure that was never about memory. An
arena folds into `heap` for the opposite reason: it is that one supply
refusing.

Measured on ten quintillion u8 — inside `buffer_fits`'s ceiling and
outside the target's, which is the whole reachable band of that guard —
exit 134 with zero bytes becomes exit 134 with exactly the record.

## 04f119ef 2026-08-23 backend: reclaim a cleanup cycle that closes through a buffer

The traversal shipped with only its `box` arm, on the stated ground that a
`buffer` inside a cleanup cycle was unreachable. It is reachable: `box`
supplies the indirection the target layout needs while the buffer stays in
the cycle. That program compiled and ran before the traversal existed and
was refused here with a bare compiler-invariant failure.

A buffer's elements need an order a box's single content does not. [STOR-3]
fixes each element's drop in ascending index order followed by the one heap
free, so the step pushes the block's entry first and then the elements from
the last index down; the last-in first-out worklist takes element 0 first
and the free last. Nothing resumes.

## 453f40e8 2026-08-23 backend: tell a wild fault from a stack running out by the probe's geometry

The handler read any fault within a megabyte below a thread's stack as that
thread running out. A megabyte is roughly sixty-four page strides and about
128,000 times the distance a real overflow lands at, so a corruption fault —
a read as easily as a write — was converted to exit 134 and a resource
record, which is the one thing this file's header says a diagnostic must not
do. The band is now one page-walk stride plus the ABI red zone, which with
`probe-stack` on every definition is the whole set of addresses a descent can
reach.

The non-guard path also restored SIG_DFL and returned. That swallows a signal
with no faulting instruction behind it and leaves the disposition restored
process-wide while the classification is per-thread, so one external SIGBUS
disarmed the floor for the rest of the run. It re-raises now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 5b460bdd 2026-08-23 backend: give the whole process one record latch instead of one per writer

"Exactly one record" was serialized per writer, not per process. The floor's
signal handler latched the stack record; the emitted module latched the trap,
heap, and target-domain records. Two threads dying of different resources
each won their own latch and each wrote, so two records could interleave on
one channel — which is the thing the sentence exists to rule out.

The floor owns the latch now and exports its address; the emitted writer asks
for it, falling back to one of its own through the same weak definition that
already covers a module linked without the floor's translation unit.

## 09247ef6 2026-08-23 docs: say what a permitted overlap does to a resource death, not what it cannot

The recipe asked the owner to transcribe a guarantee: an overlap "may not
lower [the call depth] below the depth the source-order execution reaches, so
taking the permission cannot turn a completing execution into an exhausted one
by depth alone." One command falsifies it against the binary in the same
packet. The two clones of a call do not cost the same per activation — 48 and
16 bytes a level on the tip's own ledger — so between 22.4M and 67.1M levels
the same binary completes at WF_WORKERS=0 and dies at 4.

Exhaustion is a [SCOPE-3] resource condition either way and not a [PAR-1] or
[PAR-2] observable, which is what both rules already say of the resources
overlapping spends. Edit 1 extends that to the program's own two supplies and
promises no ordering. Digest, extent, and every citation count recomputed;
grammar verifier re-run.

The record's F7 mechanism argument goes with it: a waiting thread runs stolen
work from its own depth through wf__par_wait, not from the lane bottom. The
liveness matrix stands as measured and a twin-chain probe found no failure.

## 39195bca 2026-08-24 backend: make the lane count an atomic, not a plain word two threads share

A review the owner relayed found the pool-start path rewriting
wf__par_lane_count after worker threads were already reading it in their
steal loops: a plain write racing a plain read, which the C memory model
calls a data race whatever the values. The finding is correct and the
runtime is trusted computing base, where the language's no-data-race
promise is upheld by hand. All seven access sites become relaxed atomics;
a sweep found no second bare shared word in either runtime file.

ThreadSanitizer never reproduces the racing schedule here (the parent
reaches the rendezvous lock first in every observed run, ordering all
later worker reads), while a minimal analog in which a worker signs in
first fires 5/5 — so the declaration carries the invariant and the batch
record carries the investigation, and no test that would have passed
before the fix is added.

## db543775 2026-08-24 semantic: judge the loans argument borrows hold, not only the uses rows declare

The window and loop judgments projected only effect rows onto footprints,
so a borrow whose callee row said nothing contributed nothing: two
statements each taking &uniq of one place with read-only rows were
permitted to overlap, a pure shared borrow was permitted to overlap the
move that frees its referent, a loop whose every iteration takes &uniq
of one outer cell was permitted and actually split, and a body statement
binding a bare borrow of outer storage was the same hole one layer down.
Each shape puts two usable exclusive borrows of one place, or a write
under a live shared borrow, into one moment — states [OWN-5] never
admits at one program point and [OWN-9] licenses the optimizer against.

Every borrow-moded argument now also contributes its loan, keyed on the
parameter's mode and resolved through the existing place machinery, and
the judgment applies [OWN-5]'s own matrix to loans against the other
statement's loans and uses: an exclusive loan excludes everything
overlapping, a shared loan excludes writes, two shared loans coexist.
Loans are judged before uses, so a denial cites the cause rather than
the row projection downstream of it. An unresolvable borrow actual
denies. A non-call window statement that forms a borrow refuses the
window, and a loop-body statement that forms one refuses the loop
unless every borrowed place is storage the iteration itself introduces —
the checked tree erases a written borrow's mode, and an unloaned borrow
would widen permission, but a borrow of iteration-own storage needs no
loan at all. The loop judgment gets its own loans path and denial: an
iteration's exclusive loan on storage it does not introduce denies,
while shared loans stay free, keeping read-only sharing across
iterations permitted.

ConflictKind becomes the product of its two halves over five footprint
elements. Measured across every ledger line the corpus produces and a
differential sweep against the pre-change compiler: permitted pairs,
loops, chains, and splits are unchanged; the only diffs are
already-denied pairs whose cited reason is now the loan.

Research and adversarial verification: two Opus research agents, a
completeness audit, and a post-landing differential attack (probe suites
under the operator's scratch directories); every load-bearing claim
re-verified by the lead on the real compiler. Batch record:
docs/ongoing/0081-loan-column.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

matrix against the other statement's loans and footprints, with the

requires of the union loan state exactly what [OWN-5] requires of one

direction, demanding obligations between two intervening statements that
