## 75c97e0b 2026-08-27 io: repair completion lowering and the Linux link

Two independent defects each stopped a permitted overlap from building.

`block_exit_label` predicts the label an incoming block will end at, because
the emitter writes a block's phis before it writes the blocks that reach it.
It modelled the eight ordinary block-opening constructs but not the direct
completion hand-out, so a window in any block whose successor carries block
parameters named the plain `bbN` header while the block in fact ended at
`par.done`. Every such module was invalid LLVM: a window inside a `match` arm,
a `loop` body, or an `if` did not compile at all, and only the straight-line
entry bodies the existing tests use were unaffected. It now replays the
completion queue exactly as emission drains it, and the ordinary constructs
moved into `definition_exit_label` so both hand-out mechanisms and the plain
operations read as one list.

`bridge.c` declared a union member named `linux`, which GNU C predefines as an
object-like macro outside a strict dialect. The repository gate compiles the
completion runtime as `-std=c11`, where the member is an ordinary identifier;
the driver named no dialect, so clang's `gnu17` default expanded it and no
Whitefoot program that touches I/O could link on Linux. The member is renamed,
and the driver and the backend test link both name `-std=c11` so the gate's
green is a statement about the shipped link.

Regression tests: one builds and runs a window before a block join under
`WF_IO_HELPERS` 0, 1, and 4 in both lowerings; the other syntax-checks every
compiler-owned C unit in the host compiler's default dialect, which is the
half of the matrix the gate had never compiled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 8f06cbd6 2026-08-27 io: measure completion at the program level and fix what measuring found

Spec v0.37 activated the completion I/O model on C-level component
evidence alone. This measures whole programs against the best
hand-written native shape and against Whitefoot's own sequential build,
on macOS and on Linux with io_uring.

Three lines per workload, all publishing the same checked bytes: N the
best native C shape, S the same Whitefoot source built --no-overlap, C
the same source built the way it ships. On a many-independent-files
workload C is 2.05x S on macOS and 2.41x on Linux, and lands within 3.4
percent of a hand-written io_uring pipeline at the same queue depth the
source can ask for. The remaining distance to a deeper native shape is
source width, not protocol cost: overlap groups are runs of consecutive
calls in one basic block, so the natural one-file-per-iteration loop
emits no submissions at all and measures like its sequential build.

Measuring found three runtime defects:

- A scheduler waiting in the completion join refused to park while the
  target queue held anything, and with helpers it cannot execute that
  work, so it spun. macOS default user CPU 266 ms to 60 ms.
- An unset WF_IO_HELPERS pinned one helper, the worst measured setting
  for a program with width. The policy now grows on queue pressure up to
  the machine's CPU count, and starts at zero where a native ring is
  ready. macOS default 838 ms to 475 ms; Linux 171 ms to 121 ms.
- bridge.c declared a union member spelled `linux`, which the host
  compiler predefines as a macro in the dialect whitefootc links with, so
  every Linux link of a completion program failed to compile. The
  repository's own probes use -std=c11 and never saw it.

Adds whitefootc --no-overlap, without which the sequential reference
line cannot be built, and the measurement bundle at
research/experiments/io-completion-bench/, which is deliberately not
reachable from make check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 727194fe 2026-08-27 entailment: stop rerunning identical counterfactual analyses

Semantic checking of tests/programs/wfgrep.wf cost about 25 s in the gate
profile. Counters over the closure engine locate the cost precisely: the
term table is small (91 terms at most), so the ENT-4 closure is not growing
with program size, but 82 of the 102 whole-function analyses are
bit-identical repeats of an earlier one and carry 83 % of the 2.46 billion
transitivity triples the check evaluates.

CLM-2 asks, once per claim component, whether the program still checks with
that component blinded, and answers by rerunning the entailment analysis
over the whole concrete inventory. The walk reads its claim mask at five
points; three consult only whether a mask is present, and the two that read
the mask's identity both require it to name the function being analyzed. The
analysis of a function no mask names is therefore one value shared by every
masked rerun.

CounterfactualReuse keeps that one value per function beside the exact
published-postcondition context it was computed under, and hands it back
only to an untargeted function whose context still compares equal. The
ledger's interning index becomes a derived accelerator that a clone leaves
behind and rebuilds from its own nodes, so the counterfactual reruns stop
copying one large hash table per function. Inside the closure, the
transitivity fixed point skips a triple whose premises have not changed
since it was last offered, the live bound and proof maps are rebuilt once
from the settled matrix instead of on every accepted candidate, middle-term
membership becomes a dense index, and the private interning map gets a
deterministic word hasher.

wfgrep.wf: 29.07 s -> 7.43 s CPU (median of five, interleaved), 3.9x. Peak
footprint 5.9 GB -> 4.5 GB. Short of the 5x target; the remaining cost is
the ENT-4 transitivity pass itself, proof interning, and the two inventory
clones each rerun still makes.

No verdict, diagnostic, ledger line or derivation moves: the complete
observable output of the compiler -- stdout, stderr, exit status and emitted
LLVM IR under --par --par-ledger --stack-ledger -- is byte-identical to the
pre-change compiler on all 623 sources in tests/programs, tests/codegen and
tests/conformance/cases.

Three regression guards assert the mechanisms rather than a wall-clock
number: interning into a cloned ledger keeps the original identity, a
strengthened bound still propagates in a later closure round (verified to
fail when the freshness rule looks back zero rounds), and a reuse entry is
refused for a changed published context.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## f67b2d81 2026-08-27 permission: put a consumed system `own` argument in the written footprint

[PAR-1] forms a call's written footprint from its row's `writes` paths together
with the places its consumed `own` arguments name. `user_call_footprint` pushes
that consumed-own write unconditionally; `system_call_footprint` pushed it in
an `else` of the row test, so a parameter the row mentions at all took the
row's path instead. Every row in the current catalog names its consumed `own`
parameters under `writes` or under neither, so both branches happen to produce
the same footprint and no accepted program changes. The uncovered shape is an
`own` parameter under `reads` and not `writes`: it would contribute a read
element and no written one, and a read element does not deny against another
statement's read footprint or shared loans, so another statement could read the
place alongside the consume.

There is no reproduction to write and no behavioural test to add, because no
catalog row reaches it; a test would pin the catalog rather than the checker
and become rot the moment the catalog changed. The guard is that the two
footprint functions now say the same thing, which is what the rule says.

Batch record moves to docs/done: findings, the differential matrix across
WF_WORKERS x WF_IO_HELPERS on macOS and Linux, per-platform sanitizer results,
and the flagged design gap.

## e27b13a0 2026-08-27 io: make opens and closes completion operations

Opens dominate a many-small-file workload and neither an open nor a
release reached a completion path, so both cost a blocking syscall on
the scheduler while the ring or the helper pool carried only transfers.

Linux: an open is IORING_OP_OPENAT, its kind check is a further
IORING_OP_STATX of the descriptor the open produced, and a descriptor
the check refuses is disposed of with IORING_OP_CLOSE on the same ring.
A close is IORING_OP_CLOSE. The typed outcome is unchanged because the
rule deciding it now lives once, in the shared typed file contract, and
both adapters answer with it.

Every backend: the bridge no longer keeps a helper pool layered over
the adapter's own, so one enqueue announces one request to one helper
under one lock instead of four lock round trips and a broadcast; the
pool grows when a submission finds no helper waiting, rather than when
the queue has already outrun the pool, which is a condition a short run
of independent operations almost never reached; and a resource release
is handed to a helper where one exists, because its outcome is
discarded by the language rule and nothing waits for it.

Adds the eight-wide many-files program so the comparison against a
native pool and a deep ring is made at a matched width.

## a1d073ac 2026-08-27 io: remove the two policy changes measuring worse than what they replaced

Both were proposed on evidence from a machine under heavy load, and both
are refuted by the same programs measured on a quiet one.

Growing the helper pool when a submission finds no helper waiting never
fires: a helper signalled but not yet scheduled still counts as waiting,
so a run of consecutive submissions sees an available helper every time.
The four-wide program ran 919 ms against 625 ms for the queue-depth rule
it replaced. The depth rule is back, with the refutation recorded where
the next reader will look.

Handing a resource release to a helper is neutral, so it does not earn
its mechanism. The 17 us per close that justified it came from closing
8,192 descriptors held open at once; in the pattern a program actually
uses, one open at a time, the same close costs 3.7 us against a 116 us
open, and the measured before and after agree within one percent at
every pinned helper count.

## f141d1e1 2026-08-27 io: decide an open's kind where it costs one syscall, not one round trip

The kind check that makes an open typed was written as a linked
IORING_OP_STATX of the descriptor the open produced, which keeps the
reaping thread free of host calls. Two ring round trips cost more than
the open they wrap: on the two-CPU Linux container the eight-wide
many-file program ran 152 ms against 116 ms for the bounded adapter it
replaced, and the four-wide one 203 ms against 140 ms.

Reading the mode of a descriptor the kernel has already produced is an
inode read that cannot wait on anything, so it is one fstat where the
completion is reaped. The same programs then run 119 ms and 141 ms:
parity with the path they replace, with the blocking openat gone from
the scheduler thread. A refused descriptor is disposed of by the same
single close the direct path makes, on an error path where nothing is
waiting for throughput.

The whole stage machinery goes with it.

## 79b29665 2026-08-27 tests: re-observe the default pool's steal over bounded runs

`wf__par_grants` counts steals, and a steal is a scheduling event: a pool
thread must be given a CPU before the offering lane finishes the work itself.
Under a saturated host (two full gates running at once) the default-setting

Checking tests/programs/wfgrep.wf held five complete inventories of

array whose widest variant occurs 349 times in 2.3 million nodes. Peak
resident memory was about 3.1 GB for 1400 lines of source.

accepts, in what order, or with which proof:

- the PRV entry points take borrowed function slices, which removes the

## d085133b 2026-08-27 io: judge and lower a call written in match-scrutinee position

[PAR-1] judges calls, and a `match` scrutinee is a call. The judgment reached
one only through `CheckedStatement::Let` and `PropagateLet`, and
`IrBuilder::lower_statements` recorded a call's landing site only from the
`Let` arm, so the same two operations got different work depending on how the
second one was spelled: with a `let` binding before the match, the emitted
module carries one `wf__completion_file_write_submit` and one join; with the
call written directly as the scrutinee, it carries none, and the permission
ledger reports nothing at all.

A candidate is now built from every written call position, and a site's
identity is its call occurrence rather than the binding a statement happens to
define — a scrutinee call defines no binding, so a binding cannot be the
identity. `PermissionSite::binding` becomes optional, `wait_for` names calls
by `NodePath`, and `call_results` is keyed the same way.

One recorded fact separates the two positions and the existing window rule
does the rest. `result_read_by_own_statement` says the statement's own
remainder — the dispatch and the arm it selects — reads the call's result, so
`judge` starts the interposed window at the scrutinee's own statement instead
of after it. That statement is then classified exactly as any statement of its
form is, and a match statement is a form this judgment does not project, so a
scrutinee call denies as a window's first member without a rule of its own. It
can only ever be a run's last member, which is what the IR requires: a group's
members must be defined in one block and a scrutinee's dispatch terminates
its block.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 903a5b6d 2026-08-27 io: give a submitted open its own path bytes, and publish its release

A submitted open outlives the call that formed it. The bridge stored the
caller's pointer in the request, the bounded POSIX adapter copied that pointer
into its queue entry, and the Linux ring copied it into the SQE, where the
kernel keeps it until the name is resolved — while the caller has already
regained its buffer and may rewrite it. Both adapters were resolving storage
they did not own. No shipped program hits it today only because one call site
holds at most one hand-out and the emitter's staging buffer is not written
again before the join; the barrier that hides it is what the loop pipeline
removes, and the failure mode is a silently wrong file rather than a crash.

Both records now carry the bytes. `wf_file_work` and
`wf_linux_io_uring_entry` each hold `path_storage[WF_FILE_PATH_CAPACITY]`,
stage the name into it at submission and repoint the request at the copy; a
work record is copied whenever it moves, so `wf_file_work_bind_path` rebinds at
every copy and the invariant is that a record's open never names bytes outside
itself. The capacity is 1024, which holds the widest admitted component
(Darwin's 1023) with its terminator. A name that does not fit is refused before
an operation is claimed, so the caller falls back to its direct open, which
resolves its own buffer inside its own call; no generated open can reach that
path. These are the only two backends that stage a path — the Windows IOCP
adapter carries transfers only and an open there goes through the same bounded
POSIX adapter.

That makes [SYS-2]'s `loan-released(path)` true rather than aspirational, so
both adapters now publish it. `wf_completion_publish_milestone` is a new
non-terminal route: it accumulates one milestone fact of an operation the
target is submitting or already holds, writes no result byte, does not move the
phase and raises no completion event, so a one-shot operation still has exactly
one event and exactly one terminal. It refuses `WF_COMPLETION_TERMINAL`
outright — a terminal fact without the result bytes it stands for would let a
consumer read an empty slot.

Both tests were falsified before being trusted: with the staging removed the
harness fails at `marker == 'A'` on macOS and in a Linux container with
io_uring required, and the ring probe fails on
`entry->request.buffer.path == entry->path_storage`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 87712a96 2026-08-27 io: index every completion storage element by its outstanding operation

Each per-site completion storage element — the token, the result slot, the raw
value and error, an open's outcome, a directory cursor's position, and the
staged path component — was a bare entry-block `alloca` shared by every
hand-out of that site. The element belongs to one outstanding *operation*, not
to one written call: the target writes the result into it and reads the staged
path out of it while the operation is in flight, so two operations of one site
that are outstanding together need one element each.

`indexed_entry_slot` reserves `count` slots of one type in the entry block and
returns element `index`; storage and element pointer are both entry-block
definitions, so the name dominates every block exactly as a plain `entry_slot`
name did. Every site the current lowering produces answers one, because a
schedule is submitted and joined inside the block that formed it — which is why
one shared element has never been wrong, and exactly why it would become wrong,
silently and without a compile error, the first time a schedule outlives its
block. The count and the index are now the whole of what a deeper schedule
changes.

Nothing a writer's module compiles to moves: LLVM folds a `[1 x T]` alloca and
a constant-zero `getelementptr` back into the bare alloca, and every program in
the bench corpus emits byte-identical arm64 assembly before and after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 2c342009 2026-08-27 tests: fix what the Linux gate found, and state the limits it cannot fix

The first Linux run of the canonical gate stopped in five distinct places.
Three are defects this repository could not see from one host:

- `stack_ledger` read the call graph out of assembly while stripping only
  Darwin's comment markers. On x86-64 ELF a function label is written
  `wf_spine:  # @wf_spine`, which does not end at the colon, so no label
  resolved, no instruction had an open caller, and the ledger reported a real
  recursion as a chain with no cycle. This is the shipped ledger, not a test.
- The deterministic-target host unit uses `S_IFREG`, and the link names
  `-std=c11`, under which glibc withholds the set that macro lives in. Every
  compiler-owned C unit already asks for its own feature set; this generated
  one did not.
- The offset-fault fixture's `__linux__` arm called `pthread_getattr_np`
  without `_GNU_SOURCE`. That arm had never been compiled.

Two are tests that read one optimizer's choices as if they were the rule:
`system_io` rejected any surviving `@wf.sys.` symbol, which catches the
SYS-7 error-class mapper that clang 18 leaves as a call and clang 21 outlines;
and the wfgrep cost census had no row for `@exit`, which this machine's clang
hides inside `@wf__main_body.cold.5` and the CI macOS runner does not.

The rest are host limits, now declared instead of failing:

- The wfgrep cost census and the directory-source completion case need an
  approved SYS-14 enumeration row, which Linux deliberately does not have.
- A steal is only observable with a core per lane; the three-core macOS runner
  reaches zero over the whole sample where every four-core host reaches one.
- The alias-versioning fingerprint is LLVM's memcheck shape for one target.
  Measured: rustc 1.96.0, 1.97.1 and 1.98.0 all reproduce it on
  aarch64-apple-darwin, so the precondition is the target, not the version.

The stackless migration observation now links once and samples ninety-six runs
instead of linking sixteen times.

## 19e5fa56 2026-08-27 semantic: stop the counterfactual cache from carrying a published summary

An adversarial review refuted this batch's claim that none of its five
changes can alter a derivation, and found a second defect the corpus
cannot reach.

The reuse entry lent its analysis to a rerun's inventory and reclaimed it
after the SCC scheduler had stamped a published FN-9 summary onto every
postcondition proof of a component it published. The copying version it
replaced cached the value before that loop, so it always held
`summary: None` — what the analyzer emits. `proof.summary` builds
`verified_postconditions` and `verified_postcondition_proofs`, which are
both the analyzer's context and the reuse key, so a rerun whose component
did not publish still saw an earlier rerun's summaries: on the review's
program `delta`'s counterfactual arena was 39 nodes instead of 30.
`reclaim` now clears the stamp, so the entry holds the analysis.

`InternIndex` tracked absence with a `stale` flag that `Clone` recomputed
from the original's entries, so a clone of a settled ledger — and, at the
base revision, a clone of a clone — was born looking freshly finished and
re-interned a node the arena already held under a second identity. The
flag is gone: absence is read off the ledger, so every dropper is owed the
same replay. `settle` also no longer shrinks `roots`, the one vector whose
capacity survives `finish_with_event_roots` and reaches the [DIAG-2] byte
metric.

Three guards cover the two defects and fail without the repairs. The
record adds a derivation-level oracle: a temporary probe fingerprints
every function's arena — node, edge, root and event counts and a hash of
the DAG's identities — and base 79b29665 and this branch agree over all
623 corpus sources plus the review's program, where the unrepaired branch
does not. The byte metric is unchanged with `settle` disabled.

## 2094da6b 2026-08-27 par: judge the staged loop permission as [PAR-3]

[PAR-2] divides an index range and recombines one accumulator, so its unit is
a subrange: it needs a trip count, a compiler-owned binder, and an enumerated
exactly-associative operation set, and it admits only a `for_stmt`. A loop that
does I/O needs a different overlap and none of that apparatus. Its unit is the
iteration the statement graph already gives.

[PAR-3] cuts the body of any `for_stmt` or `loop_stmt` at its first
`may-suspend` submission into a prologue P and a remainder E, and admits
executing E(i) against P(j) for j > i and against E(j) for j != i. Two schedule
sentences carry it. Prologues run in index order and never overlap one another,
which is what admits `reserve_file`'s short unique `&uniq FileFactory` loan with
no replication and no [OWN-5] relaxation. Every write E performs to storage
rooted outside the body occurs in iteration order, which is what admits
`set sum = sum +wrap digest` with no associativity, no identity element, and no
combination tree — strictly more general than [PAR-2]'s accumulator apparatus.

The judgment is `semantic/staged_permission.rs`. Every footprint and every loan
is [PAR-1]'s, including the loan column; the four dispositions are [OWN-5] and
[OWN-7] read over the two segments; the cut is a real dominator and
post-dominator query on the body's own control-flow graph, with post-dominance
taken against the normal exit only so an early typed exit lands in the prologue
and the exit condition decides it. It reads no entailment fact, and a test over
three routes to the same subscript proof pins that.

This batch is the judgment alone: no lowering, no runtime change, no measured
number, no published byte moved. The ledger prints a `stage` line per loop that
does I/O and a `place` line per classified place, and a denial names the
condition, the place, and one admitted writer form. `docs/patterns.md` P15
teaches that form.

Stage one replicates only storage the body itself constructs, so the hoisted
`many_files_narrow.wf` is denied and the new byte-identical
`many_files_loop.wf` is granted. The W1 residual — a body that returns on its
first I/O error gets no pipeline — is recorded in the batch record, not solved.

Spec v0.38 activates [PAR-3] as one added rule, 137 to 138, with no grammar,
operation, type, or spelling change; [PAR-1] and [PAR-2] each gain one
cross-reference sentence and no condition. v0.37 is archived byte-exact, the
chain and every digest anchor name v0.38, and conformance coverage moves to
138/138 with seven maintained shapes. Canonical `make check` is green.

## 45ef81f0 2026-08-27 compiler: charge every frame the return address x86-64 does not report

The Linux gate found the stack ledger over-promising recursion depth by a
factor of two: it reported 134,217,728 levels of the tight spine on the
one-gigabyte runtime stack and the program died at 134,083,510.

`-fstack-usage` reports what a function allocates for itself, and the two
qualified architectures put the return address on opposite sides of that
line. Compiled from one module for both targets, `wf_spine` reports 8 bytes
on x86-64 with a prologue of `pushq %rax` — the caller's `call` pushed the
return address above that and it is not in the 8 — and 16 bytes on arm64
with a prologue of `stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!`, which stores the return
address inside the 16. One activation costs sixteen bytes on both machines;
only the reporting differs. Every frame now carries that difference, so a
row is what one activation costs and the level count divides by it.

Over-promising depth is the dangerous direction for this artifact: a writer
who believes it writes a recursion the machine cannot run.

A new case states the arithmetic from a synthetic stack-usage report, per
architecture and without compiling anything, so the eight bytes are pinned
in the frame row, the cycle row and the division alike. It reads the
architecture from `std::env::consts::ARCH` rather than repeating the
ledger's own `cfg!`, so a ledger that added the bytes on the wrong machine
fails it.

`the_shipped_default_keeps_a_deep_recursion` bounded the overlapped world by
a multiple of the sequential clone, and that multiple did not survive its
second host: the same lowering costs 48 bytes an overlapped level on both
architectures, against 32 a sequential level on arm64 and 16 on x86-64, so
it reads as a ratio of 1.5 on one and 3 on the other and the bound of two
was a fact about the arm64 register allocator. The bound is now the overhead
itself — six machine words against a measured two and four — which is a
property of what the claim keeps live across the call.

## e0865a24 2026-08-27 tests: sample a grant observation wide enough to be about the runtime

The three-core macOS runner totalled zero grants over the default pool's five
runs in one gate run and was granted a lane on the first run of the next, so
five runs were sampling that host's schedule rather than the runtime's
behaviour. A steal is a scheduling event: the offering thread can finish the
work itself before any pool thread reaches the offer, and on a busy machine it
often does.

Both existential grant observations now sample `GRANT_OBSERVATION_RUNS` runs
of one linked module. A runtime that grants nothing still totals zero over all
of them, so the assertion is unchanged in what it refuses; it costs one link
and a fraction of a second more to stop refusing a host.

does about a target that cannot compile part of the corpus.

## 9b13bf44 2026-08-27 io: enforce the per-site completion storage invariant and close the batch's verification notes

Two independent verifiers confirmed batch 0089 and left notes. Each is closed
here with the smallest change that makes the record and the code say what is
true.

The count of one outstanding operation per completion site was a written
assumption. It is now a precondition the emitter checks:
`completion_storage_element` refuses a hand-out whose site already has an
operation in flight, with a `BackendFailure` of its own rather than
`InvalidIr`, because the IR is not malformed — it asks for a shape this
emitter has not been taught to reserve storage for. Nothing today can reach
the refusal (`emit_terminator` joins every outstanding hand-out before it
writes a terminator, so a site cannot be re-entered while its operation is
live), so the case that proves it injects the shape:
`duplicate_outstanding_completion_call_for_test` emits one submitted,
unfinished completion call twice in place. The shape test is renamed to the
claim it actually makes.

`system.rs`'s `%component` buffer, which the design named alongside the
completion slots, stays a bare per-wrapper buffer: its only host call is the
synchronous direct open, which leaves nothing outstanding. The reason is
written at the `alloca` and carried as a residual for batch 2.

Two verdict changes outside the bench corpus are now recorded rather than
merely true: `wfgrep.wf` gains two correct `PAR denied` lines, and a call
written as an `if` condition — an `if` checks into a `Bool` match — is a
[PAR-1] candidate for compute overlap. Two tests pin the positions the batch
opened and did not cover: a `ValueMatchLet` scrutinee, byte-checked under
`WF_IO_HELPERS` 0/1/4, and an `if`-condition compute group, byte-checked
under `WF_WORKERS` 0/1/4. Neither shape forms at all under the base compiler.

The Windows sentence in 903a5b6d was imprecise: `file_adapter.c` is POSIX-only,
so an open there does not go through it — that target has no submitted-open
route at all. The record says so, and `windows_completion.c` gains the
milestone route `contract.h` declares for every target, so the core contract is
uniform; `completion-windows-cross` passes with it.

The pre-existing `independent_io_reaches_the_second_operation_before_the_first_unblocks`
failed on four gate runs across three people, always under load and never in
isolation. Its assertion is unchanged and its three-second bound becomes sixty:
the parent holds the child's stdout pipe blocked for the whole wait, so what the
case proves is an order and the bound is only a liveness cut-off.

No emitted byte moves: over the 22 corpus programs that compile standalone plus
the two new probes, the module and the ledger are byte-identical to c34a2d48.

is not a race, still runs everywhere.

## 25ac56ef 2026-08-27 tests: let the offset-fault fixture own the memory below its stack

The Linux gate of 7ec7bc1a failed
only_a_fault_within_the_probe_stride_is_read_as_an_exhausted_stack on its
four-page row with exit 0: no signal, no record, nothing faulted. The write
four pages below the floor's entry stack found a writable page. The floor
maps its 64 KiB alternate signal stack after the entry stack, and the
kernel's top-down search drops it into the first gap below the stack block;
/proc/self/maps in this project's Linux container shows the rw-p mapping
directly under the ---p guard. The container's guard is 64 KiB, so it never
loses the row; x86-64 glibc's guard is one page, so there the row is lost
whenever the alternate stack has taken that spot, which the runner did once
in ten gates. The floor classifies faults and no fault happened, so this is
neither a floor defect nor a host limit: the fixture assumed the memory
below a stack is empty, and that was never the host's to keep.

The fixture now keeps it. The fault comes from a thread the fixture creates
on a stack at the top of one reservation, attached to the floor exactly as a
pool lane is, and the thread unmaps the 16 MiB below its stack after
attaching and reading its bounds — both map memory — and just before it
writes. The pad is unmapped rather than PROT_NONE because Darwin reports a
protected page as SIGBUS and an unmapped one as SIGSEGV, and the rows assert
the host's own signal for a pointer into nothing. Every assertion is what it
was. The shipped fixture text, linked against the shipped floor, is twenty
of twenty on every row in the Linux container and correct at every row on
this machine's 16 KiB pages.

The record gains the finding, the runs of 7ec7bc1a beside their outcomes,
the twelfth bench reading, and two not-done items: the five cases that own
most of the suite's 980 s on the four-CPU runner, measured from the gate log
as the input to a follow-up on test economy, and the alternate stack's
placement under the entry guard as a floor observation for a follow-up to
weigh.

## bc4f09a4 2026-08-27 tests: size the latch control for the three-core runner

The gate of 25ac56ef lost trap_latch::the_latch_is_what_keeps_the_record_single
on macos-14. The control defeats the latch with a one-token injection and
needs one of eight runs to show both racing threads writing a record before
the winner's abort takes the process down. This ten-core machine catches it
200 of 200 runs; the three-core runner caught none of eight, after twelve
gates that had caught at least one, which puts its rate near one run in
four. The first eight runs still always happen with every caught one checked
in full; after them the loop stops at the first catch or at 512 attempts,
twenty milliseconds each here, so a host at one in four misses about never,
one at one in fifty about once in thirty thousand gates, and a host that
never catches spends about ten seconds before failing honestly. Every

## d9925ae6 2026-08-27 tests: give the offset-fault row memory it owns, and name what took it

The four-page row of
exhaustion::only_a_fault_within_the_probe_stride_is_read_as_an_exhausted_stack
failed on sampling (ubuntu-24.04) at ba95aa93 with exit 0: the write four pages
below the entry stack completed, so no fault reached the floor to classify. It
had passed on the same job one commit earlier, and the failure is intermittent
rather than caused by anything this branch changed.

The cause, measured on the runner rather than in this project's aarch64
container. A temporary diagnostic ran the pre-fix body 200 times per gate and
printed the address written, the thread's own sigaltstack, and
/proc/self/maps: 14 of 200 in run 33148142621 and 11 of 200 in run 33148390275
completed the write, and in those runs the target sits inside a 64 KiB rw-p
mapping three pages under the entry stack's one-page guard whose first byte and
size are exactly the floor's alternate signal stack — ss_sp=7fc36b9df000,
ss_size=0x10000, mapping 7fc36b9df000-7fc36b9ef000. wf__floor_attach_thread
maps it after the 1 GiB entry stack exists, so the kernel's top-down search
offers it the gap directly underneath; in the runs that pass it goes above the
stack block instead (3.8 MiB over its top in the sample) and the memory under
the guard is nothing. The 64 KiB row was exposed by the same placement; the
case fails on the four-page row first only because the loop reaches it first.

The fix is batch 0090's 25ac56ef carried over unchanged. This branch forked at
7ec7bc1a and never received it, and the fixture text here was byte-identical to
the text that commit repaired, so a second fix would have been a second shape
of the same fixture. The fixture's faulting thread now owns the memory it
writes into: one PROT_NONE reservation, its stack at the top of it by
pthread_attr_setstack, attached to the floor as a pool lane is, and the pad
below unmapped only after the attach and the bounds read. Forty runs of every
row, twice on the runner and once here, are 40 of 40 correct on every row.
Every assertion is what it was.

The record gains the finding, the maps and addresses, the rate, and the
judgment call to adopt rather than rewrite. Batch 0090's own record already
carries the alternate stack's placement forward as a floor observation and is
not edited here.

## 4a748d6e 2026-08-28 wip: cut the per-operation cost of the Darwin helper path

Five changes, all in the completion runtime and none in the language:

- a drain that returns at once when nothing is published, and a drain of one
  named token for the thread that is waiting on it, so consuming a completion
  no longer costs a compare-exchange sweep of the slot array;
- an epoch announcement that takes the wake lock only when a sleeper exists,
  ordered against the two park paths by sequential consistency rather than by
  the lock;
- a queue entry moved out by the fields the request uses, so a read no longer
  copies a kilobyte of open-path storage inside the queue lock;
- a submission that wakes a helper only when one is actually asleep, counted
  under the lock the sleeper announces itself with;
- a bounded look for a completion before a joining scheduler announces sleep.

And the helper policy: start with no helper and add one only when the queue
has outrun the pool *and* the adapter's own measured host-call time says the
operations wait, with the ceiling the bridge's operation bound rather than the
machine's core count.

## 2fead577 2026-08-28 runtime: issue the helper wake outside the queue lock

A pthread_cond_signal under the queue lock wakes a helper whose next act is to
block on that lock, so the submission pays a system call to start a thread it
then stalls. The enqueue decides the wake under the lock, where the sleeper
count is exact, and the submission issues it after the unlock; a helper that
woke on its own in between only makes that signal spurious, which its
predicate loop already tolerates.

The pool-growth cases waited for the queue to empty, which is not an answer: a
helper takes a request out of the queue before it executes it, so the wait
raced the helper and failed about twice in twenty-five runs under the address
sanitizer. They wait for the completion event now.

## 96bb4778 2026-08-28 runtime: leave a positioned read where it was stated when nothing waits

When the bounded adapter holds no helper, has nothing queued, and has measured
its own operations as not waiting, a submitted read is executed by the very
thread that submitted it — at its join, after a queue crossing, a claim, four
slot transitions and a drain. Declining the submission leaves the caller the
ordinary direct call the emitter already emits for a refused one, which is the
same host call without any of that.

Only a positioned transfer is declined, and that is the liveness argument: an
offset is meaningful only on a seekable object and the typed opens that
produce one admit nothing but a regular file, so a positioned read waits on
storage. A non-positioned read or write may be waiting on something the same
program has to do, so those keep the queue. A read of nothing is left alone,
and a written WF_IO_HELPERS declines nothing: it pins the route with the count.

Every direct execution is timed by the same adapter, so the measurement keeps
running on the route it declined a submission in favour of and a program whose
reads start waiting is submitting again within a few operations.

The harness pins the route when its invocation did not name one, because its
bridge cases assert which route an operation took and that is otherwise the
runtime's choice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## f574cdaa 2026-08-28 runtime: let a publication name the slot the next drain should look at

A scheduler harvesting on everybody's behalf cannot know where an event is, so
it compared and exchanged its way across a window of the slot array to find
one. On the macos-14 runner that was 52 slot probes for every operation the
eight-wide read program completed, and the largest single cost of the path
with the pool off. A publication names its own slot; the next drain tries that
first and, when it was the only event outstanding, does not sweep at all.

The hint is advisory in both directions: a stale one costs one compare-exchange
and a missed one costs nothing, because the sweep is unchanged behind it.

It does change which of two pending events a bounded drain answers with, which
is not a promise the core makes. The one harness helper that had come to rely
on it now drains the token it names, which is what a joining scheduler does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 266acf4f 2026-08-28 runtime: drop the drain hint that reached outside the scan budget

A publication named its own slot so the next drain could try it before
sweeping. The saving was real but the reach was not bounded: the named slot
is wherever the last publication happened, and a drain took it whether or not
it lay inside the window `scan_budget` describes.

`wf_completion_drain` promises to drain at most `scan_budget` slots, and the
writer-scheduler probe pins what that promise is for. It publishes on slot 16
of 17, drains with a budget of 16, and requires the answer to be zero: a
bounded scan that stops short of a token must not make that token's dependent
writer frame runnable. The hint drained the slot and released the frame, so
the probe exited 56. The native adapter probe failed for the same reason from
the other side — with two events outstanding it drove them to terminal in
turn, and a drain that answered with the newest published rather than the one
the sweep would have met left the named token unconsumed.

Both are the same defect: the hint was not a reordering inside the bound, it
was an escape from it. Making it legal would mean hinting only into the window
about to be scanned, which is the sweep it was meant to skip.

The cost it targeted was measured before this batch's own direct
specialisation landed. Fifty-two slot probes an operation was the zero-helper
warm read path, and that path no longer reaches the bridge at all: a
positioned read with no helper, nothing queued and no measured wait is
executed where it was stated. The remaining sweeps have the zero-ready-events
early return in front of them. So this removes an unmeasured saving that cost
a stated bound, and restores the harness helper to the sweep it was asserting
before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 529edae9 2026-08-28 runtime: the named drain refuses a token whose slot was reused

wf_completion_drain_token was the only token-named entry that did not
compare the token's generation with the slot's.  A slot outlives the
operation that used it, so a retired token names whatever operation
reused its slot -- and because this entry takes an event rather than
reading one, the consequence is a live operation's completion consumed
by an owner with no claim on it, leaving the real owner waiting for an
event that no longer exists.

The generation and the take are now decided together under the slot's
publication lock, which claim and publish already hold, preceded by a
relaxed no-event load so a join loop's usual answer still costs one
load.  The harness case fails on the previous runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 7015d1b4 2026-08-28 runtime: the adapter's readiness is published, not merely written

Batch 0096 routed every *_direct entry through wf_file_execute_timed,
which reads the adapter's `initialized` field.  A direct entry runs no
once-control of its own, so that read is unsynchronized against
wf_file_adapter_init writing the same field on the thread making the
process's first submitted operation -- a data race a two-thread probe
reports under ThreadSanitizer:

  Write of size 4 ... wf_file_adapter_init file_adapter.c:614
  Previous read of size 4 ... wf_file_execute_timed file_adapter.c:473

The field is now atomic: one release store at the end of init publishes
the whole record, and every reader takes it with an acquire load, which
is the only cost the warm direct path pays.  Init assigns its fields
instead of memsetting them, because a bulk write over the flag would be
the very write the atomic exists to exclude.

The bridge's readiness flags are the same class -- pread_submit reads
wf_bridge_helpers_pinned and wf_bridge_file_ready before it reaches any
once -- and are now atomic for the same reason.

The helper cap is also bounded by the helper storage the adapter was
initialized with.  The growth rule writes helpers[held], so a cap above
that array's length was a pthread_create past its end; the storage
length is now carried and the cap clamped to it, and an initial count
above the storage is refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## e3dd1d44 2026-08-28 io: run the bridge on the helper policy a program actually gets

Nothing in the tree reached the shipped default route.  harness main
pins WF_IO_HELPERS for any run that did not name one and completion-test
names 0, 1 and 4, so the demand-driven pool and the declined positioned
read -- both new in this batch, and both choosing between two routes for
one writer-visible operation -- were covered by no test at all.

bridge_default_probe.c is that arm: four lanes and sixteen thousand
positioned reads of a fixture whose byte at offset o is o % 251, with
WF_IO_HELPERS unset and refused if set, asserting only what a writer can
observe -- every read delivers the byte at its offset, whichever route
the bridge chose -- plus a watchdog, because a route decision that
deadlocks reports nothing if the test simply hangs.

It is wired to completion-test and completion-sanitize, and it gives
io-hosts a thread-sanitizer run over the bridge: the core/read probe
links neither the bridge nor the writer scheduler, so every thread the
delivered runtime starts was outside the existing TSan step.

A failed clock also ends the join spin now.  wf_bridge_monotonic_ns
answers zero when clock_gettime fails, and the spin's only bound is a
clock reading, so the deadline was never reached and the join spun
instead of parking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 7b9b447e 2026-08-28 runtime: state the shutdown precondition and the decline check's cost

The submission path announces its queue entry after releasing the queue
lock, so a shutdown concurrent with a submission destroys the condition
variable the submitter is about to signal.  That overlap was already
unsupported -- the bridge's only shutdown is its atexit handler -- but
the precondition was nowhere written, so the entry now carries it, with
what closing the window would cost and why no caller needs it.

The decline check takes the queue lock for its 'nothing queued' term,
which is a lock and unlock on every positioned read that reaches the
question.  Said at the entry rather than left for a reader to find.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## f4e51b4b 2026-08-28 runtime: a half-built adapter is never a usable one

Init now clears the readiness flag before it writes any other field, so a
record left half built by a mutex or condition-variable failure cannot be
read as ready.  The bulk memset used to do that as a side effect; assigning
the fields one by one, which is what keeps the flag out of an
unsynchronized write, took the side effect away with it.

A refused open handed the ledger a reading of its own queue taken before
the ledger's lock was held, and the ledger then decided under that lock.
A submission landing in between made the reading stale, its wake passed
before the waiter reached the lock, and the process stopped with a helper
asleep and work in the queue.  The queue is now a callback the ledger
calls where it decides, and a thread that will run that queue does not
sleep while an item is in it.

## 8a18f654 2026-08-28 io: quiet the denied-loop notes under --no-overlap, and teach the buffer form

Two owner decisions on observations batch 0100 recorded and left open.

B5: an ordinary compile has printed every denied I/O-loop verdict to stderr
since 0099, and a build that wrote `--no-overlap` printed them too. That flag
has already said this build takes no overlap lowering, so a loop without a
pipeline is the build it asked for rather than news about the program. The
decision is by the flag, not by the text of a line: `io_notice_report` returns
the lines to print and returns none of them under it. `--par-ledger` is
untouched and prints the whole report under every lowering. Pinned by
`a_no_overlap_build_reports_no_denied_io_loop`, which compiles one
denied-output-loop source the three ways, asserts the notes are present by
default and under `--par` and absent under `--no-overlap`, and asserts the
three modules and the three verdict lists are identical -- the judgment is
pure, and a denied loop reaches the host through direct calls either way.

D1's writer half: `docs/patterns.md` P18 teaches the explicit form. Where a
writer would hold a `&uniq` resource inside a loop body, the loop holds a
buffer instead, each iteration folds its line into it with an element `set`,
and one write after the loop publishes it. The denied form's condition-3 line
and the buffered form's `permitted` line are quoted byte-exact from the branch
compiler; a helper that takes `&uniq` of the page is denied by condition 4
instead, which the entry states. The runtime half -- a final-stage write under
in-order commit -- belongs to 0095 Stage B and is untouched.

## 2e856290 2026-08-28 CLM-1: discharge a selector's frame at the merge that joins its edges

The first cut of this judgment deleted frame discharge outright. That is
right for merges downstream of the construct and wrong for an enclosing
loop head, whose entry state predates it: with the frame retained, the loop
head attributed its own selection to a match that had already reconverged,
and tests/programs/wide_scan.wf lost a claim v0.38 admits.

A frame is now dropped at the merge that joins every edge its selector
produces, after that merge has read it. For an exhaustive reconvergence and
a counted loop with no escaping edge that is v0.38's condition verbatim.
For a match whose arms all break to one loop the joining merge is the
loop's exit, so that discharge moves there: walk_loop and walk_counted drop
every frame their own exit merge acquired.

waiter running another operation keeps its place and its claim on a returned

## b0ee45d5 2026-08-29 io: the wake accounting says what was measured, not what was hoped

The announcement rule's closing sentence claimed as many wakes as there
are answers. It is false: an announcement is edge-triggered, and an aside
that comes back demotes the waiter it promoted before that waiter can
ask, so 1,000 aside cycles announce 1,000 times and hand out no answer.
The property that holds and is measured is that no route spins. Stated
that way in contract.h, at defer_begin, and in the record.

Two record wordings corrected beside it: coming back from an aside is
the only announcing candidate left silent for being answer-weakening,
not the only answer-weakening movement; and the base's zero is 0 fresh
parks with every park it reached stale, not every turn of its loop.

file_adapter.h's shutdown-precondition paragraph still said the decline
check takes the queue lock. On this branch queue_count is _Atomic and
wf_file_adapter_queued is a bare atomic load, which is what the ledger
callback requires. Both that paragraph and the cost note above it now
say what this branch's code does, and the record tells the integrator to
resolve batch 0105's version of the same paragraph toward it.

## 66bac2fc 2026-08-29 io: the interleave probe says which refusal it met

A shortfall reported by this probe was not actionable: it said only how
many opens published. It now records each open's errno and separates two
refusals. EMFILE is the refusal the repetition arranges out of its own
narrowed table; ENFILE and ENOMEM refuse an open the three descriptors
it frees would have satisfied, so the repetition never asked the
question and is reported as not asked rather than counted either way. A
shortfall whose every refusal is EMFILE stays a hard failure.

The failure line now carries what a reader needs: each errno, the
descriptors this runtime gave back during the repetition, the
re-attempts the ledger granted, and whether the host would still hand
out a descriptor after every open had published.

## 7a46c369 2026-08-29 record: the interleave probe's rare shortfall, measured and named

Round 8 guessed the machine's file table was refusing one of the probe's
opens under load. Measured over 220,000 repetitions, that is wrong:
every loss is EMFILE from this process's own narrowed table, the
machine's table held 97 to 153 files of 1,644,353, and an open made
while the table was still narrow succeeded every time, so a descriptor
this runtime returned was left unclaimed. It happens unloaded too, one
repetition in 60,000 against one in 7,000 under load.

The record now says where it comes from: an open whose first host
attempt takes a returned descriptor never becomes a waiter and spends no
award, so the ledger can award a descriptor that is already gone, and
the waiter that takes that award spends its one re-attempt on nothing.
All 18 losses whose re-attempt count was recorded had four or fewer;
none had five, which is the shape where no open takes a descriptor
outside the award system.

## d38e4af5 2026-08-29 io: a returned descriptor is promised to exactly one consumer

The interleave probe's rare shortfall was the award mark being told two
different things and neither of them all of the truth.

The mark reopened on every waiter that found the order empty, back to a
`seen` its own attempt had read — and on the ring that is the moment of
submission, long before the kernel refuses the open and longer still
before the refusal is reaped.  Refused opens therefore arrive late and
one at a time, each finding the order empty because the one before it
has left to spend its award, and one returned descriptor was awarded to
three of them in turn.  The mark now only ever rises.

An open the host satisfies takes a descriptor whether or not it ever
waited for one, and it was charged for nothing, so a return it had
carried off was still on offer to a refused open.  Every satisfied open
now reports it, on all three routes, with the re-attempt a waiter makes
on an award charged once rather than twice.

Four scripted harness cases, and the shipped probe now checks the
ledger's promise beside its count of published opens.

## 6bcb68b5 2026-09-02 Pin the ordinary-loop backedge guard contract

Investigated the report that an ordinary `loop ( invariant ... ) { }` header
wrongly fails its Backedge obligation when the body increments a cursor under
a source guard. The rejection is not an implementation defect: it is what the
active specification's fixed AUTO family yields.

A source guard such as `ilt(cursor, limit)` is an ordinary L0 relation over
the mutable cursor place. The increment's own SET-1 commit kills every fact
whose support names that place and establishes only ENT-3.S5's applicable
post-write image, which an arithmetic right-hand side does not have. The
L0-to-affine index that ENT-6 gives AUTO's final route is an ephemeral view of
the current difference-bound state, explicitly not a published affine premise,
so nothing relates the pre-write cursor image to the limit on the backedge.
Only an invariant conclusion is a theorem over immutable value images, which
is why INV-1 states that a complex backedge is stated by an `invariant_stmt`
on the reaching body path where its local premises are live.

The counted form behaves identically for the same source shape; a counted
header works only because its compiler-owned binder is never written by the
body, so the S11 true-header bound survives to the backedge while the target
is rendered over the `binder + 1` image. Ordinary and counted headers are
therefore already symmetric, and no compiler behavior changed here.

Added the coverage that was missing for that contract: unit tests for a
published guard discharging a guarded cursor increment, an unguarded increment
failing at Backedge, an unpublished guard failing at Backedge, a body
invariant after the write coexisting with a proved header, and a break-only
body leaving the preservation batch vacuous; plus one runnable conformance
case for the accepted ordinary-loop guarded-cursor form.

## 639e7c09 2026-09-03 Render an invariant-free loop header on one line

FORM-2 broke a `for` header apart unconditionally, so a counted loop with
nothing but its binding still cost three lines. The break exists to set
`header_invariant` clauses on their own lines; with no invariant there is
nothing to set apart, and the three-line spelling only made the common
counted walk harder to read.

A `for` whose header carries no invariant now renders `for (i in a..b) {`
and `for @label (i in a..b) {` on one line, and that one-line form is the
only canonical one. A header with one or more invariants keeps the existing
layout: `for (`, one item per line at depth plus one with a comma after all
but the last, then `) {` at the original depth. An ordinary `loop` is
unchanged — no parentheses without invariants, the same multi-line header
with them.

The gap builder now counts `header_invariant` children rather than all
header items, and marks the header breaks only when that count is nonzero;
the space before `(` is marked either way, since it overrides the generic
right attachment in both forms.

Every Whitefoot source in the repository whose `for` header has no
invariant is rewritten to the one-line form: 33 `.wf` files under
`tests/programs/` and `tests/conformance/cases/`, the embedded sources in
20 Rust test and driver files, and the examples in `docs/patterns.md` and
`docs/current-plan.md`. Prose in `docs/` that called the counted header
multiline is corrected to describe the invariant-carrying form. One driver
ledger assertion follows its fixture's shifted line number.

Pre-v0.41 `.wf` records under `research/experiments/` keep the older
paren-free header; they do not parse under the current grammar either way
and are left as the dated evidence they are.

## 842efa4f 2026-09-03 Admit the integer tightening of an accumulated affine candidate

A written certificate and the automatic route could form 2*(mid - hi) <= -1
for a binary-search midpoint but never divide that inequality, so the halved
relation mid < hi stayed unproved and the subscript was rejected.

Every affine atom denotes a mathematical integer, so an accumulated
k * v <= u with a positive integer k dividing every coefficient also proves
v <= floor(u / k) with the floor taken toward negative infinity. The checker
now forms exactly two such factors for one candidate and its target -- the
multiple relating the two coefficient vectors, and the greatest common
divisor of the candidate's coefficients -- and checks the ordinary DIRECT
residual against each tightened candidate. Both factors are read from the two
vectors in checked i128 arithmetic; no factor is searched for, no premise is
added, and the fixed candidate families are unchanged.

[PRF-1]'s final residual and every AUTO family route through the one new
helper, so the certificate and the automatic route admit the same integer
consequence. The specification states the step in [ENT-6]'s AUTO description
and in [PRF-1]; no rule is added or removed. New unit tests cover the divided
vector, the floored bound at its exact boundary, a candidate no factor
divides, an unrepresentable divisor, the midpoint certificate, the automatic
midpoint bound, and a signed certificate whose halved bound is negative and
odd. Two conformance cases run the proved midpoint index.

## 548ca477 2026-09-03 Skip an unrepresentable integer-tightening factor instead of aborting the list

`integer_tightenings` propagated both factor derivations with `?`, so an
`ArithmeticOverflow` while reading or verifying the target-multiple factor,
or a capacity failure while dividing it out, abandoned the whole list and
suppressed the coefficient-divisor candidate that could still have been
representable. Under [ENT-1] and AUTO's tightening rule an unrepresentable
candidate is skipped and may not suppress another candidate.

Derive and divide out each factor on its own, keeping the fixed order
(target multiple, then coefficient divisor) and the existing deduplication.
The function can no longer fail, so it returns the candidate list directly;
the single caller drops its `unwrap_or_default`, and no `?` can reintroduce
a whole-list abort.

Three unit tests cover the skip: a candidate whose target-multiple
verification overflows i128 while the divisor candidate succeeds, a
candidate whose multiple and divisor are both unrepresentable and yield a
plain empty list, and a tightening that exceeds a checker input capacity.

## d9943da9 2026-09-03 Give a set commit the value image its let spelling has

An ordinary loop whose body incremented a cursor under a source guard was
rejected at the [INV-1] backedge when written `set i = i + 1_u64;`, and
accepted when written `let j = i + 1_u64; set i = j;`. One value, two
spellings, two verdicts: the commit's image depended on the statement's shape
rather than on the value's, which the compiler rules forbid.

The cause was in the entailment walk of a `set`. The target kill removed the
guard relation `i < n`, and only [ENT-3.S5]'s three-row copy image was
established afterwards, which an arithmetic right-hand side does not have, so
nothing related the new value of `i` to `n`. The `let` spelling worked because
the binder gave the value its own term before the kill, letting [ENT-5]'s
pre-kill closure carry `j <= n` across the write.

A commit now evaluates its right-hand side to that occurrence's own commit
value: a compiler-owned [ENT-2] term identified by the statement's NodePath
and the value's fragment type, which source cannot name and no event kills.
The `let` sources and the commit share one routine over that destination —
image, closure, kill, then the S5 equality naming the value — so every S5, S6,
S7, and S9 row a `let` initializer receives, a commit receives. Wrapping,
saturating and checked forms therefore receive exactly what they receive at a
`let`, and nothing more: an unproved wrapping range still leaves the value

## 909ec42e 2026-09-03 Say what forms a commit value, and what an unimaged commit leaves

A review of the previous commit found three overreaching claims about the new
[ENT-2] commit value and one stale conformance rationale. Nothing here changes
compiler behaviour.

[SET-2] admits only an affine, region-free target, so a `replace` right-hand
side never has a fragment type and never forms a commit value. [ENT-2] clause
(f), the [ENT-5] (a) kill clause, and the doc comments repeating them
nevertheless named `replace` beside `set` as a source of one. Each now names
only an admitted [SET-1] `set` whose right-hand side has one fragment type.
Clause (a) keeps `replace` where it is true — a replace commit is still a kill
event — and only the commit-value sentence inside it was narrowed.

[ENT-3.S5] said a right-hand side matching no image row leaves v with only its
own type range, which presumes a v that is never formed: no source recognizes
such a right-hand side, so no commit-value term is interned and the commit
publishes no post-write equality at all. The sentence now says that, scoped to
S5, because a call right-hand side may still publish a receiver relation over
the post-write target through its own route. A row whose form matches while its
side condition fails is untouched and already covered by the parity sentence
above: the commit value exists and carries only its type range, exactly as the
same initializer's binder does at a `let`.

One static term per statement is sound because the forward flow visits each
statement once — a loop body once from the head state formed before that walk,
each match arm over its own statements, no statement twice — so a commit value
denotes that statement's value in the one abstract evaluation performed, as a
counted header image denotes the binder's value in an arbitrary iteration.
[ENT-2] and the `CommitValue` doc comment now state that identity discipline.

The conformance case inv1-pos-ordinary-loop-guarded-cursor still explained its
published guard by a rationale the previous commit retired: the plain `set`
spelling is accepted now, which its neighbour
inv1-pos-ordinary-loop-cursor-set-image runs. Its doc says what the case
actually shows — a writer-published body invariant on the reaching path
discharges the backedge on its own, alongside the automatic commit-value route.
The id, rules, expectation, and status are unchanged.

The regenerated identity and both transcribed digests follow the new bytes.

Tests: the specification binary 18 passed, `--lib spec` 13 passed, `--lib
entailment` 192 passed, and the conformance adapter 490 pass with 1 skip;
`make spec-digest-sync` passes.

## 808d1a19 2026-09-03 Re-close a fact state after a kill and re-emit [ENT-2] implicit bounds

`FactState::kill` and `FactState::kill_goals` removed live facts without
clearing `closed_term_count`, the marker that says the state already is its
own [ENT-4] closure. An endpoint projection also deletes the materialized
copy of the [ENT-2] implicit bounds of the killed term, including the
`len(P) = N` equality of an `array<T, N>` place, so the next query took the
closure fast path, returned the post-kill maps verbatim, and never re-seeded
that equality. Acceptance then depended on whether a join had happened to
stamp the marker at the current interned-term count: writing an array's root
binding after a join over an element read left `0_u64 < len(arr)`
undischarged, and inserting an unrelated `let` before or after the write
flipped the verdict.

Both removal endpoints now invalidate the marker, so a state that lost facts
is closed again before the next query answers. The [ENT-2] rule table moves
into one `for_each_implicit_bound`, which all three closure entry points --
the proof closure, the proof-free contradiction closure, and the fast path --
re-emit; implicit facts are a function of the term table and the place's type,
so they are regained at every query rather than having to survive in a map.
This makes the `length_term` promise in flow.rs true as written.

A killed established bound stays killed: closure over survivors plus the
implicit axioms cannot rederive it, which the new negative unit test and the
unchanged `ent5-neg-kill-on-write` conformance verdict both pin.

Evidence: 1484 lib tests pass; clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check are
clean; the conformance adapter reaches Pass=491 Skip=1 (490 before this
change, plus the case added here) and the canonical-corpus gate passes. Over a
665-program sweep only two verdicts move: the reduced repro now accepts, and
its full sibling advances past the wrong subscript rejection to a genuine
undischarged exact multiplication it had been shadowing. No accepted program
became rejected, and wfgrep.wf compiles in the same time as before.

## e19da585 2026-09-03 Report the body failure that breaks a loop backedge, not the backedge

[DIAG-1] admits exactly one rule and one location per rejection, and the
checker chose that one rejection by written position: the smallest failing
node path won. A loop-header invariant is written before its body, so its
backedge failure beat every failure inside the body — including the failure
that caused it. When a body operation cannot discharge its domain obligation,
[ENT-6] forms the binding it initializes as a fresh full-range atom, and that
demoted value is exactly what leaves the header relation unproved at the next
header. The writer saw only the [INV-1] effect and never the [OP-2], [OP-4],
or [FN-8] cause. A body-end `invariant` probe was hidden the same way, so a
probe that failed read as a probe that passed, and two separate reviews drew
false conclusions from it.

Select the reported rejection by the order in which the checker decides
obligations rather than by where they are written. Every judgment but one is
decided where it stands, so its node path is already that order. INV-1's
backedge is the exception: it is proved only after the whole loop body has
been walked, so it is positioned immediately after its loop statement's
subtree — after every failure the body holds, and still before the loop's
following siblings. INV-1's base judgment is decided at the header and stays
there, so a failed base still precedes the body failures it causes, and a
nested loop's backedge still precedes the enclosing loop's. The order is a
plain comparison over syntax child ordinals with an explicit end-of-subtree
position, and no step reads a hash.

`an_unguarded_cursor_increment_fails_the_ordinary_loop_backedge` pinned the
masked order: its unbounded `limit` made `cursor + 1_u64` fail OP-2 first, and
the test passed only because the header failure was reported ahead of it.
Bounding `limit` by a written requirement keeps that test's subject the
backedge, and its doc comment records why the bound is load-bearing.

Verified: 1483 lib unit tests pass, clippy --all-targets and fmt --check are
clean, and the conformance adapter is unchanged at Pass=490 Skip=1 — every one
of the 491 conformance cases produces byte-identical output to the previous
build. Across a 665-file experiment corpus nine rejected programs now cite the
body failure (seven OP-2, one OP-4, one FN-8) instead of the INV-1 backedge it
produced, and no program changed between accept and reject.

## 909626c4 2026-09-03 Brand every store in its type; fourth draft after falsifier round 3

A store's identity is the region that names it, and that region is a
type argument of every value taken from the store (HeapBox<'s, T>,
ArenaBox<'s, T>, PoolSlot<'s, T>, PoolVector, ArenaVector, Arena<'s,
BYTES, ALIGN>), so a value's relationship to its backing survives fields,
container elements, enum payloads, multi-return, joins and calls by type
formation alone; provenance sets remain only for the three loan-bearing
views. Reservation is an event of the region block with one reservation
point per region and a reset at exit. Disposal is one `dispose p using
(...)` statement, structural and closed under containment, and propagate
with a live linear binding is an error. Measure data are keyed on program
point, place and measure; every operation that writes a measured place
publishes each of its measures; the arena carries its extent in its
type. [CNT-5] is deleted, box_new and arena_new leave [OP-1], the
contract surface gets its own clause_expr production, seq_vacant and
`update ... into` are added, [RES-7]'s exclusion list becomes a property
test. Section 6.7 records each round-3 finding and the rule that refuses
it now. Companions brought into agreement.

## b2bbd4d7 2026-09-03 Sixth draft: inputs and outputs, derived linearity, surface proposals

Parameters are inputs and results are outputs: the &uniq container
parameters and the exit datum are withdrawn, helpers are value-in and
value-out with an ordered result list and the exchange admission of
set, and a contract relates results to inputs with no entry or exit
convention. Linearity is derived: a value whose release requires a
capability is linear, closed under containment, and no writer marks a
store-derived type; the linear modifier is for logical obligations
only, with a writer guideline. dispose is a consume and a write. The
block typestate becomes an initialized window with the prefix as its

carries a retained label and a reset transfer, and derived columns
replace hand-filled ones. A notion table states the closure property
of each notion. Every language-surface addition the design relies on
is listed as PROPOSED in a dedicated section with alternatives; nothing

## 5333a0cb 2026-09-03 Force region elision: kernel specification v0.42 candidate

[FORM-8] Canonical region spelling. A region name is written exactly
where the document does not otherwise fix the region denoted and is
absent everywhere else, so each region position has one legal spelling.
A declaration writes a region name only to relate two of its own
positions or to name a result region no input determines; every other
position is unnamed and distinct. A borrow writes its region only when
it is not the innermost region block's; a region block is named only
when the name occurs inside it; a call writes only the region arguments
no actual determines, as the leading members of its `::` application,
and no application at all when none remains. Every clause is decided
from the owning declaration's own text.

The grammar gains five optional REGIONID decisions and no production;
resolution mints unspellable synthetic regions for unnamed positions;
the checker infers determined call regions from the actuals and rejects
the other spelling under FORM-8 with the spec's restructuring text.
Every program in tests, docs and live research is respelled
mechanically: 2623 region tokens across the four test corpora become
260, all of them relating two positions or naming a result region.
Eight conformance cases pin the rule; three "wrong region-argument
count" cases retire because a rule with one legal list cannot express
that fault. The specification is a v0.42 CANDIDATE over v0.41; no
archive is written and no ACTIVE-SPEC line is added; every check stage
except the candidate's expected spec-archive-integrity stop is green.

## 6c4e30e4 2026-09-04 Loop bodies are region blocks; associative image joins: v0.43 candidate

Two amendments over v0.42. First, every loop body is itself a region
block [OWN-11]: a borrow of an outer binding inside a loop body is
written bare and lives in the body's own unnamed per-iteration region,
so the guarantee that outer bindings are written again between
iterations is unchanged; a region block that is a loop body's only
statement restates what the loop already says and is a [FORM-8]
rejection, while a block beside other statements keeps its distinct
[OWN-6] statement scope and stays legal. Second, [ENT-6]'s control-flow
join folds every delta atom an earlier join minted back into its
interval before comparing images and takes the hull, so nested
conditionals reach exactly the image one flat match over the same
branches reaches; acceptance no longer depends on the shape of the
control join, and delta atoms stay ordinary shared atoms between joins.
The corpus loses its four sole-statement loop region blocks; six
conformance cases pin the two rules; conformance Pass=512, snapshot
Pass=491 Flip=0, every check stage green except the candidate's
expected spec-archive-integrity stop.

## e047310d 2026-09-03 Adopt T4 (resource dependencies are API relations) and record the park-on-miss review

Constitution: new standing theorem T4 (owner ruling 2026-09-04). Every finite
resource a system operation consumes is an owned value in its signature,
drawn from a factory whose capacity never exceeds what the target provides;
move ordering is the only sequencing of resource use; an implementation never
waits, awards, retries, or keeps a ledger to hide an outcome the sequential
program does not produce. Test for every device API: if overlap can invent an
outcome the sequential program never produces, a resource is missing from the
API.

FIRST-PRINCIPLES §12: the permit reserves one real unit or nothing the checker
can use; the proof-only FilePermit of [SYS-10] is the stated gap, and the
descriptor retirement ledger is the measured cost of it.

Roadmap BOUND-1: the backed FilePermit is the next item, with the exact
[SYS-10] sentences it replaces and the derived work that ships with it (the
spec file itself is not edited here: that change carries the operation table,
conformance cases and the runtime deletion in one batch).

research/investigations/io-model: the park-on-miss design (PARK-ON-MISS.md)
after a seven-critic design review, with the decisions file (54 entries, five
owner rulings) and the discussion file (one open correctness issue, 56, on the
completion-record bound, awaiting an owner ruling).

## 3aaeb5d8 2026-09-04 Back the FilePermit: v0.42 candidate, credit-counted factory, explicit closes, gated pipelines

Specification (CANDIDATE v0.42 supersedes v0.41): `reserve_file` answers
`Result<FilePermit, IoError>` from a factory whose capacity is fixed at
program start and never larger than what the target provides; three explicit
closes (`close_read`, `close_directory`, `close_directory_source`) return
the credit after derived release's one close attempt; an open holding a
permit is refused a descriptor only by honest target exhaustion. [SYS-10],
[SYS-11], [SYS-14], the operation, target-contract and outcome tables, and
the META-5 delta are respelled; the derivation ledger carries the v0.42
paragraph and the T4 ground.

Compiler: catalog rows for the closes and the Result-returning reserve;
`emit_reserve_file` calls the floor's credit count (`wf__file_reserve`) and
answers the Result shape; `emit_close` performs the native close attempt and
returns the credit; qualification ordinals 16-18; the embedded spec identity
re-pinned to the candidate bytes; catalog totals updated.

Runtime: one atomic credit count in the floor (POSIX: RLIMIT_NOFILE less a
fixed reserve; Windows: a fixed capacity far below the handle limit).

Lowering: the bounded-batch driver admits prologue gates, a `match` on a
never-suspends operation whose one continuing arm holds the staged
submission and whose other arms leave the loop. An exiting arm drains the
batch in flight before it leaves, so the remainders of earlier iterations
run in source order; on a target without native completion the pending-exit
edge is unreachable. Without this every file loop would have lost its
two-slot pipeline to the reserve's Result.

Corpus: every `reserve_file` site in the conformance cases, test programs,
research programs and Rust-embedded fixtures moves to the match idiom; one
new conformance case shows a close's permit opening again; docs/patterns.md
and the roadmap describe the backed permit; docs/current-plan.md records the
batch plan.

## e60ee2ae 2026-09-04 Retire the candidate spec state and stop quoting the identity in prose

Two simplifications of the specification gate, decided by the owner on
2026-09-04 after the v0.43 and v0.44 candidates each merged to main and
each needed a zero-content activation PR (#16, #19) to turn main green.

1. No candidate state. `spec/kernel-spec.md` always declares
   `Status: ACTIVE vN` and hashes to the chain tail. An amendment lands
   in one change: the amended file, the archive of the outgoing bytes,
   the appended approval record with its `ACTIVE-SPEC:` line, and the
   regenerated `compiler/src/spec_identity.rs`. `spec-archive-integrity`
   now requires the ACTIVE status line and drops its candidate branch
   and the `spec-candidate-integrity` alias; `whitefoot-spec` parses
   only the ACTIVE form, and its candidate lineage tests go with the
   state they tested.

2. Prose stops quoting the identity. The chain tail and the generated
   identity module are the two machine-checked homes of the version and
   digest. `spec-digest-sync`, which forced six documents to quote the
   digest and an "active vN" sentence at every activation, is replaced
   by `spec-prose-integrity`, which fails when live prose quotes a
   64-hex digest or names a version as the active authority. README,
   compiler/README, WORKFLOW, current-plan, roadmap (revision 69),
   patterns, and the derivation ledger's header now point at the chain
   instead; the ledger's per-version amendment bindings are frozen
   history and stay, so the ledger is held to the phrase check only.

Also in the same spirit: `compiler/src/spec.rs` derives the version and
hash constants from `spec_identity.rs` (a compile-time hex decode)
instead of a hand-transcribed literal. The literal's test, which said
the same thing the chain check already says, is retired with that
explanation; the independent `shasum` measurement still enters through
the approval record.
