## af4033af 2026-09-04 B2: the measure terms, descriptor support, one goal disposition, const generics

Lands the containers-and-resources design's [MSR] proof surface as four added
specification rules and the compiler that carries them.

[MSR-1] makes len(P), cap(P), room(P) and head(P) [ENT-2] terms over an
admitted measure place formed with field selections, deref wrappings and
subscripts, states that a measure table exists and gives every measured type a
row with one of exact, bounded or absent per cell, carries that table as a
wf-measures fence, and fixes the logical coordinate system whose origin is
head together with its injectivity sentence. [OP-1] gains the three readers.

[MSR-2] states the support of a measure term as the place's descriptor storage
rather than its root binding, so a write to a sibling field kills no measure
and a write at an element position kills the measures of the written element
and none of the run's own; [ENT-5]'s element-position carve-out is removed
rather than narrowed. It also fixes the standing facts every measured value
carries and appends len + room = cap to [ENT-6]'s automatic affine premises.

[MSR-4] states once the complete ordered derivation of a numeric goal in six
steps and retires [ENT-6]'s per-family route grants; [ENT-6] carries one
compiler-owned immutable affine atom per live measure term.

[MSR-6] admits an in-scope const generic as a [TYPE-6] pbase and with it as an
[ENT-2] for_stmt endpoint and an [MSR-5] clause operand.

The three reader spellings are dotless and IDENT-shaped, so [OP-1] adds all
three to ReservedLowerNames and no source declaration may be spelled cap, room
or head any more. The corpus used all three as ordinary binding spellings, so
this change renames those bindings in its own sources -- room to spare, head to
front, cap to limit -- across 118 snapshot cases, 30 conformance cases, seven
tests/programs sources and the compiler's embedded test sources. Every renamed
program keeps the verdict it recorded: no snapshot row and no conformance
expectation is edited.

## aaf0b4f2 2026-09-04 B4: join-checked liveness and the one set commit

[LIV-1] and [LIV-2] are added to the active specification, and [OWN-1],
[OWN-11], [SET-1], [STOR-1], [STOR-3] and [TYPE-5] are amended in place to read
them. `set_stmt`'s target list takes a written value list beside its one call,
which is the owner's decision D2, and the grammar tables are regenerated.

[LIV-1] makes a binding's live-or-dead status a property of a program point:
every predecessor of every join and every loop head agrees on it, a
disagreement names the binding and both predecessors, and because the status
agrees, every scope-exit release is unconditional. The loop-head instance is
[OWN-11]'s per-iteration judgment over the structural backedge, which replaces
its blanket prohibition on moving an outer binding into a loop body.

[LIV-2] states one commit for one or more targets: every target is resolved
before the right-hand side, a `move` of a target place or of a place reached
through one is that target's read-out and kills no root, one target is read out
at most once, and all targets are reinitialised at one commit under three
conditions -- the dead target, whose live affine case keeps [STOR-1]'s error;
pairwise non-overlapping targets on [OWN-7]'s terms, which replaces [SET-1]'s
pairwise-distinct-roots placeholder; and exact arity and type. The compiler's
`ResultListSubscriptTarget` stop and [STOR-1]'s second restructuring are both
retired by the rule.

Nine conformance cases carry it and no corpus verdict moved: the native adapter
reports Pass=540, Xfail=1, Skip=1 and the snapshot corpus Pass=491, Flip=0.

## 0288b650 2026-09-04 B5: linearity, the release graph, and the destructuring forms

[PROV-6] is added to the active specification, and [FORM-2], [TYPE-2], [TYPE-3],
[OWN-1], [LIV-1], [STOR-3], [FN-2] and [EFF-2] are amended in place to read it.
Three grammar productions arrive with it -- `dispose_stmt`, `region_param` and
`linearity_bound` -- and three lowercase atoms, `dispose`, `linear` and
`affine`, which [FORM-3] therefore excludes from IDENT; the grammar tables are
regenerated. The added surface is exactly [S12], [S13], [S18] and [S32] as the
owner adopted them, and `dispose p;` takes no `using` list.

[PROV-6] makes a value linear in a scope exactly when it owns, at any depth, a
value whose release action requires a capability that scope does not hold or a
value of a nominal declared `linear`, and affine there otherwise. One release
graph is what the compiler-derived release and `dispose p;` both walk; `let
N(f: a, ...) = move v;` consumes a value of nominal struct type whole and binds
every declared field; a consume of a proper sub-place of a linear value is
refused unless the same statement's commit reinitialises it [LIV-2]; and a
written `affine` or `linear` bound states the class a declaration was written
for, checked at every type instantiation.

The ambient heap is the only store whose reclamation is a release in this
version and it is not a value, so every scope holds it: nothing is linear here
by the capability criterion, no walk resolves a provider place, and the
memory-reclamation actions keep the empty row. What the version does measure is
D3's visibility claim in the shape it can: a body that writes `dispose cell;`
must declare `writes(cell)`, and the same body without it declares `pure`.

Two clauses are DEFERRED with stated zero deltas. The refusal of a type whose
release graph has a cycle is stated and not enforced, because landing it
retires `tests/programs/recursive_tree.wf`, which this compiler accepts and
three live tests compile; that verdict move is the owner's disposition. The
linearity-bound check over a region argument decides nothing while every store
a region names is reclaimed by its own region release.

conformance case spelled a contract member `dispose` and a compiler test source
spelled a generic function `affine`.

## 020ffd51 2026-09-04 B7a: the brand, the runs, and the kernel declaration domain

[PROV-1], [BLK-0], [BLK-1], [BLK-2] and [BLK-3] are added to the active
specification, and [TYPE-2], [TYPE-3], [TYPE-5], [TYPE-6], [CONST-1], [OWN-1],
[FN-2], [FN-7], [OP-1], [OP-4], [OP-9], [MSR-1], [MSR-2], [MSR-3],
[ENT-3.S13], [STOR-1], [STOR-3], [STOR-5], [PROV-6], [PROG-1], [SYS-3] and
[DIAG-1] are amended in place. `struct_decl` and `enum_decl` each take an
optional `region_params` [S20], which is the whole grammar change; the tables
are regenerated from the amended grammar and no production and no atom is
added.

[PROV-1] makes a store's identity a region and puts that region in the type of
every value the store backs, so preservation is a closure property and needs no
clause: no value-forming step changes a value's type and therefore none changes
its store. A region is named by at most one reserving occurrence, and every
elided store brand resolves by one rule -- the enclosing nominal's sole region
parameter at a stored position, the entry heap's store region at a parameter or
result position -- while a bump extent's region is one the caller must choose
and is written at every position under [FORM-8]'s own judgment.

[BLK-0] makes the container and store operations one compiler-owned generic
declaration domain, a fourth admitted declaration source admitted to every unit
on [SYS-3]'s terms. Each operation is one complete signature record whose
written arguments are decided per argument, whose value arguments are named
[GRAM-11], and which is complete over every measure it writes on every exit,
including a refusal; [ENT-3.S13]'s population is extended to those rows, so a
row's declared relation establishes at a caller beside the source-call datums.

[BLK-1] states the two runs and the one window: exactly the `len` slots
beginning at `head` modulo `cap`, the rest raw, with no per-slot tag and no
runtime discriminant; a subscript is a logical offset whose [OP-4] obligation

window is what makes an affine element sound. [MSR-1]'s table gains three rows
and its first bounded cell, a run's window origin. [BLK-2] and [BLK-3] are the
inventory: four formation rows, one frame reservation, and the four boundary
operations, each taking its run by value and handing it back so that no
published relation reads as a fixed point of itself [MSR-3].

Five clauses are DEFERRED with stated deltas. [FN-7]'s `command.heap` row
cannot be written at all: its label tail is the spelling [EFF-1] fixes as the
allocation atom of `allocates(heap)`, which [FORM-3] therefore excludes from
IDENT, so the row lands with that atom's retirement. [BLK-2]'s `arena_extent`
row waits on the per-activation refusal its soundness needs. [STOR-5] states

is not -- and defers the position closure and the `&uniq` parameter refusal at

`Vector<'s, T>`, `FixedVector<T, n>`, `Heap<'s>` and `Arena<'s, bytes, align>`

classes, their [STOR-3] release actions, their [MSR-1] measure-table rows and

The nine [BLK-0] operations are one added declaration source beside the

under the ordinary [DIAG-1] rank, and add nothing to `ReservedLowerNames`,

Vector` and a source `fn seq_place` are therefore [TYPE-6] collisions and

constant and an independent runtime quantity of the descriptor -- beside the

fixes and the relation publication [CALL-6] carries for a declaration record

taken since v0.31, and `compiler/README.md` records it as this compiler's

## ccdeac8d 2026-09-04 B7a2: a kernel row is a callee, and its relations publish

[BLK-0] says each operation of the container and store domain is one complete
signature record. `semantic/kernel.rs` is that record data in exactly the rule's
shape -- generic parameters with the per-argument `supplied` judgment, named
value parameters with modes, an ordered result list, one effect row, one
requirement list and one relation list -- and two machine checks hold the table
to the rule: every row's parameter and result spellings equal the resolver's,
and every row is complete over every measure it writes on every exit, read with
[MSR-2]'s standing identity for `room`.

A call to a row is checked from that record and from nothing else: written
arguments are decided per argument, value arguments are the ordinary [GRAM-11]
named list, the run type parameter `V` is supplied by the `vector` operand
[BLK-3], and the row's effect row is projected through its actuals exactly as an
ordinary call's is. `len`, `cap`, `room` and `head` over a run or a bump extent
are the [OP-1] reader rows [MSR-1] gives them, and a subscript over a run is
[OP-4]'s ordinary obligation against `len`.

The publication path is keyed on the row rather than on a source node, which is
what B7a could not reach. `PreparedCall` now carries a callee that is either a
source `FunctionId` or a row's `container_declaration_ordinal`, and
`RelationProvenance` is the same split inside a derivation record: a row's
relations are instantiated at the call, its call datums are minted at
[ENT-3.S13]'s pre-transfer point -- including the `at the call` datum a `&uniq`
state operand's relations name -- and each relation is established at
[CALL-4]'s destinations under [CALL-6]. Each declared requirement is one
obligation of a new [MSR-4] family judged at the call; an undischarged one cites
BLK-0 and names the operation and the requirement's position in that row's own
declared list, because a record has no `requires_clause` occurrence and no
fabricated `NodePath` may enter [DIAG-1].

The four store-backed rows of [BLK-2] stop before their operands are read, as
one explicit unsupported capability with its name.

## fc14423e 2026-09-04 B7a2: the two runs lower and the window wraps

Lower the [BLK-2] formation rows, the four [BLK-3] boundary

[CALL-4] deferred three admissions in v0.44. Two of them land here:
a result ordinal's declared type may be a measured type, and a

## 836c1067 2026-09-04 B7a3: the release of a cyclic release graph enters itself

The owner deleted [PROV-6]'s release-graph cycle refusal on 2026-09-04
and ruled that the walk may recurse. This is the compiler half: the
derived release of a type whose release graph closes on itself is one
release action per node type, calling itself at the closing edge, and
the explicit heap worklist that ran that walk off the machine stack is
gone with the refusal it was written for.

The worklist bought its bounded depth with a `realloc` on the release
path and an abort when the host refused it -- an allocation and a trap
the writer never wrote, on a path [STOR-3] gives the empty effect row.
Its removal takes `TargetStorageType::Struct`, `structure` and
`validate_runtime_storage` with it, which had no other caller.

Three properties are restated rather than dropped, each in place:

- `a_cyclic_release_graph_lowers_to_one_release_action_that_enters_itself`
  replaces `no_compiler_derived_drop_reaches_itself`. It reads the same
  emitted module and the same two indirections a cleanup cycle can close
  through, and asserts the call graph closes instead of asserting it
  does not, plus that no release action allocates or aborts.
- `the_compilers_own_drop_glue_has_rows_and_reports_its_cycle` replaces
  the no-cycle half of the stack-ledger case. The recursion has no name
  in the source, and the ledger's `STACK cycle` row is where a writer
  sees it, beside the recursions they wrote.
- `a_buffer_in_a_cleanup_cycle_is_walked_in_the_order_the_rule_fixes`
  reads the buffer's own release action rather than a worklist step. The
  [STOR-3] order it pins is unchanged: elements from index zero upward,
  then the block that holds them.

`recursive_drop_worklist_growth_proves_each_address_domain` is retired:
it pinned the three no-wrap facts of a worklist growth that no longer
exists. `a_deep_boxed_spine_is_reclaimed_without_a_record` keeps its
end-to-end claim and drops its depth from a million to ten thousand;
how deep a recursive release can go is the stack-availability question
[SCOPE-3] defers for every program that is not resource_closed, and a
heap-allowed program is the only kind that can have a cyclic release
graph at all.

## e24bb416 2026-09-04 B7a3: a loop invariant carries a measure term

[GRAM-4]'s `affine_factor` admits a `call`, and [INV-1] admits exactly the
four measure formers there over an admitted measure place, written as
[MSR-5] writes them and resolving in the same context that rule already
gives an IDENT. This is the promise the containers design's amendment
register made for B2 -- "affine_factor GAINS terms at [MSR-4] in B2" --
and that B2 did not keep: B2 widened the affine *domain* and left the
production alone, so a measure term became an automatic premise and
stayed unwritable, and `invariant grown: len_of(built) >= at` was a
GRAM-4 parse rejection at the former. Without it no filling loop states
the relation its own operation needs on the backedge, which is why none
of the library's loops parse.

The affine domain is unchanged: it already carried one atom per live
measure term, so nothing is derived that was not derivable. What the
writer gains is the ability to state the relation. The atom is
retargeted by exactly the [ENT-5] events that kill its term [MSR-2],
which is what stops a header conclusion from outliving the write that
refutes it: `apply_affine_kills` drops the killed term's atom so the next
occurrence mints a fresh one, exactly as a local's image is dropped by a
write to that local. A measure the table fixes as a constant has no
mutable image at all and reads as the standing fact [MSR-2] gives it.

Three conformance cases and two unit tests carry it, and one pinned
sentence: the one `call` an affine factor admits is a measure former, and
any other call there is refused at the call node carrying the four
formers.

The specification also states [BLK-0]'s completeness sentence the way its
own machine check already read it -- `room_of` is the complement the
standing identity determines, so a row publishing `len_of` and `cap_of`
has published it -- and A.2's note says the same, which is what makes
`seq_arena`'s Some arm complete as written.

## 1b1047ae 2026-09-04 Enumerate every interleaving of the scheduler core, and fix what it found

Batch 2 slice 1, second half: the merge gate of PARK-ON-MISS.md §11.

The enumerator (compiler/src/backend/sched/enumerate.c, enumerate.h,
schedules.c, switch.h) compiles core.c against a replacement prim.h
(-DWF_SCHED_ENUMERATE): one OS thread, the controller on the process
stack, T simulated threads as coroutines each calling wf_sched_run, a
device process per submitted record, every primitive announcing its step
and performing it when chosen, the lock, the park and a yield as wait
states, and every §11 invariant checked after every step. The gate's
search is explicit-state: each scheduling point is checkpointed (the live
bytes of every stack, the core, the device, the checker's bookkeeping, the
schedule's state), digested and never explored twice; a step touching no
shared object goes alone, and a device completion is explored only where a
thread's next step can observe it. The re-executing walk of every
interleaving is the reference, feasible at one thread, where the two must
reach the same arms; the cargo wrapper asserts that. Twenty-one of §10's
schedules are scenarios in schedules.c; S8, S10b and S11 are not
enumerable. The sweep is (T=1,S=2), (T=1,S=3), (T=2,S=3), (T=2,S=4), as
backend/tests/sched.rs (one test each plus the cross-check) and
`make -C compiler sched-enumerate` under completion-test.

Six defects in the core, each reached by the enumeration and fixed in
place; docs/current-plan.md, Batch 2, slice 1, "Status" records each with
the schedule and configuration that reached it:

1. the entry thread's last pool stack was unresumable after the status
   post; the exit switch's far side now continues the loop;
2. a publisher could act on a waiter's phase after the parker had
   cancelled, run on and parked again; a publisher now claims the
   registration with a compare-exchange before it touches the phase, and a
   parker that finds DONE cancels only when it takes its registration
   back, so §6's cancel-consuming-NOTIFIED arm no longer exists;
3. DONE was stored before the waiter was read and an I/O record is a block
   of the joiner's frame, so a publisher could read a dead frame; the
   record now goes PENDING, COMPLETING, DONE, with DONE the publisher's
   last touch;
4. a thread waiting in place inside the I/O arm registered nothing, so a
   drain on another thread stored DONE and woke nobody; the arm registers
   WF_SCHED_WAITER_IN_PLACE and a claimed marker wakes the epoch;
5. the compute arm's empty-handed turn only yielded and, with the target
   held by a stack parked on I/O, spun forever; it now drains first;
6. a worker whose start came late found every stack parked; the creator
   reserves the worker's stack with wf_sched_start_thread at creation.

prim.h widens item 1 with the two read-modify-writes the idle bitmap uses
and names each critical section on item 5's lock, both for the reduction;
the host ignores the section. core.h's capacity constants are overridable
so the enumerator builds with two lane slots. The switch is shared through

## e6ddd54c 2026-09-04 B7a3b: a contract clause side is an affine expression

The owner's ruling of 2026-09-04 resolves the ambiguity that stopped B7a3.
`clause_expr := affine_expr (clause_op affine_expr)?` consumes `+`, `-` and
`*` inside each side, so the prefix conflict with the infix alternatives
disappears and the clause tail carries exactly the Bool-valued rows of
[OP-1]: the six comparisons and the five infix `defined` queries. One
production is added, `clause_op`, and two change: `clause_expr` and
`affine_factor`, which now admits an `atom`, a `call` and a `construct`.

One production serves both placements of one relation. [INV-1] states its
own admitted factors -- one bare IDENT place, one integer literal, one
measure former -- so a field selection, a subscript, a `move`, a borrow and
a construction derive under the production and are refused at the factor
citing INV-1 rather than at the parser. The affine atom keeps its own
resolution universe: a `pbase` directly below an `affine_factor` inside an
invariant or a proof use takes the InvariantValue or ProofValue role, and
every other `pbase`, including the operand of a measure former, is an
ordinary place base.

A clause side's `+`, `-` and `*` denote the mathematical integer expression
[INV-1] fixes and perform no [OP-1] operation, so a clause creates no [OP-2]
domain obligation and admits no runtime value it could overflow. [FN-8]'s
requirement carries the whole affine expression: `requires at + 2_u64 <=
len_of(run);` projects to the ordinary difference bound `at - len_of(run) <=
-2` and discharges the callee's own subscript bound.

[FN-9]'s relation operand becomes one datum displaced by a written constant,
which is the shape [ENT-4]'s closure represents and the shape every kernel
row already writes [BLK-0]. `Relation::Equal` and `Relation::Distinct` gain
that difference, so `ensures len_of(rest) + 1_u64 == len_of(vector);` is one
relation occurrence and not a second fact class; a displaced disequality is
provable from a strict bound and establishes no stored fact, which only
under-derives. A clause side carrying two datums, or a datum with any other
coefficient, is outside the fragment and is an FN-9 rejection at the clause.

One diagnostic selection moved with the production and is recorded rather
than hidden: a `define` written after a `requires` now leaves a frontier
whose expectation list carries IDENT, and [FORM-3]'s reserved-word row owns
it before [GRAM-2]'s section-order repair is reached. The same sentence is
still reached by a `requires` written after an `ensures`, which is what the
probe now pins.

Conformance reports Pass=580 Xfail=1 Skip=1 over 582 cases; the snapshot
corpus reports Pass=491 Flip=0 and no recorded verdict moves.

## c08ed22a 2026-09-05 B7a3b: a parameter's measure in an ensures is its entry datum

[MSR-3]'s second placement lands beside the call placement it deferred
behind. At body entry, per parameter of measured type and per [MSR-1]
measure of it a declared relation names, one compiler-owned immutable term
is minted and established equal to that measure. It is the same kind of term
as a call datum: no place occurs in it, so no [ENT-5] event kills it, and
[FN-9] reads it where it used to read the live place.

That is what the two `entry image` rows of [MSR-3]'s own table always said,
and it is what B7a2 measured missing. `set vector = seq_place(vector: move
vector, ...)` -- the ordinary shape a [LIV-2] commit gives an operation over
an `own` parameter -- killed the parameter's measure terms, and [FN-9] then
made every clause naming it unavailable, including `ensures head_of(rest) ==
head_of(vector)`, which the compiler reported as `head_of(vector) =
head_of(vector)` Unproved. 3.L.4's `try_place` and `try_take` now compile as
the design writes them.

The placement is exactly as wide as the rule: a parameter of fragment type
is not a measured value and has no measure to carry, so its entry image
stays the live place and a body that writes it back still loses it. The
conformance pair carries both halves, and
`measure_entry_datums_survive_element_writes_and_root_replacement` restates
the unit case whose second half pinned the cost of reading the live term:
its relation is now discharged, and it is the same relation the writer
stated.

## fbb3ac85 2026-09-05 B7a4: the bump extent is reserved, and its runs execute

[BLK-2]'s three reservation and take rows over a bump extent are lowered, and
the whole path behind them is real: `arena_frame` reserves one extent in the
reserving activation's own frame, `seq_arena_proved` and `seq_arena` take a run
of `count` slots from it, the `Vector<'s, T>` descriptor those hand back is the
one the four boundary rows and the window subscript already worked over, and
LLVM comes out and runs. `tests/programs/arena_workspace.wf` reads the store's
own cursor before and after each take, observes that a refused take leaves it
where it was, fills a taken run through `seq_place` and reads the window back.

Two collisions between the inventory's record data and [FORM-3] are repaired
here, and the second was measured rather than reasoned. The provider operand of
each acquiring row was named `arena` or `heap`, and both are fixed grammar
atoms -- the `arena<'r, T>` type and `allocates(heap)`'s allocation atom --
which [FORM-3] excludes from IDENT, so `seq_arena(arena: ...)` was a FORM-3
parse rejection and no call to any of the three rows could be written at all.
Nothing had caught it because no test had ever written one. The operand is now
spelled `store` in all three rows, which is [3.K.10]'s one name per concept,
and `every_declared_spelling_is_writable` holds the whole table to
[FORM-3]'s IDENT class so the class of defect cannot return.

`advance<T>(count)` is the stride and not the size. A run's slots are
stride-spaced [BLK-1], so `count` of them occupy `stride_ceiling(T) * count`
bytes and a take of `size_ceiling(T) * count` would hand out a run whose last
slots lie outside what the store gave it. [BLK-0] says so and the compiler's
one reader of the quantity says so.

A row's requirement carried its written displacement nowhere: the caller's goal
was built from the two operands alone, so `room_of(store) >= advance<T>(count)`
was submitted as `room_of(store) >= 0` and discharged by every store. The
requirement now carries it, `every_displaced_requirement_side_is_the_zero_term`
holds the record data to the one shape a goal can express, and a call whose
count is not a closed expression -- where the advance is an opaque term no
caller has a source spelling for -- is an explicit unsupported capability
rather than a silently skipped obligation.

[BLK-2]'s placement judgment and [PROV-1]'s one-store-per-region refusal are
implemented: the written store region must be one an enclosing `region_stmt` of
the reserving function introduced, the occurrence must be a statement of that
block and of no loop inside it, and a second occurrence naming one region is
refused at its store argument. [BLK-2] and [PROV-1] therefore become cited
rules of `SemanticRule` and take their definition ranks.

The extent's release action is deleted rather than kept: the reservation
establishes the cursor at zero at every activation of its region block, its
storage is the activation's own frame, and nothing of it is observable outside
that block, so no edge leaving the block has work to do. [BLK-2] and [STOR-3]
say that instead of naming a reset row.

`seq_heap` keeps its explicit `ContainerRuntime` stop with its reason
restated: a heap-backed run's release action is a free this version's
region-erased `IrType::Vector` cannot select, and [FN-7]'s own row -- the one
route by which a program obtains the general store's provider -- is still that
rule's DEFERRED entry.

## 1b1ae79d 2026-09-05 B7a4: a const generic is an affine atom

[MSR-6]'s fourth position lands. `invariant spare: room_of(built) + at >= n;`
is what a capacity-parametric loop wants to state, and B7a3b measured that it
could not: the const generic reached [ENT-2]'s endpoint and [MSR-5]'s clause
and not [INV-1]'s atom role, so `tests/programs/fixed_run_library.wf` bound
`let limit = n;` in three functions and stated its bound over the local. Those
three lines are gone and the three loops name `n`.

The admission is on the const generic's own ground rather than on the named
const's. [ENT-2] clause (c) makes an in-scope const generic a *constant*: it is
not a tracked place, so it needs no liveness, no entry state and no support,
and nothing kills it. A named const is a term of clause (a), and [INV-1]'s
exclusion of it stands unchanged; admitting it is a separate question this
version does not answer. [MSR-6] and [INV-1] say exactly that.

Nothing is derived that was not derivable: a concrete instance reads the
mathematical value [FN-2] fixed for it and the one source-canonical symbolic
instance reads the symbolic constant term, which the affine domain carries as
one immutable atom keyed on that term, exactly as it carries a measure. What
the writer gains is the ability to state the relation.

The substitution reaches the affine atom by being threaded from the enclosing
declaration rather than by an ambient cell, so which instance is being checked
is a parameter of the judgment and not compiler state.

## 23bdd475 2026-09-05 B7a5: the specification amendment and the grammar S37 changes

The owner's 2026-09-05 ruling on generic parameter bounds lands in the
specification, and with it the one production change and the one added atom it
needs.

A bound is a closed class the argument must fall into, derived from the
language's own classifications and never a user trait. [PROV-6] states the
three linearity classes as the strict chain `copy < affine < linear`, ordered
by what a body may do with a value of the class -- duplicate, use bare and
drop; `move` at most once and drop; consume exactly once and never drop -- and
makes satisfaction that chain read left to right: an argument of class C
instantiates a bound B exactly when C <= B. That corrects the equal-class check
the same rule carried under S32, which made a bound a partition rather than a
ceiling and refused `hold::<u64>` at `T: linear` for no reason a writer can
state.

[GRAM-2] makes a type parameter's bound mandatory: `gparam` loses its optional
alternative and `linearity_bound` gains `copy`, the batch's one added fixed
lowercase atom, which [FORM-3] therefore excludes from IDENT. A region
parameter's bound stays optional and is `affine` or `linear` and never `copy`,
because it names the class of the store the region identifies and no store is
reclaimed by duplication.

[FN-2] and [OWN-1] state that the template is the spelling authority: a generic
body is checked once at the symbolic instance under its written bound, and the
concrete-instance recheck does not re-judge the spellings [FORM-1] keys on a
value's class. There are two such spellings and not one -- `move p` against a
bare `p` [OWN-1] and `replace` against `set` [SET-1, SET-2] -- so [SET-2]
carries the same sentence as a cross-reference. Without it no generic body can
serve a copy type and an affine type at once.

[LIV-2]'s declaring `set` target stops being DEFERRED and becomes normative: a
bare identifier target that resolves to no binding declares one exactly as a
`let` binder does, and only a bare identifier target does. [BLK-1]'s
element-position admission drops the word *unbounded*, which named a class of
parameter this ruling deletes.

The tables are regenerated from the amended EBNF rather than edited: `gparam`
loses one decision, so the committed inventory holds 134 decisions and 6,228
select rows over the same 88 productions, and the fixed-terminal inventory
holds 103 predicates with `copy` in `linearity_bound`'s first-occurrence
position.

## 5a9250b9 2026-09-05 B7a5: the bound, the declaring set target, and a run's release class

Four things land in the compiler and in both corpora, and each is what one part
of the specification amendment before this commit says.

**S37's bound.** `GenericParameter::Type` carries one mandatory `GenericBound`,
which is a marker row or one of the three classes; there is no unbounded
alternative left to represent, because the grammar has none. `LinearityClass`
gains `Copy` and is ordered, so satisfaction is `argument <= bound` and the
diagnostic names the parameter, the bound and the argument's own class. A type
parameter standing for itself at a symbolic instance has exactly the class its
written bound names -- `is_copy_type` and `linearity_class` both read the
declaration -- which is what admits the bare repeated use a `copy`-bounded body
writes and what makes a `linear`-bounded body's dropped value the ordinary
not-consumed rejection, naming the bound where a marked nominal would be named.

**The template's spelling authority.** `check_function_signature` records
whether the body it is about to check is a concrete instance of a generic
template, and the four `MoveOfCopy` sites keyed on a value's class, plus
[SET-2]'s copy-target refusal, ask before rejecting. Every other judgment of
those rules is unchanged and still made at the instance. The unit test that
asserted the opposite is rewritten with the reason in its own doc comment:
under S32 an `affine`-bounded body writing `move value` was an [OWN-1]
rejection at every copy instance, so no generic body could serve both classes,
and the corpus still keeps `const1-neg-eval-overflow` for the instance recheck
that does reject.

**[LIV-2]'s declaring `set` target, in the resolver.** B7a4 measured that this
is not checker work: the target identifier is an unresolved use before the
checker runs. The promotion is one pass of the resolver's own lookup -- a bare
identifier target of a `set_stmt` whose lookup finds no visible binding becomes
an ordinary `let` declaration owned by its own `pbase`, visible after the
complete statement -- repeated until every use resolves, so a declared target is
judged by exactly the rules a `let` binder is. The checker mints the binding
dead with its own ordinal's type after the right-hand side, and the ordinary
commit revives it; lowering treats such a target as the binding's
initialization, as a `let` is.

**A run's release class travels on its type.** `CheckedType::Vector` and
`IrType::Vector` carry it, read off the store region's declaration alone: an
`affine`-bounded region parameter and a `region_stmt` region are bump extents,
and the entry heap, an unbounded region parameter and a `linear`-bounded one
are general stores. Nothing spends one yet, so a unit test pins the four
classifications rather than a program observing them.

**And the region axis reaches a call's container types.** A parameter type
naming a formal region -- `Vector<'s, T>`, `Arena<'s, b, a>` and `Heap<'s>`
beside the `Slice<'r, T>` that already worked -- determines that region from its
actual and is substituted with it, so a source function is generic over a store
for the first time. That is what makes the region axis of the bound check
reachable at all, and `prov6-pos-a-region-argument-names-a-bump-extent` runs it.

The corpus is respelled with the bound each body needs: 61 declarations across
both corpora, every one `affine`, which is the class an unbounded parameter
already had. Two bindings spelled `copy` are respelled, `copy` now being an
atom [FORM-3] excludes from IDENT. `tests/programs/fixed_run_library.wf` is
generic again in all six functions and exercises each affine-bounded one at
`u8` and at `Option<u8>`; `filled` is `copy`-bounded and runs at two copy
types, an affine instance being what its own bound refuses.

One corpus verdict moves, and it is the intended one:
`prov6-pos-linearity-bound-on-a-region-parameter` passed a plain `region { }`
region to `'s: affine` and was accepted only because the instantiation check had
no region axis. It is `prov6-neg-a-region-argument-that-names-no-store` now,
expecting `reject PROV-6`, with both of its docs rewritten to say what it
demonstrates.

## 53ed4b6e 2026-09-05 B7a5: the records

The container design gains S37 in 3.S: the decided-list row, the owner's ruling
recorded verbatim, and the ground for what it settles that S32 did not -- the
equal-class check that made a bound a partition, the optional bound that made
the unwritten case a fourth unnamed class, and the instance recheck that
re-judged the spelling and cost every generic body one of its two element
classes. S32's row and paragraph are marked superseded on those three points.
The one thing that grew beyond the ruling is recorded there rather than hidden:
the exception is over the spellings [FORM-1] keys on a value's class, and there
are two of them, because `take_at`'s own `replace short[at] = move endv;` is
[SET-2]'s copy-target refusal at a copy instance for exactly the reason its
`move` was [OWN-1]'s.

Dated corrections land under [PROV-6] -- which corrects [FN-2] and [OWN-1] with
it -- under [BLK-1] for the deleted word *unbounded*, and under [LIV-2] for the
declaring target that is no longer DEFERRED and for where it had to be
implemented. 3.L's six library declarations carry the bounds they need, and
Q8's copy/affine half is closed where 3.L.4 raised it.

6.0k says what landed and what did not. **Runs of runs did not**, and the block
pool depends on them: the obstacle is representation and not judgment, since
`CheckedFlatElement` is a non-recursive `Copy` element domain embedded in
`CheckedType`, so an element carrying its own descriptor needs either an
interned element table travelling with the checked program or a boxed element
that costs `CheckedType` its `Copy`, and then the same lift in `IrType`, in the
layout ceilings and in the lowering. A one-level lift is the cheaper shape and
is what a later batch should price first. [MSR-1]'s `len_of(P[i])` over a run of
runs, [MSR-2]'s element-position kill at that granularity, [LIV-2] condition 2's
`grid[k]` against `grid[i][j]`, and B4's affine element read-out wait with it.

The v0.45 draft record gains its B7a5 CONTENT, two CONSEQUENCE entries -- one
for the added atom and the two bindings it forced to be respelled, one for the
mandatory bound and the 61 declarations it did -- and its CONFORMANCE BOUNDARY:
nine added cases, one renamed and modified with its before and after stated in
full, eight more whose source changed and whose verdict did not, and no
deletion. The adapter moves from Pass=595 over 597 cases to Pass=604 over 606,
with the one xfail and the one skip unchanged and the snapshot corpus at
Pass=491 Flip=0.

`compiler/README.md` restates the container gap: `seq_heap` now stops for one
reason rather than two, because a run's release class travels on its type; a

## ddcd9b34 2026-09-05 B7a5: the region axis is an equality of store class, and copy is not one

Three corrections the first pass got wrong, each measured rather than reasoned.

**The region axis is not the type axis' chain.** `check_region_linearity_bound`
asked whether the argument's store class *satisfies* the bound, which under the
chain lets a bump extent instantiate a `linear`-bounded region parameter. A
region bound names which kind of store its region identifies, not a ceiling on
an obligation, so satisfaction there is the equality [PROV-6] already stated: an
extent does not stand in for a general store, and a region that names no store
satisfies neither bound.

**`copy` is not a class a store has.** `linearity_bound` is one production with
three alternatives, so the grammar admits `'s: copy` wherever it admits
`'s: affine`. No store is reclaimed by duplication, so the class is refused at
the `region_param` itself rather than leaving every call to reject with a
message about a mismatch the declaration could have prevented. [PROV-6] says so
and `prov6-neg-a-region-parameter-bounded-copy` holds it.

**Two pinned counts, and one cited rule.** `bin/grammar.rs`'s own consistency
test pins the decision and terminal counts a second time, and `gparam` losing
its optional bound moves both. [LIV-2]'s new sentence said an unresolved
projected-target base keeps its ordinary [TYPE-6] rejection; [TYPE-6]'s own
cited-rule table gives a `pbase` IDENT lookup failure TYPE-5, which is what the
compiler cites and what the case expects, so the sentence names the lookup
rather than the citation.

## 733f76e8 2026-09-05 B7a6: S38 respells the kernel vocabulary, and the design records the scheme

The owner's 2026-09-05 ruling gives the whole container vocabulary one naming
rule, and this commit is that rename and nothing else: no production, no atom,
no rule, no record shape, and no verdict moves with it.

**One rule, two halves.** A non-consuming derivation from a value is spelled
`X_of(v)`, which is what the four measure readers already were [S36] and what
the two view formers should have been; a consuming transformation that hands a
new value back is spelled `verb_object`, and the object follows the TYPE names
the owner chose [S1, S2]. The word *run* is design-internal and now appears in
no spelling at all. Ten names move: `seq_fixed` to `fixed_vector`, `seq_arena`
to `arena_vector`, `seq_arena_proved` to `arena_vector_proved`, `seq_heap` to
`heap_vector`, `seq_place` to `place_back`, `seq_place_front` to `place_front`,
`seq_take` to `take_back`, `seq_take_front` to `take_front`, and A.2's two view
rows `seq_slice` and `seq_mut_slice` to `slice_of` and `mut_slice_of`, which
B8 lands. `arena_frame`, `arena_extent` and the four readers are unchanged.

**What the compiler carries is record data.** The nine spellings live in
`resolution::kernel`'s table and are read generically, so the rename is that
table's `spelling` fields plus the `KernelRow` discriminants named after them —
which now read `FixedVector`, `ArenaVector`, `ArenaVectorProved`, `HeapVector`,
`PlaceBack`, `PlaceFront`, `TakeBack` and `TakeFront`, the last four being the
`IrBoundary` names the lowering already used. No grammar production and no
fixed atom is touched, so `generated.rs` is not regenerated: an operation
spelling is data of [BLK-0]'s declaration domain and never a grammar atom.

**No corpus declaration collides with a new spelling.** B2 and B7a3 both had to
repair a program whose own binding a new reserved reader took; this batch has
none to repair, because the nine kernel spellings are declaration records
rather than [OP-1] table rows and enter `ReservedLowerNames` not at all — a
source declaration spelling one of them is the ordinary [DIAG-1] collision.
Twenty-five corpus files are respelled -- twenty-one conformance cases, three
programs and six manifest doc strings -- and every verdict is unchanged: the
adapter reports Pass=605, Xfail=1, Skip=1 and the snapshot corpus Pass=491,
Flip=0.

**One thing the scheme decides that B8 must act on**, recorded in 3.S rather
than hidden: `slice_of` is already a live [OP-1] table row, the v0.44 view
former over `array` and `buffer`, so renaming A.2's kernel view row to
`slice_of` makes two [TYPE-6] domains claim one spelling. The design states the
two repairs and picks neither, because neither row lands here.

3.S gains S38 with the ruling verbatim and its ground; S7, S8 and S10 are
marked "see S38". A.2, 3.K.10, 3.L's programs and the written-argument table
carry the new spellings, and three call sites in the design still writing the
pre-B7a4 `arena:`/`heap:` operand are corrected to `store:` while they are
being edited. Section 6's dated landed-records keep the spelling they were
written in, which is the convention S35 set for the same reason.

## 22e1758a 2026-09-05 B7a6: a slot may hold a run, and the release walk over its window is emitted

The element domain gains one level of lift, which is what 6.0k priced as the
cheaper shape, and the four things that lift makes reachable land with it.

**One level, and the whole path carries it.** `CheckedElement` and `IrElement`
are the element domain: a flat element, or one run of *flat* elements whose
descriptor lives in the slot. `FixedVector<Vector<'s, u8>, 8>` and
`FixedVector<FixedVector<u8, 4>, 4>` are exactly one level and are what this
design asks for. A third level is an explicit unsupported capability, because
an arbitrarily deep element needs an interned element table travelling with the
checked program or a boxed element that costs `CheckedType` its `Copy`, and no
program here wants one. A slot's layout ceiling is the element type's own, so a
run of descriptors is `[8 x { ptr, i64, i64, i64 }]` followed by its own two
words; the element read and the element store move that whole aggregate through
the same `(head_of + i) mod cap_of` a scalar slot uses.

**[PROV-6]'s release walk is emitted rather than refused.** A run whose element
derived any release action used to be `InvalidIr` at the emitter. It is one
helper per run type now: over the window and not the capacity, because a slot
outside the window is raw [BLK-1] and reading it would be an uninitialized
read; in ascending logical order; and with the run's own backing released
*after* the loop, which is what the rule's ordering means at the instruction
level. The predicate that decides whether a run derives anything at all is its
**release class** and no longer the bare fact of being store-resident, so an
extent-backed run of flat elements derives nothing and the pool emits no
release code. `heap_vector`'s free will land after that loop, in a place that
now exists.

**A formal region one level down is determined by its actual.** [FORM-8] says
*at any depth of its `type`*; the compiler read the top level only, so a
parameter of type `FixedVector<Vector<'s, u8>, 8>` determined nothing and its
caller was told to write a region [FORM-8] forbids writing. Where both levels
name a region the outer one alone is substituted and the position is the
ordinary [TYPE-5] mismatch: fail-closed, and stated as a gap in the source.

**Two resolver defects the design's own block pool exposed.** A nominal's
`region_params` [S20] reached no owning declaration, so every nominal in a unit
shared one region scope and `Lease['s]` beside `BlockPool['s]` was refused
twice — once as an [OWN-3] repeated region and once as a [TYPE-6]
redeclaration. A nominal is its own region scope exactly as a function is, in
the uniqueness check and in the scope tree alike; [OWN-3] gains the one
sentence that says so, which is this batch's whole specification delta.

**`tests/programs/block_pool.wf` is 3.L.4 over the lift, and what it lacks is
not the lift.** Eight 256-byte arena-backed runs carved into one
`FixedVector<Vector<'a, u8>, 8>`, a block leased off the back boundary, and a
block returned to a free list `pool_release` *proved* had room, with both pool
operations generic over the store. It is the pool without its two nominals,
because a source nominal is not generic over its store region: `struct
BlockPool['s]` declares and no call instantiates `'s`, so a `Chunk(page: move
page)` at an actual region is a [TYPE-5] mismatch against the formal. [S20]
declared that axis and nothing ever instantiated it, which no earlier batch
could see because no program used such a nominal as a type. The proved
release's requirement is discharged by a dominating branch on `room_of` rather
than by `pool_take`'s routed relation, because a route over a returned enum's
variant is [CALL-4]'s own DEFERRED form.

Five cases carry it, and no corpus verdict moves: the adapter goes from
Pass=605 over 607 to Pass=610 over 612, the one xfail and the one skip
unchanged, and the snapshot corpus stays Pass=491 Flip=0.

## 3acc3e95 2026-09-05 The completion record is the frame's block, found by address

Design §7: the slot pool and its tokens, claims, milestones, drains,
consumes, dependent frames and capacity waits are deleted from the
completion core, the bridge, the file adapter and the io_uring adapter.
wf_completion_record begins with the scheduler core's wf_sched_record;
contract.h is its header; runtime.c keeps the wake epoch and the park.
The io_uring adapter builds the SQE from the record and carries its
address as user_data; its depth is a ring parameter of its own. The
file adapter queues pending work on an intrusive FIFO through the
records. Every submit ends in wf_completion_record_complete, which is
wf_sched_complete on the record: the ring reaps it, a helper runs it,
or the submitting thread executes it and publishes. The joins wait in
place through the core's own registration, and the core's park and
wake are the bridge's, so one wake reaches the ring's eventfd and the
condition variable alike.

The harness and the probes are on the record API; the tests of the
deleted machinery are retired with §7 named at each site, and what
remains is retested. The Windows record port is not in this change;
docs/current-plan.md says so.

## 4fa3e781 2026-09-05 B8a: the specification amendment for the region axis and the element read-out

Five rules are amended, no rule, production, atom, operation spelling or
declaration record is added or retired, and no DEFERRED clause lands: the
counts in META-5's v0.45 delta declaration do not move, and its amended-rule
list already names the two amended rules this version did not itself add.

**A nominal's region parameters fix its instance.** [TYPE-2] already made the
declared regions components of the nominal's type name; it now says what that
decides. An instance is keyed on its region arguments beside its type and const
arguments, two instances of one declaration at two regions are two types under
the exact identity [TYPE-5] and [OWN-12] already perform, every position of the
declaration naming a region parameter carries that instance's own argument — so
a `Vector<'s, T>` field in an instance at `'a` is a `Vector<'a, T>` and takes
the release class `'a`'s own declaration gives it — and the arguments are
written as the **leading members of the same `targs` list** the two runs and the
two providers already use, at every `type` position and at every `construct`.

**A construct writes them on [TYPE-5]'s own ground.** Construction consults no
expected nominal type, so the written arguments are the only supply there is,
which is exactly why that rule makes a generic nominal's type and const
arguments mandatory. It is not a second region-spelling rule: [FORM-8] writes a
REGIONID wherever this document does not otherwise fix the region, and nothing
fixes a nominal's region argument there. A *parameter* whose type names a
nominal with exactly one region argument determines it from the actual and the
caller writes nothing, which is [FORM-8] unchanged; two or more determine none,
the same fail-closed reading a doubly branded run takes.

**[PROV-1] extends its store-identity sentence** to a source nominal's region
argument, which is invariant there exactly as a container's or a provider's is,
and states the consequence in the design's own words: `struct BlockPool['s]`
names one store per instance, `BlockPool<'a>` and `BlockPool<'b>` are two types,
and a run of one may not enter the other.

**An affine element has a second route out of its slot.** [TYPE-2]'s element
sentence gains it and [LIV-2] states it: a subscripted target `P[i]` is read out
by a `move` of `P[j]`, or of a place reached through it, exactly when the two
offsets are provably the same — two written literals of equal value — because
reading one element out and reinitialising another would leave one slot holding
a value that never left and the other holding none. An offset the rule cannot
decide reads out nothing, so a live affine element target keeps [STOR-1]'s
rejection and the `move` keeps [TYPE-2]'s. The read-out is the [SET-1]
assignment half of [BLK-1]'s element-position commit and stands on exactly
[SET-2]'s ground: no writer-observable program point lies between it and the
commit. [BLK-3]'s element-swap sentence is therefore that one commit,
`set (v[i], v[j]) = move v[j], move v[i];`, in place of `take_back`, one
`replace` and `place_back`.

## 552f6e52 2026-09-05 B8a: a nominal instance is keyed on its region, and the region is erased at lowering

[S20] gave a nominal `region_params` in B7a and nothing ever instantiated them.
This is that axis, landed the way B7a5 landed the one for a function's
parameter types, plus the two things it turned out to need underneath.

**The instance key.** `GenericSubstitution` gains a region axis beside its type
and const bindings, `NominalTemplate` carries the declaration's own
`region_params`, and a nominal that declares only regions is a template like any
other: it has a symbolic instance binding each region parameter to itself, and
every use mints a concrete one. A `type` and a `construct` read the leading
members of the same `targs` list as region arguments, and a field type is parsed
under that substitution — so `Vector<'s, u8>` inside `BlockPool<'a>` is a
`Vector<'a, u8>` and takes the release class `'a`'s own declaration gives it
[PROV-6]. A parameter position substitutes a formal nominal with the **actual's
own instance**, which the two agreeing in everything but the region is what
admits; a result position keeps the declaration's instance, exactly as an
`Option<Vector<'s, T>>` result already did, and the caller's next transfer
substitutes from the actual it holds.

**A store region is invariant at a call, and was not.** [PROV-1] has said since
B7 that two values have the same store exactly when their types name the same
region, decided by exact identity. The call path bound a formal region occupying
a container position by the ordinary least-region observation, so `fn
wider['s](one: own Vector<'s, u8>, two: own Vector<'s, u8>)` accepted two runs
of two different extents whenever one region outlived the other. The first store
position now fixes the formal and every later one is substituted with it, which
makes a second store the ordinary [TYPE-5] mismatch at that argument. A view's
loan region is untouched: it names no store and relates two positions by
outlives.

**Where the region leaves the program is the lowering.** A region names a store
for the proof and nothing at run time — `IrType::Vector` has erased one since
B7a5 — so two instances of one declaration that differ only in their region
arguments are two checked types and **one IR nominal**. That is what lets a
callee's own formal-region instance and a caller's actual-region instance meet
at the boundary between them without monomorphizing every function over its
regions, and it is checked rather than assumed: the relation compares the two
instances' lowered content with every region erased and every region-derived
datum kept, so two whose release classes differ are two representations and are
neither erased together nor substituted for one another. `lower_type`,
`lower_element`, `lower_flat_element` and the enum-type lowering take the
erasure, and `IrBuilder` carries it for the instruction sites that name a
nominal directly.

**Two defects the design's own pool exposed, both older than this batch.** A
destructuring consume written inside a `match` arm — `let Lease(run: back) =
move lease;` — classified its binder as an arm binder rather than a `let`
binder, because the resolver asked whether an `arm` was anywhere above the
`fieldbind` instead of which construct owned its list; the program stopped as an
internal failure rather than compiling. And a caller's contract instantiation
did not substitute a nominal's region arguments, so a `requires` over a
parameter of nominal type could not be read at a call whose actual named a
different region.

## d8e28bdd 2026-09-05 B8a: two elements of one run exchange slots in one commit

B4 landed [LIV-2]'s read-out over whole places and left the element case
standing, with the reason written into the code: a resolved place names no
offset, so a `move` of a target's place is a different element as often as it is
this one. The offset a target needs was already there — a `set` target carries
its own written offset — so the match is between two things the statement holds
and not between two resolved places, and this is that match.

**One offset reading, used twice.** A `CommitOffset` is a written literal or
opaque; two literals are provably distinct exactly when their values differ,
which is the relation [LIV-2] condition 2 already stated and which the commit's
own overlap test now reads instead of comparing literals by hand, and provably
the same exactly when they agree, which is what a read-out needs. Everything
else is opaque: provably equal to nothing, itself included, so a target carrying
one is never read out and never admitted beside a second subscript of its run.

**The subscript read.** A subscript of an affine element is [TYPE-2]'s
rejection, and this adds the one exception [LIV-2] states: a `move P[i]` in the
right-hand side of the `set` whose own target is `P[j]` at a provably equal
offset. The offset is read there before the ordinary judgment reaches it, and an
offset that does not check matches nothing and leaves every diagnostic where it
was — no read-out is recorded and the affine rejection stands. One target is
read out at most once, so the second `move` of one element is an ordinary use of
what the first consumed and rejects as one.

`set (v[0_u64], v[1_u64]) = move v[1_u64], move v[0_u64];` therefore exchanges
two store-backed runs in one commit, and
`liv2-pos-an-affine-element-read-out-swaps-two-slots` runs it and reads each
run's own capacity back out of the slot the other came from. Three negative
cases hold the boundary: an affine element moved outside its own commit, a live
affine element target whose right-hand side reads nothing out, and two read-outs
of one target.

## 6646f7a8 2026-09-05 B8a: the block pool runs with 3.L.4's two nominals

`tests/programs/block_pool.wf` is the design's block pool entire:
`struct BlockPool['s]` holds the free list, `linear struct Lease['s]` holds the
leased run, and `pool_new`, `pool_take` and `pool_release` are all three generic
over the store. B7a6's version was the same mechanism with the bare
`FixedVector<Vector<'s, u8>, 8>` the struct would have held; what it was missing
was the region axis, and the `linear` wrapper waited with it.

**The `linear` modifier is what makes the return unavoidable**, and the program
shows it: the one path that does not hand the lease back to `pool_release` has
to take it apart with `let Lease(run: orphan) = move ticket;`, and simply
dropping it is [PROV-6]'s refusal. That is 3.L.7's whole argument, executing.

Four spellings of 3.L.4 moved, and two of them are real bounds on the shape
rather than preferences. `pool_new`'s store parameter is named `store`, because
`arena` is a fixed grammar atom [FORM-3] excludes from IDENT. Its loop body is
**one statement** — `match arena_vector::<u8>(store: &uniq deref(store), count:
256_u64) { ... }` — because a `let` and then a `match` on its binding are two,
and the child reborrow in the first would need a region whose block does not
extend beyond that statement while a loop body's own region extends over the
whole body [OWN-6]. Every clause naming a measure over a *result*'s field is
dropped, because that is [CALL-4]'s own first DEFERRED admission, so `main`
reads `len_of(pool.free)` and `room_of(rest.free)` and branches — the price this
design already names twice — while `pool_release`'s `requires
room_of(pool.free) > 0_u64` over a **parameter**'s field is an ordinary [MSR-1]
place and is what the call site discharges. And each construct writes its
nominal's region argument, `BlockPool<'s>(free: move free)`, which is where
[TYPE-5] puts it.

Four conformance cases carry the axis: a nominal generic over its store, built
at a caller's own extent and read through a helper that writes no region

## eb7b716e 2026-09-05 B8b: a result's region is the actual's, and two stores are two result types

B8a landed the region axis and left one hole in it: a nominal result — and,
since B7a5, an `Option<Vector<'s, T>>` result — kept the *declaration's*
region. Two calls of
`fn f['s: affine](store: &uniq Arena<'s, ...>) -> made: own BlockPool<'s>`
at two extents therefore produced results of one type, and a run taken from
arena A could be typed later as a run of arena B. That is a soundness hole and
this is its repair.

**[FN-2] substitutes into every position, and a result is one of them.**
[FORM-8] already said a call's undetermined region parameters are fixed by its
own actuals and that a related result region reaches as far as its inputs
allow; what was missing was the sentence that carries that into the result
*type*, and the compiler's own substitution stopped at a nominal by an explicit
comment. The substitution is now structural over the complete checked type
domain, so a region is reached wherever it occurs: under `Option` and `Result`,
inside a source nominal instance's own region arguments and its type arguments,
in a run's element position, in a `box` referent and an `arena`'s content, and
in every ordinal of the compiler-owned result-list nominal a multi-result
callable hands back. A run's release class is a function of its region's
declaration [PROV-6], so it is re-read from the substituted region rather than
carried across.

**A parameter position one level down takes it too.** `absorb(store: &uniq
Arena<'s, ...>, spare: own Option<Vector<'s, u8>>)` fixes `'s` at its store
operand and the second parameter's *inner* run must then be that store's. Every
region a call has already fixed — a written `::` member, and a store region an
earlier operand named [PROV-1] — is substituted into the whole of each later
parameter type before that position's own top-level judgment runs. A region no
position has bound yet is deliberately left alone: [FORM-8] gives it to the
actual at the position that first names it, which is the judgment that was
already there.

**The instance a result names may be written nowhere.** No position of
`let held = hold(store: &uniq first);` spells `Option<Holder<'a>>`, so the
interning pass cannot have found it. It is reported as the ordinary deferred
nominal a derived `box<T>` already is, and the driver interns it and checks the
function again. Phase A's "no source instance is discovered here" guard is
replaced by the honest invariant: an instance discovered there must be one
representation with an instance the written text already interned, so lowering
still erases it onto that instance's IR nominal.

**The erasure had to widen with it.** B8a related two source instances of one
declaration; a substituted result is just as often a prelude instance or a
result-list nominal, and two of those differing only in a region are one IR
representation exactly as two source instances are. The relation now reads a
name shape — one declaration at two regions, one prelude shape, one result list
with the same ordinal names, one `box` or one `arena` — and then the same
region-blind content comparison, which is what keeps a difference the run time
can see out of it.

`checked_type_name` spells a nominal instance's region arguments, because the
two sides of this repair's own rejection are otherwise the same word twice.

Two conformance cases: two extents' results refused as two types, and a
result-only region written at the call and admitted at the caller's own extent.
The adapter moves from Pass=618 over 620 cases to Pass=620 over 622, the one
xfail and the one skip unchanged, and the snapshot corpus stays at Pass=491,
Flip=0.

## 986ad3c8 2026-09-05 B8b: a run's element read owes the same obligation its target does

[OP-4] carries the bounds obligation `i < len_of(p)` at every subscript and
says in one sentence that a target's discharge judgment is *identical* to a
read's. B7a3b landed the element-position store with that judgment and the
element read without it: `judge_expression` had an arm for `ArrayIndex`, one
for `BufferIndex`, one for `SliceIndex` and none for `RunIndex`, so a run
subscript in read position fell to the walk-the-children default and submitted
nothing.

The hole is not narrow. `let run = fixed_vector::<u8, 4>(); let seen =
run[0_u64];` compiled, linked and ran, reading a slot outside the window of an
empty run — a raw slot no operation had written. Every source read of a run
element was admitted this way, whatever the run and whatever the offset.

The repair is the arm the other three already had, with the run's own measured
kind and the sentence [OP-4] and [BLK-1] state for its target twin: the offset
is a logical one, the window's length bounds it, and the written capacity is
not the bound. No rule is amended, because [OP-4] already said this.

**One program in the corpus was standing on the hole.**
`tests/programs/run_queue.wf` reads `grown[2_u64]` where `grown` comes back
from `append`, and `append` published nothing about its result's length; the
read had no proof and was accepted anyway. It now publishes
`ensures len_of(result) >= len_of(vector) + 1_u64` — the relation its own
`place_back` establishes [MSR-3] — and the call site derives `2 < len_of(grown)`
from that and `pair`'s own published length. No verdict of either corpus moved:
the adapter goes from Pass=620 over 622 cases to Pass=622 over 624 with the two
cases this adds, and the snapshot corpus stays at Pass=491, Flip=0.

## cc1fc49d 2026-09-05 evidence: what binary arithmetic in the proof surface actually costs

Four independent sweeps against the v0.44 compiler: three constructed
programs in their own domain (loop-carried bounds, multi-dimensional and
strided access, codecs and capacity arithmetic), one counted the 1229 .wf
files already in the tree. Every verdict recorded here was compiled.

All four converged on one sentence rather than on prover strength. ENT-6
computes the four endpoint products of a non-constant multiplication,
proves all four are in range, and discards them, so the multiply is
admitted and its result carries no bound. E1 accepts the product, E5
rejects the add that follows it, and supplying exactly the discarded
bound as a written guard turns E5 into an accept.

The same measurement found a second gap that is not about nonlinearity:
a contract clause admits no binary arithmetic at all. `count * 2_u64` and
`count + 2_u64` are the same FN-8 rejection, so a size precondition is
unwritable and a widened multiplication would not fix it.

The corpus count (1.7% of files) and the constructed count (9 of 11
natural forms rejected) disagree because the corpus cannot measure this:
it is written in the language that has the gap, and one of its own files
records picking a power-of-two grid width to dodge the family.

This is selection ground only. No spec byte, compiler code, or
conformance content changes here.

## af7164f6 2026-09-05 evidence: correct the contract-clause reading, and add its probes

The first reading of the contract surface was wrong in a way that changes
what the fix is. A clause does admit binary arithmetic, nonlinear included:
`define needed = count *sat count;` forms, and so does `count +wrap 2_u64`.
Both fail later, at the caller, Unproved. What a clause refuses is the
exact rows — requires.rs:813-816 rejects any operation whose is_exact()
holds — so the divide is exact against total, not addition against
multiplication. A second and independent wall is arity: clause_expr admits
one operator, so `requires a >= b + 1_u64;` is a GRAM-5 parse rejection
whatever the row.

The consequence is unchanged: `requires len(out) >= 2 * len(src)` is
unwritable. The cause is a formation-time policy over one operator set,
grounded in a clause being runtime-typed where an affine expression is
mathematical, so the repair is an allow-list plus a spec amendment rather
than a second relation model.

That also reorders the work. Widening a written surface before the fact
base can hold what it states turns a clean rejection into a silent
non-fact: checked_affine_relation_l0 publishes only unit-coefficient
relations, and a measure has no affine image at all. The fact base is fed
first.

## effe2e20 2026-09-05 One lowering for every I/O operation; the direct family leaves

Design §8. Every ordinary I/O wrapper in the system emitter reserves
the record in its own alwaysinline frame, submits, joins and maps the
completion, and derived release closes through one shared helper that
does the same. The four text builders the handed-out path and the
wrappers share are the one spelling of submit, transfer target and
retirement. The direct family (pread, write, open_at, status, close,
directory_next), the qualification rows that named it and every
declaration of a _direct symbol are gone from the compiler, the bridge,
the Windows runtime and the harness. The open_file and open_directory
kind check and its close on mismatch are the runtime's, decided from
expected_kind, so no emitted code holds a struct stat. The
deterministic test target takes the same shape with submit and join
stubs. A thread joining its own queued submission runs that record
itself, so an ordinary write no longer waits behind an unrelated
blocked one when helpers are pinned.

## f14a70f4 2026-09-05 Order the ring's reaper after the submitter with one release-acquire pair

The record carries an `issued` word: the ring's submit stores it with
release after every other word of the record is written, and the CQE
reaper loads it with acquire before reading any of them. The kernel
carries the record's address from the SQE to the CQE, but a mapped
ring is not a C11 synchronization, and the entry pool's state word that
used to give this ordering went with the pool. The thread sanitizer on
the real Linux host reported exactly that gap in the default-route
probe; it is quiet on the core/read, default-route and bridge-and-ring
stages now. A CQE naming a record that was never issued is a protocol
failure.

## 69cec6cc 2026-09-05 Publish the interval an admitted product already proved: v0.45

[ENT-6]'s fixed interval-product rule proves an inclusive interval for
each operand of a non-constant multiplication, forms the four products of
their endpoint pairs, and admits the multiplication exactly when all four
lie in the result type. It then discarded them. So the multiply was
admitted and the value it bound carried no bound at all, and the `+` that
followed was refused [OP-2] for want of a premise the checker had just
computed.

[ENT-3] gains source S14, which establishes the least and greatest of
those four products on the value the multiplication binds. Nothing about
the derivation widens: both published relations are constant bounds
against the distinguished zero term, so they are ordinary L0 facts whose
[ENT-5] support is the bound value alone. That is what they mean — they
describe the value already produced, so a later write to an operand
leaves them true while a write to the bound place kills them under the
ordinary rule. No relation over the operands, no new term, and no
automatic route by which a product enters a premise family is added; a
written `use` remains the only way a product participates in a
certificate.

The measurement moves into affine_integer_product_interval, which the
domain decision and S14 both read, so the admitted range and the
published bound cannot disagree. The interval travels out of the
judgment on ProofResult and waits keyed by the operation's own carrier
node, because the domain is judged while the initializer is walked and
S14 establishes at the binding that walk then reaches; a domain
discharged by the finite L0 or affine-clause route carries nothing and
publishes nothing.

Evidence: E1_bounded_product.wf is accepted because the interval rule
discharges `r * w`; E5_product_then_add.wf is the same program plus
`base + c` and was refused. Both now accept, as does an invariant stated
over the product's result. Over the 55 constructed multi-dimensional and
strided programs exactly two verdicts move, both from refusal to
acceptance, and the guarded flattened-index programs relocate from [OP-2]
to the [OP-4] subscript bound they were always about. The snapshot corpus
holds at 491 pass, 0 flips, and conformance covers 136/136 rules.

The backend qualification tripwire is reviewed and carried forward: the
amendment is front-end fact publication over erased proof state, admits
only programs previously refused, and introduces no operation kind, entry
form, result shape, or ABI mapping.

## 18955162 2026-09-05 Record what L1 costs: the clause surface needs a measure atom first

Built the smaller half of L1 and ran it rather than reasoning about it.
Admitting the exact affine rows in clause position is 22 lines, and with
them an expansion codec's precondition forms where v0.45 refuses it at
formation. It then fails at every caller:

  [FN-8] UndischargedCallRequirement
    instantiated_goal: "len(out) >= len(src) * 2_u64"
    disposition: Unproved

The call site is len(out)=8 and len(src)=4, so the goal is true. Neither
fact domain can hold it: L0 is a two-term difference bound and carries no
coefficient, and the affine layer has no measure atom — affine_term_value
images Zero, Constant, and unprojected binding places, and every length
term falls to the None arm, which is what spec:1429 means by "not yet an
affine atom".

So the smaller half alone would ship a precondition a writer can state
and no caller can meet. That is the failure the contract scoping
predicted for widening a surface ahead of the fact base, so the patch is
recorded here and not merged. L1 is both halves in one amendment: the
exact rows read mathematically, and len(P) admitted as an affine atom.

## 5fd98b4e 2026-09-05 B8b: the subscripted place, from the measure term to the slot address

B7a6 and B8a both established that [MSR-1]'s `len_of(table[i])`, [MSR-2]'s
element-position kill at that granularity and [LIV-2] condition 2's `grid[k]`
against `grid[i][j]` are one change and not three: a measured or targeted place
was a `BindingId` plus a `Vec<u32>` of field selections, and every consumer of
that vector was keyed on its shape. This is that one change.

**The place gains a step, and the step gains an offset.** A tracked place's
path is now field selections and subscripts in written order, and a subscript
carries the offset the place relations read: a written literal, a live `own`
fragment-integer binding, or an in-scope const generic [MSR-6]. That is not a
convenience — the identity of the place is decided over it. [OWN-7] decides two
subscripted places by their offsets, and [ENT-5] takes each offset's own support
into every measure term the offset occurs in, so an offset neither relation can
name would make two measures of two elements one term. An offset of any other
form in a measure place is the explicit compiler capability it is, reported as
one rather than as a source rejection. The same domain reaches
`ProjectedPlaceTerm`, `GoalProjection`, `CallDatumProjection`, the checked
container root and the publication table's operand key; the compact `PlaceTerm`
keeps its field-only shape and a subscripted place is a projected one.

**[OWN-7] is stated over the complete path.** Two places fail to overlap
exactly when some step of their common prefix provably selects two different
storages — two fields, or two subscripts whose offsets are both literals with
unequal values — so `grid[k]` and `grid[i][j]` are decided at `k` against `i`
and never at their last offsets. [LIV-2]'s second condition reads that relation
at a commit and its element read-out reads the same path, which is what makes
`set (grid[0][1], grid[1][1]) = 9_u8, 8_u8;` two targets and
`set (grid[0][1], grid[0][1]) = ...` one. B8a's `CommitOffset` is superseded in
place by the offset the places carry.

**[MSR-2]'s granularity is now the relation and not a flag.** Every element
write carries the element's own place — `P[i]`, with the offset a run target
wrote and the opaque offset a callee's projected write names — so the kill is
the sentence the rule states: a write at an element position of P overlaps the
descriptor storage of `P[i]` and none of P's own. A measure of `P[i]` dies at
that write; a measure of `P` does not; a whole-value write of `P` kills both.
The old "an element write kills no measure at all" clause is gone, because it
was only ever true of a table with no measured element type.

**[OP-4] is submitted where the place is formed.** A subscript inside a
measured place owes `i < len_of(base)` against the prefix that reaches its base,
judged at the measure former exactly as a written subscript's is judged at the
read [MSR-4]; a measure over a place whose subscripts are not all discharged is
no term.

**The lowering reads the descriptor through the slot address.** A measured
place's value is projected step by step — a field selection is the ordinary
struct projection, a subscript is [BLK-1]'s element read — and an element store
is written back the same way, so `grid[i][j]` reads the inner run's descriptor
out of slot `i` and stores the modified run back into it.

An [INV-1] affine factor is checked without the enclosing concrete instance in
hand, so a subscript inside a measure place there keeps its own explicit
unsupported report rather than being formed from a different premise set; that
is the one position this change does not reach.

Five conformance cases: the measure over a subscripted place running end to
end, the subscript inside it owing its own obligation, the element store killing
the element's length and keeping the run's, and condition 2 over two nested
targets both ways. The adapter moves from Pass=622 over 624 cases to Pass=627
over 629, the one xfail and the one skip unchanged, and the snapshot corpus
stays at Pass=491, Flip=0.

moved, no DEFERRED clause landed or added — a CONSEQUENCE entry for the two

the adapter at Pass=627 over 629 cases, coverage complete at 148/148 and the
snapshot corpus at Pass=491, Flip=0. `run_queue.wf`'s added `ensures` is named
there as what it is: a program of the executable corpus, outside the boundary,
that was standing on the read obligation and now pays it.

The design gains 6.0n and one dated correction under [MSR-1]. The correction is
the thing the design itself did not say: which offsets a subscripted measure
place admits. [OWN-7] decides two such places by their offsets and [ENT-5] takes
each offset's own support into every measure it occurs in, so an offset neither
relation can name would intern two measures of two elements as **one term** —
which is why a written literal, a live `own` fragment-integer place and an
in-scope const generic are the admitted forms and everything else is a place
this version does not represent. 6.0n records the two repairs, the one position
the change does not reach — an [INV-1] affine factor is read without the
enclosing concrete instance, so a subscript in a measure place there keeps its
unsupported report — and, separately, a **third soundness hole older than this
batch and left where it lies**: a function that calls `arena_vector_proved`
discharges every [OP-4] obligation it contains, so a nine-slot read of a
four-slot array compiles, links and runs at the batch's own base commit. That
row's published relations are making the fact state universally discharging,
which [MSR-4] says is a contradiction to be stated first and once, and the
repair belongs with that row.

`compiler/README.md` restates the container section: the place is a root plus
